topic.intro: Program ka kaam sirf calculate karna nahi — input lena aur output saaf dikhana bhi utna hi important hai. Yahan print ke sep/end, f-string ke format specs, input() ka 'hamesha string' behaviour aur stdout vs stderr ka fark cover hota hai. Ye section wo habit banata hai jisse aapka output readable aur aapka input crash-proof ho.
theory: print() har argument ko str() se convert karta hai, sep (default space) ke saath jodta hai, end (default newline) lagata hai, aur None return karta hai — isliye 'x = print(...)' se x None hi milega.
input() hamesha str return karta hai, chahe user number daale. Isliye conversion alag step hai aur usme ValueError aa sakta hai; input khatam ho jaye to EOFError aata hai.

f-string ka format spec chhota language hai: [[fill]align][sign][width][,][.precision][type] — jaise f'{x:>10,.2f}' (right align, comma grouping, 2 decimal). Type code value ke type ke saath match karna zaroori hai, warna ValueError.
stdout data ke liye hai, stderr errors/logs ke liye. Ye Unix convention script ko pipe-able banata hai: 'prog > out.csv' se sirf data file me jata hai aur logs screen par dikhte hain.
repr() debug ke liye hai (quotes aur escapes dikhata hai), str() dikhane ke liye. '"7"' aur '7' ka fark output me dikhana ho to !r use karo — warna debugging guesswork ban jati hai.
syntax:
print('a', 'b', sep=' | ')          # a | b
print('loading', end='...')          # newline nahi
print('done', end='')                # ek hi line me aage likhna
print(f'{name!r} -> {score:>6.2f}')  # repr + formatted

raw = input('Enter port: ')     # hamesha str
value = int(raw)                 # ValueError possible
print('got', value)              # None return nahi karta

import sys
print('debug line', file=sys.stderr)   # logs stderr par
sys.stdout.write('no auto newline')
args = sys.argv[1:]
lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()

end='' se newline rukta hai, isliye agla print usi line par chalta hai: 'Loading... done'.
Width/alignment ka combo (< aur >) se columns align hote hain; repr (!r) string ke quotes bhi dikhata hai, jo debugging me farak rakhta hai.

print('bytes :', f'{1536:,.0f}', '->', f'{1536 / 1024:.1f} KB')
print('pad   :', f'{7:04d}', '|', f'{"skewed":*^12}', '|', f'{-12:+d}')
explain: Header aur data rows same width specs use karte hain, isliye columns perfectly align hote hain (monospace font me table jaisa).
:,.2f me comma grouping + 2 decimals hai — finance output ka standard format.
:>8.1% percent type hai: value ko 100 se multiply karke percent sign lagata hai, isliye 0.05 -> 5.0%.
Fill+align (*^12) string ko stars se center me pad karta hai; +d sign force karta hai (-12 -> -12, 12 -> +12).

explain: redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr se do streams ko alag buffer me capture kiya — yahi test karne ka tarika hai ki data aur logs mix nahi hue.
stdout me sirf machine-readable rows gaye aur stderr me human logs — isi wajah se 'python x.py > data.csv' clean data deta hai.

!r se string ka quotes aur escape (
) dikhta hai; plain str me '7' aur 7 dono same dikhte hain aur debugging me confusion hoti hai.

realWorld: Logging discipline: logs stderr par jaate hain aur data stdout par, isliye CLI tools ko shell pipeline me use kiya ja sakta hai (prog | grep, prog > report.csv) bina logs file kharaab kiye.
Billing aur invoices me format specs legal requirement ban jate hain — currency grouping, 2 decimal aur percent display galat hone par customer complaint aati hai (aur audit me mismatch nikalta hai).

ETL me 'input hamesha string' rule sabse zyada bug deta hai: CSV/JSON/env se aaya '007' int ban gaya to leading zero gaya, ya '3.10' ko float banaya to version number 3.1 ho gaya (aur comparison galat).

interview.q: stdout aur stderr alag rakhna kyun zaroori hai?
interview.a: Unix philosophy: stdout machine-readable output ke liye, stderr diagnostics ke liye. Isse 'prog > file' par sirf data jata hai aur errors screen par dikhte hain; 'prog 2>/dev/null' se logs silence kiye ja sakte hain bina data khoye. Interactive tools (progress bar) bhi stderr par likhte hain taaki pipe na toote.
interview.tip: Ek concrete pipeline example do (prog > data.csv, 2> app.log) — isse pata chalta hai aapne real CLI banayi hai.

interview.q: input() se number lene me kya kya edge cases hain?
interview.a:
Ek: input() hamesha str deta hai, isliye conversion explicit hai aur ValueError possible hai. Do: EOFError jab input stream khatam ho (Ctrl+D ya piped file) — library code me ye crash banata hai. Teen: whitespace ('42
' vs ' 42 '), locale decimal comma ('1,5'), aur huge input par block waiting. Isliye library me input() na rakho — parameter lo, aur CLI layer par validation karo.
interview.tip: Ye question 'testability' ko touch karta hai — input() ko function boundary se bahar rakhne ka reason batao.

interview.q: f-string ke format specs ke common pitfalls kya hain?
interview.a: Type mismatch (str par :f, float par :d) ValueError deta hai; precision money me silently rounding hai (:.0f se paise gayab); width se truncate nahi hota (string bada ho to column toot jayega); aur locale-aware grouping (!, aur locale module) ka farak. Plus f-string '=' spec (f'{x=}') debugging me useful hai.
interview.tip: Truncation ke liye ':.3' (precision on str) bhi batao — log messages me kaam aata hai.

interview.q: Ek function likhna ho jo output ko testable banae — architecture kya hogi?
interview.a: Business logic ko pure function rakho jo data return kare, aur printing ko thin layer me. Tests phir return value par assertions karenge; output format ke liye contextlib.redirect_stdout se capture karke compare karo (ya snapshot test). Isse output badalna test todta nahi, sirf ek format test todta hai.
interview.tip: redirect_stdout ka mention karna practical signal hai — isse pata chalta hai aapne output ko actually test kiya hai.

beginner.q: Aur bina newline ke 'Loading...' aur uske baad 'done' ek hi line me print karo.
beginner.a: print('Loading', end='') phir print('... done') — pehle print newline nahi deta, dusra apna newline de deta hai.
beginner.explain: end ka default '\n' hai; end='' karne se cursor usi line par rehta hai (progress output ka basic tarika).

print('... done')

print('row 2')
beginner.tip: Progress bar me end='\r' bhi use hota hai — same line overwrite karne ke liye.

beginner.q: Teen words ko 'a - b - c' format me print karo bina manual join ke.
beginner.a: print('a', 'b', 'c', sep=' - ') — sep sirf beech me lagta hai.
beginner.explain: sep arguments ke beech apply hota hai, isliye shuru/ant me separator nahi aata (manual join me ye galti hoti hai).

print('a', 'b', 'c', sep=' - ')
print('a', 'b', 'c', sep='')
print(1, 2, 3, sep=', ', end=';\n')
beginner.tip: CSV banate waqt sep=',' kaafi nahi — quoting chahiye (advanced coding task me hai).

beginner.q: Score 7 ko '0007' aur 3.14159 ko '3.14' print karo.

beginner.tip: Banker's rounding: 2.5 -> 2 par round() aur format dono same rule follow karte hain — money me Decimal use karo.

intermediate.q: Bytes ko human-readable banao: 1536 -> '1.5 KB', 1048576 -> '1.0 MB'.

intermediate.explain: Assertions ke saath ye pattern CI me 'logs kabhi data me leak na hon' test ban jata hai.

advanced.q: Ek 'output contract' test likho: function ka stdout exactly kya hona chahiye, assertion ke saath verify karo.
advanced.a: io.StringIO + redirect_stdout se output capture karo, phir expected string ya lines list se compare karo.

advanced.q: CSV line ko safely quote karo: comma, double quote aur newline wale fields handle karo.
advanced.a: Field ko double quotes me wrap karo aur andar ke " ko "" karo (RFC 4180 style).
advanced.explain: Quoting sirf zaroorat par hoti hai (comma, quote, newline) — yahi conditional rule RFC 4180 ka core hai. Andar ke quotes double karne se parser unhe correctly unescape kar pata hai.
advanced.tip: Hand-rolled CSV se aage badhkar csv module use karo (dialect, quoting options) — interview me ye mention karo.

interview.q: Ek CLI tool ke output ko testable banane ke liye kya karoge?
interview.a: Logic ko pure functions me rakho jo data return karein, aur print sirf thin layer me karo. Format tests ke liye redirect_stdout/stderr se capture karke compare karo; colours/progress ko TTY check par conditional rakho (sys.stdout.isatty()) taaki piped output me escape codes na jayein.
interview.explain: isatty() ka zikr production CLI experience dikhata hai.

interview.q: Bade output (lakhs of lines) ko efficiently kaise likhoge?
interview.a: str join karke ek write karo (ya generator + writelines), per-line print se bacho; '".join(lines)' memory leta hai to chunking karo (10k lines per flush). sys.stdout.write buffering, aur flush sirf zaroorat par (interactive/progress) karo — warna syscall overhead performance kha jata hai.
interview.explain: Print per line I/O bound hota hai; buffered writes ka farak measurable hota hai.

interview.tip: Ye answer 'benchmark karke dekha hai' confidence deta hai — print loop vs join ka farak mention karo.

interview.q: CSV vs TSV vs JSON output — kab kaunsa choose karoge?
interview.a: CSV: flat tabular data, spreadsheet-friendly, human-readable; nested data nahi rakhta aur escaping ka dhyan rakhna padta hai. TSV: tabs na aayein to escaping sasti hai, par tab wale text par toot jata hai. JSON: nested/typed data ke liye best, streaming ke liye JSON Lines (ek object per line) use karo. Decision input consumers par depend karta hai, 'kaun padhega' se.
interview.explain: JSON Lines ka mention streaming/ETL context dikhata hai.

realworld.q: Invoice output banao jisme currency grouping, 2 decimal, aur percent rate sab legal format me ho.
realworld.a: Format specs: ':,.2f' for money aur ':.1%' for percent; header ke saath widths align karo.
realworld.explain: Amount column me raw calculation se pehle format lagana zaroori hai (rounding display-only hai). Total ko subtotal + tax se dobara compute karo taaki formatted rows se drift na ho.
realworld.code:
items = [('Consulting hours', 42, 1500.0), ('Report design', 1, 7500.0)]
TAX = 0.18

print(f'{"Item":<20}{"Qty":>5}{"Rate":>12}{"Amount":>14}')
print('-' * 51)
subtotal = 0.0
for name, qty, rate in items:
    amount = qty * rate
    subtotal += amount
    print(f'{name:<20}{qty:>5}{rate:>12,.2f}{amount:>14,.2f}')

tax = subtotal * TAX
print('-' * 51)
print(f'{"Subtotal":<37}{subtotal:>14,.2f}')
print(f'{"GST (18%)":<37}{tax:>14,.2f}')
print(f'{"Total payable":<37}{subtotal + tax:>14,.2f}')
print(f'tax rate shown as percent: {TAX:.1%}')
realworld.tip: Real invoices me line totals round karke sum karte hain (sum of rounded == rounded sum guarantee) — ye business rule clarify karo.

realworld.q: CLI tool ka usage/help output likho jo argv ke saath validations kare aur exit code de.
realworld.a: argv parse karo, missing/invalid par stderr par usage print karo aur non-zero exit code do (usage error ke liye 2, business error ke liye 1).
realworld.explain: SystemExit with a message stderr par likhta hai aur non-zero status deta hai — ye argparse ke bina bhi standard behaviour hai. main() int return karta hai isliye tests exit code assert kar sakte hain.

row   1 | value      1
row   2 | value      4
row   3 | value      9
exit code: 0
json mode : [{"row": 1}, {"row": 2}]
exit code: 0
usage error: rows must be positive, got 0
realworld.tip: Interview me sys.exit(main(argv)) ka pattern batao — isse exit codes testable rehte hain.

realworld.q: Ek progress/status line banao jo pipe hone par (non-TTY) saaf ho jaye aur file me garbage na likhe.
realworld.a: isatty() check karo: TTY par '\r' wali dynamic line, warna sirf final summary print karo.
realworld.explain: Non-TTY me intermediate lines skip kar di jati hain aur sirf final line aati hai — isse logs/CI me clean output rehta hai. TTY mode me '\r' prefix hota hai jo same line overwrite karta hai.
realworld.code:
import sys

def progress_line(done, total, tty=False):
    percent = done / total
    bar = '#' * int(percent * 20)
    line = f'[{bar:<20}] {done}/{total} ({percent:.0%})'
    if tty:
        return '\r' + line
    return line if done == total else None

for done in (1, 2, 3):
    line = progress_line(done, 3, tty=False)
    if line:
        print(line)

preview = progress_line(2, 3, tty=True)
print('tty mode repr:', repr(preview))
realworld.tip: sys.stdout.isatty() real detection hai; tests me flag pass karna better hai (dependency injection).

coding.question: Receipt printer likho: items ki list se aligned receipt banao (item, qty, rate, amount) aur total print karo.
coding.build: print_receipt(items) — column widths compute ho, currency 2 decimal me ho, aur total last line par.
coding.hint: Widths ke liye max(len(...)) use karo; amount ko :>10,.2f se format karo.
coding.solution:
def print_receipt(items):
    header = ('Item', 'Qty', 'Rate', 'Amount')
    rows = [(name, str(qty), f'{rate:,.2f}', f'{qty * rate:,.2f}') for name, qty, rate in items]
    widths = [max(len(header[i]), *(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) for i in range(4)]

    def line(cells):
        return '  '.join(f'{cell:<{widths[i]}}' if i == 0 else f'{cell:>{widths[i]}}'
                         for i, cell in enumerate(cells))

    print(line(header))
    print('-' * (sum(widths) + 6))
    for row in rows:
        print(line(row))
    total = sum(qty * rate for _, qty, rate in items)
    print('-' * (sum(widths) + 6))
    print(line(('Total', '', '', f'{total:,.2f}')))

print_receipt([('Idli', 2, 60.0), ('Filter coffee', 3, 45.5), ('Masala dosa', 1, 120.0)])
coding.explanation: Widths pehle compute hoti hain (header + saare rows ka max), phir ek hi line() helper left-align/right-align apply karta hai — isse alignment code duplicate nahi hota. Total raw floats se nikaalta hai, formatted strings se nahi (warna rounding drift aata).
coding.time: O(rows × cols) — width calculation aur printing
coding.space: O(rows × cols) formatted cells ke liye
coding.better: Bahut bade reports ke liye streaming: widths ke liye ek pass, printing ke liye dusra pass (ya file me do baar padho) — memory bachti hai.

coding.question: Debug dumper likho jo kisi bhi value ka type, len, str aur repr dikhae — aur '7' vs 7 jaise traps expose kare.
coding.build: dump(value) -> single line; multiple values ke liye aligned output.
coding.expected: Aligned rows jisme str aur repr alag columns me hon.
coding.hint: len ke liye hasattr check, aur repr me newline ko visible banao (replace '\n' with '\\n').
coding.concept: repr vs str, type introspection, defensive attribute access
coding.solution:
def dump(value):
    kind = type(value).__name__
    size = len(value) if hasattr(value, '__len__') else '-'
    shown = str(value).replace(chr(10), '\\n')
    return kind, str(size), shown, repr(value).replace(chr(10), '\\n')

values = ['7', 7, 7.0, True, None, [1, 2], {'a': 1}, 'a' + chr(10) + 'b']
rows = [dump(v) for v in values]
widths = [max(len(h), *(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) for i, h in enumerate(('type', 'len', 'str', 'repr'))]

print(f'{"type":<{widths[0]}} {"len":<{widths[1]}} {"str":<{widths[2]}} {"repr":<{widths[3]}}')
for row in rows:
    print(f'{row[0]:<{widths[0]}} {row[1]:<{widths[1]}} {row[2]:<{widths[2]}} {row[3]:<{widths[3]}}')
coding.output:
type     len str      repr
str      1   7        '7'
int      -   7        7
float    -   7.0      7.0
bool     -   True     True
NoneType -   None     None
list     2   [1, 2]   [1, 2]
dict     1   {'a': 1} {'a': 1}
str      3   a\nb     'a\nb'
coding.explanation: repr aur str dono columns me rakhna isliye zaroori hai kyunki trap wahi hai: '7' aur 7 str me same dikhte hain par repr me quotes ka fark nazar aata hai. Newline ko visible escape me badalna table ko tootne se bachata hai.
coding.better: Production me pprint/rich.pretty ya logging with repr formatting use karo; custom dumpers ko nested structures ke liye depth limit do.

coding.explanation: Har format ka apna pure renderer hai (string return karta hai), aur emit() sirf stream + summary handle karta hai — isliye renderers ko bina I/O test kiya ja sakta hai. Validation ek hi jagah hai, isliye saare formats me same rows filter hote hain (consistency). Summary stderr par jata hai taaki piped output me sirf data rahe.

coding.question: Ek 'explainable diff' printer likho: do dicts ke fark ko aligned, human-readable output me dikhao (added, removed, changed).

coding.input: old = {'host': 'localhost', 'port': 5432, 'debug': False} vs new with port change + new key
coding.expected: Readable sections with aligned keys aur old -> new arrows.
coding.hint: Keys ka union lo, phir teen buckets me classify karo; har bucket ki width alag compute karo.

ADDED (1)
  retries  3
REMOVED (1)

UNCHANGED (2): host, workers
coding.explanation: Set operations (union/difference/intersection) fark ko teen saaf buckets me todti hain, aur per-bucket width se keys align hoti hain. Lambdas se render logic section ke andar hi rehta hai, isliye teen sections same loop se print hote hain.
coding.better: Nested dicts ke liye recursive diff (dotted paths) likho, aur values ko unified-diff style line format me do taaki tooling parse kar sake; colour output optional rakho (TTY check).
coding.followUp: Nested structures aur lists ka diff kaise represent karoge (index-based vs key-based) — aur kaunsa format tooling ke liye best hai?

debugging.broken:
print('saving report', file='report.log')
print('done')
debugging.error: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'write'
debugging.why: file parameter file-like object maangta hai (jiske paas write method ho), file ka naam nahi. String dene par print usko write karne ki koshish karta hai aur AttributeError aata hai.
debugging.fix: open() se file object banao (with block me), ya logging module use karo. Path dena ho to context manager ke saath kholo.
debugging.correct:
import io, sys

buffer = io.StringIO()
print('saving report', file=buffer)
print('done')
print('captured:', repr(buffer.getvalue()))
print('stderr is a file object:', hasattr(sys.stderr, 'write'))
debugging.output:
done
captured: 'saving report\n'
stderr is a file object: True
debugging.lesson: print() ka file ek stream hai, path nahi. Ye bug beginners ka classic hai, aur isi wajah se logging module ('file path do') aur print ('stream do') me confusion banti hai.

debugging.broken:
price = '249.99'
print(f'{price:>10.2f}')
debugging.error: ValueError: Unknown format code 'f' for object of type 'str'
debugging.why: Format code 'f' sirf numeric types ke liye valid hai. Yahan price string hai (raw input/CSV se aaya), isliye f-string numeric formatting refuse kar deta hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle type convert karo (float/Decimal), phir format lagao — ya '.2' (precision on string) use karo agar display-only truncation chahiye.
debugging.correct:
raw = '249.99'
price = float(raw)
print(f'{price:>10.2f}')
print(f'{raw:>10.2}')

from decimal import Decimal
print(f'{Decimal(raw):>10.2f}')
debugging.lesson: Format code type par depend karta hai — CSV/JSON se aaya har number string hota hai, isliye conversion step kabhi skip mat karo.

debugging.broken:
total = 250
print('Total:', total, sep='=')
debugging.error: Logic error — output 'Total:=250' aata hai, jabki intent 'Total: 250' tha
debugging.why: sep sirf arguments ke beech lagta hai. Yahan do arguments hain ('Total:' aur 250) isliye sep '=' unke beech aata hai; colon pehle argument ke andar hai isliye double separator dikhta hai.
debugging.fix: Do options: sep=',' ke bajaye f-string use karo (print(f'Total: {total}')) ya argument me colon na rakho (print('Total', total, sep=': ')).
debugging.correct:
total = 250
print(f'Total: {total}')
print('Total', total, sep=': ')
print('Total:', total)
debugging.lesson: sep ke saath punctuation pehle se argument me likhna confusing output deta hai. Formatting ke liye f-string saaf aur predictable hai.

debugging.broken:
amount = 1234.56
print(f'Amount: {amount:>10.0f}')
print(f'Rate  : {0.185:>8.0%}')
debugging.error: Logic error — output 'Amount:       1235' aur 'Rate  :      19%' aata hai; cents aur precision gayab
debugging.why: Precision 0 ne decimals truncate kar diye: money ka 0.56 round hokar 1235 ban gaya aur percent 18.5% se 19% ho gaya. Display ne data kho diya.
debugging.fix: Money ke liye ':,.2f' aur percent ke liye ':.1%' use karo — precision ko business requirement ke hisaab se set karo, 0 par default mat chhodo.
debugging.correct:
amount = 1234.56
print(f'Amount: {amount:>10,.2f}')
print(f'Rate  : {0.185:>8.1%}')
print(f'Exact in words: {amount} rupees, rate {0.185}')
debugging.output:
Amount:   1,234.56
Rate  :    18.5%
Exact in words: 1234.56 rupees, rate 0.185
debugging.lesson: Precision ek business decision hai, formatting detail nahi. Money display me 2 decimals aur rates me kam se kam 1 decimal rakho — warna customer dispute aata hai.

debugging.broken:
rows = [('idli', 60), ('dosa', 80)]
out = ''
for name, price in rows:
    out += f'{name},{price}'
print(out)
print('lines written:', out.count(chr(10)))
debugging.error: Logic error — CSV do columns ek hi line me chipak jati hain; lines count 0 aata hai
debugging.why: Har row ke baad newline add nahi hui, aur row ke andar bhi ',' separator ke baad newline ka confusion hai. Result: ek single line 'idli,60dosa,80' jo CSV parser ke liye invalid hai.
debugging.fix: Har row ko newline ke saath join karo — list collect karke '\n'.join(lines) (ya har row par end='\n' wala print) use karo.
debugging.correct:
rows = [('idli', 60), ('dosa', 80)]
lines = ['name,price']
lines += [f'{name},{price}' for name, price in rows]
out = chr(10).join(lines) + chr(10)
print(out, end='')
print('lines written:', out.count(chr(10)))
debugging.lesson: Record boundaries (newline) data ka hissa hain, decoration nahi. CSV likhte waqt hamesha 'ek row ek line' contract rakho aur lines count se verify karo.

projects.name: Receipt Printer (Version 1)
projects.problem: Dukaan/restaurant ka bill haath se likhna ya spreadsheet me banana slow hai, aur columns align na hone se padhna mushkil hota hai.
projects.objective: Ek program jo items ki list se aligned receipt print kare — qty, rate, amount aur total ke saath.
features: Money 2 decimal aur comma grouping me
Header, separator lines aur total row
projects.structure:
receipt_printer/
└── receipt.py        # saara logic, ek file
steps: Items ki list define karo: (name, qty, rate).
Widths compute karo: header aur saare formatted rows ka max.
Rows print karo aur end par total line do.
Edge cases test karo: empty list, bahut lamba item name, 0 qty.
projects.code:
ITEMS = [
    ('Idli', 2, 60.0),
    ('Filter coffee', 3, 45.5),
    ('Masala dosa', 1, 120.0),
]

HEADERS = ('Item', 'Qty', 'Rate', 'Amount')

rows = [(name, str(qty), f'{rate:,.2f}', f'{qty * rate:,.2f}') for name, qty, rate in ITEMS]
widths = [max(len(HEADERS[i]), *(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) for i in range(4)]
rule = '-' * (sum(widths) + 6)

print('=' * (sum(widths) + 6))
print('RECEIPT'.center(sum(widths) + 6))
print('=' * (sum(widths) + 6))

print('  '.join(f'{h:<{widths[i]}}' if i == 0 else f'{h:>{widths[i]}}' for i, h in enumerate(HEADERS)))
print(rule)
for row in rows:
    print('  '.join(f'{cell:<{widths[i]}}' if i == 0 else f'{cell:>{widths[i]}}' for i, cell in enumerate(row)))
print(rule)

total = sum(qty * rate for _, qty, rate in ITEMS)
print('  '.join([f'{"Total":<{widths[0]}}', f'{"":>{widths[1]}}', f'{"":>{widths[2]}}', f'{total:>{widths[3]},.2f}']))
projects.explanation: Widths ek hi baar compute hoti hain aur phir wahi header aur rows par use hoti hain — isliye alignment consistent rehti hai. Total raw floats se nikalti hai, formatted strings se nahi.
projects.testing: Empty items list (max() par error aa sakta hai — guard add karo), 100-character item name, 0 qty wala item, aur 1000+ rate ke saath alignment check karo.
projects.errors: Empty list par widths computation ValueError dega kyunki max() khali sequence par fail hota hai — Version 2 me empty guard add hoti hai.
improvements: Items ko file se load karo (CSV/JSON) taaki har baar code na badalna pade
Empty list aur invalid rows ke liye validation + clear error messages
Items ke input mode add karo (library function se, stdin se nahi)
advanced: Multi-page receipt with page breaks aur repeated headers
Tax/discount lines with per-line rounding aur reconciliation
Output formats: text, 58mm thermal-style (narrow width), aur HTML
projects.realWorld: POS systems, invoice printers aur accounting exports sab isi column-alignment problem par kaam karte hain; galat receipt customer complaint aur audit issue banata hai.

interview.q: Widths compute karne ke liye do passes chahiye — memory bachane ke liye kya karoge?
interview.a: Pehla pass sirf max length record karega (O(cols) memory), dusra pass print karega. Streaming source (file/cursor) ho to dobara padhna padega ya intermediate spool file use karo.

interview.q: Item name bahut lamba ho to kya karna chahiye?
interview.a: Wrap ya truncate with ellipsis — truncation ka rule document karo aur chhoti width par readability badhane ke liye second line me poora naam do.

interview.q: Receipt ka format region-specific kaise handle karoge?
interview.a: Format spec ko config me rakho (currency symbol, decimal separator, date format) aur locale-aware formatting use karo — code me hardcode na karo.

interview.q: Rejected rows ko poori report fail karne ke bajaye skip kyun kiya?

projects.explanation: main() ne streams inject kiye (stdout/stderr params) aur exit code return kiya — isliye poori CLI bina subprocess ke test ho jati hai. Usage errors (exit 2) aur data errors (exit 1) alag rakhe gaye, aur child rows reject hone par bhi report milti hai (partial output + warnings).
projects.testing: argv ke cases: no args, valid format, invalid flag, invalid format — exit codes assert karo. Data cases: empty input, bad header, bad row. Aur verify karo ki stdout me sirf report hai (warnings nahi).

interview.q: Exit codes ka convention kya hai?
interview.a: 0 success, 1 general/runtime failure, 2 usage error (argparse bhi 2 use karta hai), aur 126/127 permission/not-found jaise shell codes. CI aur shell scripts isi par branch karte hain, isliye 'always 0 return karna' sabse mehnga bug hai.

interview.q: Partial failure par exit code kya hona chahiye?
interview.a: Policy decision: agar kuch rows reject hui par report bani, exit 0 + warnings (ya --strict flag ke saath 1). Isko document karo taaki CI strictness configurable ho. Silent partial success sabse khatarnak hai.

interview.q: CLI ko testable kaise banaya?
interview.a: main(argv, stdout, stderr) signature — streams inject karo aur exit code return karo (sys.exit sirf wrapper me). Isse tests StringIO ke saath chalti hain, subprocess nahi chahiye, aur failures ka output easily assert hota hai.

concepts.title: Section overview
concepts.body: Text har jagah hai: naam, message, password, file path. Strings me indexing aur slicing ek baar samajh gaye to lists aur tuples me bhi wahi kaam aayega. String moti ki mala hai: har moti (character) ki ek position (index) hoti hai, 0 se shuru. Mala ka ek hissa kaat sakte ho, par ek moti badal nahi sakte.

concepts.title: Creating Strings
concepts.body: String single ' ', double " " ya triple ''' ''' quotes me likhi ja sakti hai. Triple quotes multi-line ke liye.
concepts.code:
s1 = 'hello'
s2 = "world"
s3 = '''multi
line'''
print(s1, s2)
print(s3)
print("It's fine")     # andar apostrophe: double quotes use karo
concepts.output:
hello world
multi
line
It's fine

concepts.title: Concatenation
concepts.body: Do strings ko + operator se jodna.
concepts.code:
first = "Hello"
second = "World"
print(first + " " + second)

concepts.title: Repetition
concepts.body: String ko * se kai baar repeat karna.
concepts.code:
text = "ab"            # line banane ka mast tarika
print(text * 3)
print("-" * 20)

concepts.title: len()
concepts.body: String me total characters ginta hai (space bhi count hota hai).
concepts.code:
text = "Python"
print(len(text))
print(len("Hi there"))

concepts.title: Escape Characters
concepts.body: Special characters ke liye backslash: \n new line, \t tab, \\ backslash, \" quote.
concepts.code:
print("Line1\nLine2")
print("Name:\tAshu")

topic.intro: String Python me text ka data type hai — 'Ahetesham', 'select * from users', 'RAG pipeline' sab strings hain. Ye immutable sequence hai, yani ek baar bana to uske andar ka character badla nahi ja sakta; har method nayi string return karta hai. Aage ke poore course me jo bhi input aayega (file, CSV, API JSON, LLM prompt) wo pehle string hi hota hai, isliye string manipulation aana matlab data cleaning, validation aur parsing aana.
theory: String ek ordered, immutable sequence hai Unicode characters ki. Index 0 se shuru hota hai, negative index peeche se ginta hai (-1 last character), aur s[i:j:k] slicing se sub-string banta hai.
Kyunki string immutable hai, s[0] = 'x' TypeError deta hai. 'Modify' karne ka matlab hamesha nayi string banana hai — isliye methods ka result store karna padta hai.

Methods kaafi hain par kaam ke groups: case (lower, upper, title, casefold), trim/pad (strip, lstrip, ljust), search (find, index, startswith, count), replace (replace, translate), split/join (split, rsplit, splitlines, join).
f-string (f'{name}') modern formatting hai: expression andar chalta hai, spec se rounding/width milti hai (f'{x:.2f}'), aur repr ke liye !r. Purane % aur .format() ab sirf legacy code me milte hain.

Escape sequences (\n, \t, \\, \') aur raw string (r'C:\new') ka fark yaad rakho — regex aur Windows paths me raw string hi sahi hai. Encoding ka default UTF-8 hai; multi-line text ke liye triple quotes use karo.
syntax:
s = 'Python'        # single quotes
s2 = "Python"       # double quotes — same cheez
tri = '''multi
line'''
raw = r'C:\new\test'  # backslash literal rehta hai

s[0]      # 'P'  — first character
s[-1]     # 'n'  — last character
s[1:4]    # 'yth' — start se pehle end tak
s[::-1]   # 'nohtyP' — reverse
s[::2]    # 'Pto'  — every second character

s.upper(); s.lower(); s.strip(); s.split(','); ','.join(parts)
s.replace('old', 'new'); s.find('th'); s.startswith('Py'); s.count('t')
f'{name} scored {score:.1f}'   # formatted insert

examples.code:
name = 'Ahetesham'
print(name[0], name[-1])
print(name[0:4])
print(len(name))
print(name.upper())
explain: name[0] pehla character deta hai, name[-1] last — Python negative index ko length se jodta hai, isliye -1 ka matlab len(name) - 1.
name[0:4] me end index include nahi hota, isliye 4 characters aate hain: 'Ahet'.
len(name) characters ki ginti deta hai (bytes nahi) — 'Ahetesham' me 9.
upper() original ko nahi badalta, nayi uppercase string return karta hai; immutable hone ki wajah se ye hamesha naya object hai.

examples.code:
raw = '  Python, SQL ,  pandas  '
skills = [s.strip().lower() for s in raw.split(',')]
print(skills)
print('|'.join(skills))
print(f'{skills[0].title()} — {len(skills)} skills')
print(raw.strip().replace('  ', ' '))
examples.output:
['python', 'sql', 'pandas']
python|sql|pandas
Python � 3 skills
Python, SQL , pandas
explain: split(',') har comma par todta hai aur spaces bhi saath le aata hai — isliye har tukde par strip() lagana zaroori hai.
casefold/lower lagane se 'SQL' aur 'sql' ek jaise ho jate hain; comparison ke liye ye normalization basic step hai.
'|'.join(skills) list ko wapas string banata hai — separator wo string hai jispar join call hua, list nahi.
f-string ke andar expression aur method call dono chalte hain: {skills[0].title()} aur {len(skills)}.
Aakhir me strip() bahar ke spaces hatata hai aur replace('  ',' ') andar ke double spaces single karta hai — typical clean-up pipeline.
re.sub ke saath negated character class [^a-z0-9\s] har non-alphanumeric ko space se badal deta hai — punctuation hat jata hai.
text.split() bina argument diye whitespace par todta hai aur duplicate spaces ignore karta hai, phir ' '.join se single-space version milta hai.
compress() run-length encoding hai: jab tak same character repeat ho raha hai count badhta hai.
f'{text[i-1]}{count}' wahi character plus count deta hai, par count 1 hone par sirf character likha jata hai — isliye 'abc' waisa hi rehta hai.
Loop len(text)+1 tak chalta hai taaki last run bhi flush ho jaye — boundary par ek extra iteration classic technique hai.

realWorld: Data cleaning: CSV/Excel se aaya ' Pune ' aur 'pune' ek hi city hai — strip + casefold + replace ka combo har ETL job me pehla step hota hai.
Log parsing: production log line se timestamp, level aur message nikaalna split/rsplit aur startswith se hota hai; isi par alerting banti hai.
PII masking: 'Ashu Khan' ya '9876543210' ko report/LLM prompt me bhejne se pehle mask karna padta hai (s[:3] + '*'*n) — compliance requirement hai.
Prompt building: LLM ke liye system + context + user message ko f-string/template se jodna padta hai, aur token limit ke hisab se truncate karna padta hai.

interview.q: Strings immutable kyun hain aur iska practical asar kya hai?
interview.a: Immutable hone se string ko hash kiya ja sakta hai (dictionary key ban sakti hai), multiple threads bina lock share kar sakte hain, aur interned short strings memory bachate hain. Asar: har 'change' nayi string banata hai, isliye loop me s += x karne se O(n^2) ho jata hai — wahan list + join use karo.
interview.tip: Answer me hashability aur thread-safety dono mention karo, sirf 'change nahi kar sakte' mat kaho.

interview.q: == aur is me string comparison me kya fark hai?
interview.a: == value compare karta hai (character by character), is identity compare karta hai (same object). CPython chhoti literal strings ko intern karta hai, isliye 'ab' is 'ab' aksar True milega — par ye guarantee nahi hai. Kabhi bhi identity par bharosa karke string equality mat likho; sirf identity check ke liye is use karo.
interview.tip: Interviewer yahan interned behaviour ka edge case sunna chahta hai — 'aksar True, par guaranteed nahi' bolna strong answer hai.

interview.q: s[::-1] kaise reverse karta hai?
interview.a: Slice syntax start:stop:step hai. Jab start aur stop khaali ho aur step -1 ho, Python end se shuru karke 1-1 peeche chalta hai, isliye poora string reverse milta hai. Ye O(n) hai aur ek nayi string banati hai.
interview.tip: Slice ka default (start=0, stop=len, step=1) mention karo — interviewers basics ka clarity test karte hain.

interview.q: Loop me string concatenation slow kyun hai aur alternative kya hai?
interview.a: String immutable hai, isliye har += nayi string banata hai aur purana content copy hota hai — n iterations par O(n^2). Sahi tarika: parts ki list banao aur ' '.join(parts) se ek hi allocation me jodo, jo O(n) hai.
interview.tip: Real numbers do: 100k strings par += seconds leta hai jabki join milliseconds.

interview.q: split() aur split(' ') me kya fark hai?
interview.a: Bina argument split() whitespace ke har run par todta hai aur empty strings nikaal deta hai, isliye multiple spaces aur tabs ignore ho jate hain. split(' ') exactly ek space par todta hai, isliye consecutive spaces se khali strings aa jati hain — clean data ke liye pehla safer hai.
interview.tip: Isi logic se rsplit aur splitlines ke use case bhi bol dena.

interview.q: String formatting ke liye f-string vs .format() vs % — production me kya choose karoge?
interview.a: f-string: fast, readable, debug-friendly (f'{x=}'), par expression evaluate hote hain isliye user-controlled template ke saath injection ka dhyan rakhna padta hai. .format() tab jab template runtime par aaye (config/translation files). % sirf legacy logging code me; logging me actually lazy % style logger.info('%s', x) recommended hai taaki message format sirf zaroorat par ho.
interview.tip: Logging ka lazy-format point batao, ye practical depth dikhata hai.

beginner.q: String reverse karo.
beginner.a: s[::-1] ek step me reverse kar deta hai (O(n), nayi string).
beginner.explain: Negative step end se start ki taraf chalta hai, isliye start/stop khaali chhod do.
beginner.code:
s = 'Ahetesham'
print(s[::-1])
print(''.join(reversed(s)))
beginner.tip: Donon tarike batao — slice idiomatic hai, reversed() iterator deta hai.

beginner.q: String ki length find karo (spaces ke saath aur bina).
beginner.a: len(s) total characters deta hai; spaces hata kar ginti ke liye len(s.replace(' ', '')) ya sum(not c.isspace() for c in s) use karo.
beginner.code:
s = 'RAG pipeline works'
print(len(s))
print(len(s.replace(' ', '')))
beginner.commonMistake: len(s.strip()) se lagta hai spaces hat gaye, par strip sirf kinaron ke spaces hatata hai.

beginner.q: String me vowels count karo.
beginner.a: Ek set me vowels rakho aur character-wise check karo — set lookup O(1) hai, isliye overall O(n).
beginner.code:
s = 'Machine Learning'
vowels = set('aeiou')
print(sum(1 for c in s.lower() if c in vowels))

beginner.q: String me uppercase aur lowercase characters count karo.
beginner.a: c.isupper() aur c.islower() per-character check dete hai; ginti ke liye sum() ya loop use karo.
beginner.code:
s = 'PyThOn 3.14'
print(sum(c.isupper() for c in s), sum(c.islower() for c in s))
print(sum(c.isdigit() for c in s))
beginner.explain: bool int ki tarah sum ho jata hai: True = 1, False = 0 — ye idiom Python me common hai.

beginner.q: First aur last character find karo.
beginner.a: s[0] aur s[-1]. Empty string par IndexError aata hai, isliye pehle `if s:` check karo.
beginner.commonMistake: Bina guard s[0] likhna — empty input par crash.

beginner.q: Palindrome hai ya nahi check karo.
beginner.a: Normalize (lower + alphanumeric only) karke s == s[::-1] compare karo.
beginner.code:
def is_palindrome(s):
    clean = ''.join(c.lower() for c in s if c.isalnum())
    return clean == clean[::-1]

print(is_palindrome('Madam'))
print(is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'))
beginner.tip: Interview me yahi question 'ignore punctuation and case' ke saath aata hai — pehle normalization likho.

intermediate.q: String me duplicate characters find karo.
intermediate.a: collections.Counter se frequency lo aur count > 1 wale characters filter karo.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

dupes = [c for c, n in Counter('programming').items() if n > 1]
print(sorted(dupes))

intermediate.q: Most frequent character find karo.
intermediate.a: Counter(s).most_common(1) ya max(counter, key=counter.get) — donon O(n).
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

c = Counter('machine learning')
print(c.most_common(2))
intermediate.explain: most_common ties ko insertion order me todta hai, isliye deterministic hai.

intermediate.q: Sentence ke words ka order reverse karo (characters nahi).
intermediate.a: split() se words list banao, reverse karo, aur ' '.join se jodo.
intermediate.code:
s = 'python for data science'
print(' '.join(s.split()[::-1]))

intermediate.q: String se duplicate characters remove karo, order preserve karke.
intermediate.a: Seen set rakho aur sirf naye characters append karo — O(n) aur order safe (set() alone order tod deta hai).
intermediate.code:
s = 'programming'
seen, out = set(), []
for ch in s:
    if ch not in seen:
        seen.add(ch)
        out.append(ch)
print(''.join(out))
intermediate.commonMistake: set(s) se order random ho jata hai — interview me 'preserve order' likha ho to ye galat hai.

intermediate.q: Text me word frequency nikaalo.
intermediate.a: split + Counter; case normalize karna na bhoolo warna 'The' aur 'the' alag gine jayenge.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

text = 'Data data science is data driven'
print(Counter(w.lower() for w in text.split()).most_common(3))

intermediate.q: Email format validate karo (regex ke bina bhi).
intermediate.a: Simple check: exactly ek '@', local aur domain dono non-empty, domain me '.' ho aur aakhri part 2+ characters ka. Regex copy-paste karne se pehle ye rules bolna interview me better lagta hai.
intermediate.tip: Real project me aakhri faisla server-side validation ka hota hai — client check sirf UX hai.

advanced.q: Custom string compression (run-length encoding) implement karo.
advanced.a: Consecutive same characters ka run count karke 'char+count' likho; count 1 ho to sirf character. O(n) time, O(n) space.
advanced.explain: Loop len(s)+1 tak isliye chalta hai taaki last run flush ho jaye.

advanced.q: Longest substring without repeating characters find karo.
advanced.a: Sliding window + last-seen index map: left pointer ko duplicate ke baad shift karo, har step par window length update karo. O(n) time.
advanced.tip: Brute force O(n^2) se shuru karke window par optimize karna interviewer ko pasand aata hai.

advanced.q: Anagram groups banao.
advanced.a: Har word ka sorted-characters ya character-count tuple key banake dictionary me group karo. Sorted key O(k log k) hai, count tuple O(k) — bade inputs par count tuple better.
advanced.code:
from collections import defaultdict

groups = defaultdict(list)
for w in ['eat', 'tea', 'tan', 'ate', 'nat', 'bat']:
    groups[''.join(sorted(w))].append(w)
print(sorted(groups.values()))

advanced.q: Text normalization system banao (punctuation, case, whitespace).
advanced.a: Lowercase → non-alphanumeric ko space → whitespace collapse. Ye idempotent hona chahiye: normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x).
advanced.explain: Idempotency NLP me zaroori hai — warna dobara process karne par data badalta rehta hai.

advanced.q: Search/autocomplete logic implement karo (prefix match).
advanced.a: Sorted words par bisect se prefix ka insertion point dhoondo aur aage scan karke matches do; O(log n + k) milta hai. Yehi tarika SQL ke LIKE 'abc%' se sasta hai jab data memory me ho.
advanced.code:
from bisect import bisect_left

words = sorted(['rag', 'ranking', 'random', 'range', 'transformer'])

def autocomplete(prefix, limit=3):
    i = bisect_left(words, prefix)
    return [w for w in words[i:i + limit] if w.startswith(prefix)]

print(autocomplete('ran'))
print(autocomplete('ra'))

interview.q: Interview me poocha jaye: 'Ek 5 GB log file me ek keyword kitni baar aaya, nikalo' — string knowledge kaise use karoge?
interview.a: Poori file memory me mat lo; line by line padho aur per-line count += line.count(keyword) karo. Agar keyword line boundary par toot sakta hai to chunk overlap rakho. Agar multiple keywords hain to Aho-Corasick ya multi-pattern approach bolna depth dikhata hai.
interview.tip: Memory constraints pehle bolo, phir approach — interviewer yehi order sunna chahta hai.

interview.q: Interview: do strings 'same characters, different order' hain ya nahi — O(n) me batao.
interview.a: Counter(s1) == Counter(s2) O(n) hai; sorted comparison O(n log n) hai. Unicode/bade alphabet me counting array 26 se kaam nahi chalega, Counter safer hai.
interview.tip: Edge cases bolna: length mismatch, spaces, case sensitivity.

interview.q: Interview: string me first non-repeating character find karo.
interview.a: Ek pass me Counter, doosre pass me pehla character jiska count 1 ho — O(n) time, O(k) space.
interview.tip: Ordered pass zaroori hai — sirf Counter ka most_common se ye answer nahi milta.

interview.q: Interview: password strength checker likho aur batao kaunse string operations lagenge.
interview.a: length, any(c.isupper()), any(c.islower()), any(c.isdigit()), any(not c.isalnum()) — paanch checks. Result ko score me convert karo aur weak/medium/strong do. Regex se bhi ho sakta hai par multiple lookaheads readability todte hain.
interview.code:
def strength(p):
    score = sum([len(p) >= 8, any(c.isupper() for c in p), any(c.islower() for c in p), any(c.isdigit() for c in p), any(not c.isalnum() for c in p)])
    return ['very weak', 'weak', 'medium', 'medium', 'strong', 'very strong'][score]

print(strength('Ahetesham@2026'), strength('abcdef'))
interview.tip: Security interview me plain-text password store/log karne ka zikr bhi mat karo — hashing mention karo.

realworld.q: CSV header names ko database-friendly banado ('Monthly Revenue ($)' → 'monthly_revenue').
realworld.a: Lowercase → non-alphanumeric ko underscore → duplicate underscores collapse → kinare ke underscores strip. Ye idempotent hona chahiye.
realworld.code:
import re

def slug(name):
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', name.lower()).strip('_')
    return s

print(slug('Monthly Revenue ($)'))
print(slug('  User-ID  '))

realworld.q: Log line '2026-09-24 10:31:02 ERROR db timeout' se level aur message nikalo.
realworld.a: split(maxsplit=3) se chaar hisse milte hain — date, time, level, message. Fixed positions par split safe hai kyunki message me spaces ho sakti hain.
realworld.code:
line = '2026-09-24 10:31:02 ERROR db timeout'
date, time, level, msg = line.split(maxsplit=3)
print(level, '|', msg)
print(line.startswith('2026'))
realworld.explain: maxsplit=3 exactly 4 hisse deta hai; message ke andar ke spaces safe rehte hain.

realworld.q: Customer name aur phone ko report/LLM prompt me mask karo.
realworld.a: Pehle kuch characters rakho, baaki '*'. Phone ke liye last 4 digits dikhana standard hai.

realworld.q: LLM prompt me context ko token limit ke andar kaise laoge?
realworld.a: Approximate tokens ≈ len(text) / 4 (English), isliye budget se characters nikaalo aur us se zyada context ko end se truncate karo — beginning me instruction rakho, kyunki models start/end par zyada dhyan dete hain. Exact count ke liye tokenizer use karo.
realworld.tip: Ye 'lost in the middle' problem hai — real interview me ye term bolna strong hai.

coding.question: Count vowels, consonants, digits aur spaces ek hi pass me.
coding.build: Function jo counts ka dictionary return kare.
coding.hint: Set banao vowels ka, phir c.isalpha() se consonant verify karo (vowel minus).
coding.explanation: Pehle vowel check karna zaroori hai, warna 'a' consonant group me chala jayega. elif chain single pass me sab classify karti hai.
coding.better: Bade text ke liye Counter(categorise(c) for c in s) se grouped counts milega, par single pass me memory kam lagti hai.
coding.followUp: 5 GB file par kaise karoge? (streaming, chunk overlap, multiprocessing)

coding.question: Palindrome checker likho jo punctuation aur case ignore kare.
coding.build: Function is_palindrome(text) -> bool, sirf alphanumeric compare.
coding.input: 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'
coding.hint: Pehle normalized string banao, phir slicing se reverse.
coding.solution:
def is_palindrome(text):
    clean = [c.lower() for c in text if c.isalnum()]
    return clean == clean[::-1]

print(is_palindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'))
print(is_palindrome('Python Strings'))
coding.explanation: List of chars par comparison slice reverse se hoti hai; do pointers wala approach bhi O(n) hai par zyada code likhna padta hai.
coding.better: Bade input par left/right do pointer use karo — extra list nahi banti, space O(1).
coding.followUp: Sirf punctuation ignore karna ho par case na ho to change kya hoga?

coding.question: Run-length encoding aur decoding dono implement karo.
coding.build: encode(s) aur decode(s), dono round-trip par original wapas dein.
coding.expected: encode → 'a3bc4d' aur decode se original wapas
coding.hint: Decode me digits multi-digit ho sakte hain, isliye accumulate karo.
coding.explanation: Encode me last run flush karne ke liye loop len+1 tak jata hai. Decode me digit run ko accumulate karna zaroori hai warna 'a12' do characters samajh liya jayega.
coding.better: Decode ko index-based while loop ki jagah regex (\w)(\d*) findall se likh sakte hain — chhota code, same complexity.
coding.followUp: Best case me RLE compressed string badi ho jati hai — kab faayda, kab nuksan?

coding.question: Longest substring without repeating characters nikalo.
coding.build: Function longest_unique(s) → substring return kare.
coding.hint: Sliding window: har character ka last index yaad rakho aur left pointer ko duplicate ke aage shift karo.
coding.concept: Sliding window over an immutable sequence
coding.explanation: last[ch] >= left check window se bahar ke purane occurrence ko ignore karta hai — iske bina left galat shift hota hai.
coding.better: Set-based version se bhi O(n) milta hai par set par remove karna padta hai; index map version ek pass me chalta hai.
coding.followUp: Agar at most k repeats allowed hon to kaise badaloge? (window + count map)

coding.question: Anagram groups banao aur har group ko alphabetical order me do.
coding.build: Function group_anagrams(words) → list of sorted groups.
coding.hint: Key ke liye sorted characters ya character-count tuple use karo.
coding.explanation: Canonical key se 'eat' aur 'tea' ek hi bucket me aate hain. Post-processing me groups aur unke andar ke words sort karna expected output deterministic banata hai.
coding.time: O(n · k log k), k = word length
coding.better: Counting tuple (26-tuple) key O(k) hai isliye bade words par sorted key se tez — Unicode ke liye Counter tuple.
coding.followUp: Streaming input (words aate rehte hain) par grouping kaise karoge?

coding.question: Text se top-N keywords nikalo stop words hata kar.
coding.build: Function top_keywords(text, n) → [(word, count)] frequency order me.
coding.input: Machine learning is a field of study and machine learning needs data
coding.hint: Normalize → split → stop word set se filter → Counter.
coding.explanation: strip('.,!?') punctuation hatata hai, lower case normalize karta hai, aur generator expression stop words ko counter tak pahunchne hi nahi deta.
coding.better: Stemming/lemmatization (learning → learn) se 'learning' aur 'learn' merge ho jate hain; bade corpora me regex tokenizer better.
coding.followUp: TF-IDF kya add karega frequency ke upar? (rare words ko weight)

coding.question: Caesar cipher (shift) implement karo aur shift-aware validation rakho.
coding.build: encrypt(text, shift) aur decrypt(text, shift) — sirf letters shift hon.
coding.hint: chr/ord se wrap karo: uppercase aur lowercase ka base alag hai.
coding.output: Dwwdfn dw gdzq! Attack at dawn!
coding.explanation: % 26 se z se aage wrap hota hai; base ord('A')/ord('a') alag rakhne se case preserve hota hai.
coding.better: str.translate + translate table banane se C-level speed milti hai — per-character Python loop hat jata hai.
coding.followUp: Frequency analysis is cipher ko kaise todti hai, aur modern encryption kya alag karti hai?

print('Marks: ' + marks)

debugging.why: Python weakly typed nahi hai — + do strings ko jodta hai, int ko automatic string nahi banata. Java/C# ka implicit conversion yahan nahi hota.
debugging.fix: f-string use karo ya str() se convert karo.
debugging.correct:

debugging.broken:

print(s.count())

projects.name: Text Analyzer (Version 1)
projects.problem: Naye learners ko string methods, loops aur dictionaries ka ek hi practical run chahiye — par plain practice ke bina ek 'result' feel hoti hai jo seekhne me madad karti hai.
projects.objective: Ek chhota program jo user ke text ka character count, word count, vowel count aur sentence count bataye.
features: Character count (spaces ke saath aur bina)
Word count aur average word length

└── analyzer.py      # saara logic, ek file

Counts ko dictionary me rakho aur f-string se report print karke test karo.
projects.code:
def analyse(text):
    words = text.split()
    vowels = set('aeiou')
    counts = {
        'chars_with_spaces': len(text),
        'chars_no_spaces': len(text.replace(' ', '')),
        'words': len(words),
        'vowels': sum(1 for c in text.lower() if c in vowels),
        'sentences': sum(1 for c in text if c in '.!?'),
    }
    counts['avg_word_len'] = round(sum(len(w) for w in words) / len(words), 2) if words else 0
    return counts

report = analyse('Python strings are immutable. String methods return new objects!')
for k, v in report.items():
    print(f'{k:20} : {v}')

concepts.title: Section overview
concepts.body: Python me strings par kaam karne ke liye ready-made methods hote hain. Ye original string ko badalte nahi, hamesha naya string return karte hain, isliye result ko variable me store karna zaroori hai. String methods Swiss army knife ke tools hain. Har tool ek chhota kaam karta hai: kaatna, jodna, badalna, dhoondhna.

concepts.title: upper()
concepts.body: Sare characters ko UPPERCASE me convert karta hai.
concepts.code:
text = "hello world"
print(text.upper())
print(text)  # original nahi badla
concepts.tip: String methods original string ko change nahi karte, naya string return karte hain. text = text.upper() likhna padega.

concepts.title: lower()
concepts.body: Sare characters ko lowercase me convert karta hai. Comparison se pehle use karo.
concepts.code:
text = "HELLO WORLD"
print(text.lower())
email = "Ashu@Gmail.COM"
print(email.lower())

concepts.title: strip()
concepts.body: Start aur end se extra spaces (ya given characters) hata deta hai. User input saaf karne ke liye must.
concepts.code:
text = " hello "
print(text.strip())
print("xxhixx".strip("x"))

concepts.title: lstrip() / rstrip()
concepts.body: Sirf left ya sirf right side se spaces/characters remove karta hai. repr() se quotes dikhte hain.
concepts.code:
text = " hello "
print(repr(text.lstrip()))
print(repr(text.rstrip()))

concepts.title: split()
concepts.body: String ko separator ke basis par tod kar list bana deta hai. Bina argument ke spaces par todta hai.
concepts.code:
text = "apple,banana,mango"
print(text.split(","))
print("I love Python".split())

concepts.title: join()
concepts.body: List of strings ko separator ke saath jodkar single string banata hai. split() ka ulta.
concepts.code:
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
print(", ".join(fruits))
print("-".join("abc"))
concepts.tip: join() sirf strings jodta hai. Numbers ki list ho to pehle convert karo: ",".join(str(n) for n in nums).

concepts.title: replace()
concepts.body: Ek part dhoondh kar dusre se badal deta hai. Default me saare matches badalta hai.
concepts.code:
text = "I like cats and cats"                  # sirf pehla
print(text.replace("cats", "dogs"))
print(text.replace("cats", "dogs", 1))
concepts.output:
I like dogs and dogs
I like dogs and cats

concepts.title: startswith()
concepts.body: Check karta hai string given prefix se start hoti hai ya nahi.
concepts.code:
text = "hello world"
print(text.startswith("hello"))
print("report.pdf".startswith(("data", "report")))   # tuple bhi chalta hai

concepts.title: endswith()
concepts.body: Check karta hai string given suffix par end hoti hai ya nahi. File extension check ke liye best.
concepts.code:
text = "hello world"
print(text.endswith("world"))
print("photo.jpg".endswith((".jpg", ".png")))

concepts.title: format()

topic.intro: String methods wahi roz-marra ka kaam karte hain: input saaf karna, text todna-jodna, dhundna aur validate karna. Sabse bada trap ye hai ki string immutable hai — method naya string return karta hai, original ko chhoota nahi. Isliye 'method chala diya par result store nahi kiya' wala bug beginners ke saath hamesha hota hai, aur isi section me usko hamesha ke liye theek kiya jata hai.
theory: Har string method naya string (ya number/list) return karta hai; original string kabhi nahi badalti. Isliye cleaned = text.strip().lower() likhna padta hai — sirf text.strip() ka result kho jata hai.

Case methods: lower/upper display ke liye, casefold comparison ke liye (Unicode-safe, 'STRASSE'.casefold() == 'strasse'), title/capitalize human display ke liye — aur ye har word ki hyphen/quote boundary par bhi todte hain.

Whitespace aur splitting: strip/lstrip/rstrip optional characters lete hain, split() bina argument kisi bhi whitespace run par todta hai (aur leading/trailing hatata hai), jabki split(',') exact character par todta hai. join() list ko jodta hai — separator 'sep'.join(parts).

Search aur replace: find() -1 deta hai, index() ValueError deta hai; startswith/endswith tuples accept karte hain (multiple suffixes), replace() ek count limit leta hai, removeprefix/removesuffix (3.9+) prefix/suffix ke liye safer aur explicit hain.

Validation: isalpha/isdigit/isalnum/isspace/isnumeric/isupper/islower. Ye Unicode-aware hain — '१२'.isdigit() True ho sakta hai. Translation ke liye str.maketrans + translate, aur formatting ke liye format/format_map.
syntax:
s.strip(); s.lstrip('0'); s.rstrip('.!?')
s.split(); s.split(',', 1); s.rsplit(',', 1)
'-'.join(parts); s.partition(',')
s.replace('a', 'b', 2); s.expandtabs(4)

s.lower(); s.upper(); s.casefold(); s.title(); s.capitalize()
s.find('x'); s.rfind('x'); s.index('x'); s.count('x')
s.startswith(('http://', 'https://')); s.endswith('.csv')
s.removeprefix('v'); s.removesuffix('.txt')

s.isalpha(); s.isdigit(); s.isspace(); s.isidentifier()
str.maketrans({'a': '4', 'e': '3'}); s.translate(table)
f'{name}'.strip(); '{:.2f}'.format(value); '{name}'.format_map(row)

s.zfill(8); s.center(20, '-'); s.ljust(10); s.rjust(10)
s.splitlines(); s.splitlines(keepends=True)
s.encode('utf-8'); b.decode('utf-8')

strip() ka result store nahi kiya, isliye raw waise hi raha — len() dono ka fark yahi dikhata hai (immutability ka live proof).

endswith() tuple leta hai, isliye ek hi call me multiple extensions check ho jate hain.
rsplit('/', 1) aur rsplit('.', 1) right side se ek hi baar todte hain — filename aur extension nikalne ka safe tarika (path me multiple dots ho to bhi kaam karta hai).
find() position deta hai, count() ginti — replace() ka count argument sirf pehli n occurrences badalta hai.

examples.code:
TEXT = '''Python   string methods
many kaam karte hain!!  

Clean karna zaroori hai.'''

def normalize(text):
    lines = [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines()]
    lines = [line for line in lines if line]
    return ' '.join(lines)

def collapse_spaces(text):
    return ' '.join(text.split())

clean = collapse_spaces(normalize(TEXT))
print(repr(clean))
print('words:', len(clean.split()))

stripped = clean.lower().strip('!. ')
print('stripped punctuation:', repr(stripped[-30:]))

table = str.maketrans({'a': '4', 'e': '3', 'i': '1', 'o': '0'})
print('leet:', clean[:28].translate(table))

print('title :', clean.title()[:34])
print('center:', '[{}]'.format(clean[:10].center(16, '=')))
print('checks:', clean[:5].isalpha(), clean[:5].istitle(), repr(clean[:5].zfill(8)))

'Python string methods many kaam karte hain!! Clean karna zaroori hai.'
words: 11
stripped punctuation: 'hain!! clean karna zaroori hai'
leet: Pyth0n str1ng m3th0ds m4ny k

center: [===Python str===]
checks: True True '000Pytho'
explain: splitlines() newline types (\n, \r\n) dono handle karta hai — isliye file text clean karne me splitlines safer hai.
collapse: text.split() saare whitespace runs ko todta hai aur ' '.join se single spaces aate hain — double space aur tabs ek saath normalize ho jate hain.
translate + maketrans character-level replacement ka fast tarika hai (chain of replace() se behtar), aur strip('!. ') strip ko char-set treat karta hai, prefix nahi.

realWorld: Form aur CSV cleaning: user ka ' Pune ' aur 'pune' ek hi city hai — strip + casefold + punctuation remove ka order har data pipeline ka pehla step hota hai, warna group-by me do rows ban jati hain.
Log parsing: find/index se message nikalna, count se error tally, aur replace se masking (credit card digits, email) — security logs me PII redaction isi tarah hota hai.
Filename aur URL handling: removesuffix/removeprefix aur endswith tuple validation se extension-based routing (upload API me .csv/.json) safe rehta hai — bina regex ke.

interview.q: strip() aur replace() ne string badla nahi — kaise?
interview.a: Strings immutable hain: ye methods naya object return karte hain aur original waisa hi rehta hai. Isliye s.strip() ka result store karna padta hai. Performance-wise in-place feel deta hai kyunki Python internally join/replace ko optimized C me karta hai, par semantics copy-based hai.
interview.tip: Interview me immutability ka practical asar (hashability, thread safety, memory) bhi mention karo.

interview.q: split() aur split(' ') me difference kya hai?
interview.a: split() whitespace ka koi bhi run separator maanta hai aur leading/trailing whitespace hata deta hai — is liye 'a  b'.split() -> ['a', 'b']. split(' ') exact single space par todta hai, isliye 'a  b'.split(' ')-> ['a', '', 'b'] (empty string aa jati hai). CSV/TSV me exact separator chahiye, human text me split() better hai.
interview.tip: Ye interview me favor ka question hai — ek line ka example do, bas.

interview.q: Text comparison ke liye lower() ya casefold()?
interview.a: casefold() — ye Unicode ke liye aggressive normalize karta hai (ß -> ss), isliye case-insensitive comparison correct hoti hai. lower() sirf character-wise lowercasing karta hai aur kuch scripts me 'equal hone chahiye' wale cases miss kar deta hai. Display ke liye lower()/title() theek hai, comparison ke liye casefold().
interview.tip: Turkish 'I'/dotless-i case bhi batao — locale-aware comparison ka nuance dikhata hai.

interview.q: find() vs index() vs in — kab kaun?
interview.a: Sirf 'mojood hai ya nahi' puchna ho to 'sub in s' (fast, readable). Position chahiye par missing case normal hai to find() (-1). Missing case exception hona chahiye to index(). Repeated search ya multiple patterns ke liye re module better hai — 1000 calls se pehle regex consider karo.
interview.tip: Exception-driven flow vs sentinel return ka trade-off discuss karo — interviewer design sense dekhta hai.

interview.q: Ek bada log text se saare URLs nikalne hain — string methods kaafi hain?
interview.a: Nahi. String methods substring ke liye hain, pattern ke liye nahi. URL/email jaise structured patterns ke liye re (regex) use karo: re.findall(r'https?://[^\s]+', text). String methods tab best hain jab delimiter fix ho (split, partition, startswith/endswith).
interview.tip: Regex ka answer dene ke baad ek simple case bhi batao jahan string method better hai — balanced judgement dikhata hai.

beginner.a: s.removeprefix('v') aur s.removesuffix('.csv') — exact match par kaam karte hain aur na mile to string unchanged return karte hain.

intermediate.q: Ek email-ish string ko validate karo: ek '@', koi space nahi, domain me dot.

intermediate.q: Text ke duplicate words dhundo aur batao kaun kitni baar aaya.
intermediate.a: casefold ke baad split, Counter se ginti, phir 1 se zyada count wale words.
intermediate.explain: Case normalization pehle karna zaroori hai warna 'Data' aur 'data' alag maane jayenge.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

text = 'Data science me data clean karna Data ka pehla step hai'
words = [w.strip('.,!?').casefold() for w in text.split() if w.strip('.,!?')]
counts = Counter(words)

print('total words:', len(words), 'unique:', len(counts))
for word, n in counts.most_common(5):
    print(f'  {word:10} {n}')
print('duplicates:', sorted(w for w, n in counts.items() if n > 1))

intermediate.q: Log line se severity, timestamp aur message alag karo (string methods se).

intermediate.q: Slug banao: 'Python String Methods!' -> 'python-string-methods'.
intermediate.a: casefold, non-alnum ko space me badlo, split, strip, join('-').
intermediate.explain: Slug generation URL-safe naming ka standard hai; translate() se punctuation hatana fast hai.

advanced.q: Ek redaction function likho jo email aur phone ko mask kare (log safety ke liye).
advanced.a: Pattern-based replace: email ke local part ka pehla character rakho, phone ke aakhri 4 digits rakho.
advanced.explain: Security-safe logging me PII mask karna compliance requirement hoti hai.
advanced.code:
import re

def mask_email(match):
    local, domain = match.group(0).split('@')
    return f'{local[0]}***@{domain}'

def mask_phone(match):
    digits = match.group(0)
    return '*' * (len(digits) - 4) + digits[-4:]

PHONE = re.compile(r'\b\d{10}\b')

raw_tags = '  Python , Data Science ,python,  ML  , , DATA SCIENCE  '

def normalize_tags(raw, sep=','):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for tag in raw.split(sep):

coding.solution:
import string

PUNCT = string.punctuation

def clean_words(text):
    words = []
    for raw in text.split():
        word = raw.strip(PUNCT).casefold()
        if word:
            words.append(word)
    return words

text = '  Python   STRING methods!!  Text clean karna aasan hai.  '
cleaned = clean_words(text)
print(cleaned)
print('count:', len(cleaned))
print('unique:', len(set(cleaned)))
print('collapsed repr:', repr(' '.join(cleaned)))

coding.question: Ek 'keyword search' function likho jo text me query ke saare occurrences position ke saath de, case-insensitive.
coding.build: find_all(text, query) -> list of (start, end, snippet)
coding.expected: Har occurrence ki index aur 20-char snippet.
coding.hint: Dono ko casefold karo (length same rehta hai lowercase me) aur find() ko loop me start se aage badhao.
coding.solution:
def find_all(text, query, context=12):
    haystack = text.casefold()
    needle = query.casefold()
    if not needle:
        return []
    hits, start = [], haystack.find(needle)
    while start != -1:
        end = start + len(needle)
        snippet = text[max(0, start - context): end + context].replace(chr(10), ' ')
        hits.append((start, end, snippet))
        start = haystack.find(needle, end)
    return hits

text = 'Data science me data cleaning zaroori hai. Data ka analysis baad me hota hai.'
for start, end, snippet in find_all(text, 'DATA'):
    print(f'{start:>3}-{end:<3} ...{snippet}...')
print('total hits:', len(find_all(text, 'data')))
print('empty query:', find_all(text, ''))
coding.output:
0-4   ...Data science me ...
 16-20  ... science me data cleaning za...
 43-47  ...aroori hai. Data ka analysis...
total hits: 3
empty query: []
coding.explanation: start = end se aage badhna overlapping hits ko rok deta hai aur infinite loop bhi (query 'aa' ke saath) — ye zaroori safety hai. casefold ke baad index positions original text me hi valid rehte hain (length preservation assumption document karo).
coding.time: O(n × m) worst case (n text, m query) — Python ka find optimized C me hai
coding.better: Bahut bade text ke liye re.finditer ya KMP/Aho-Corasick (multi-pattern) use karo; overlapping matches chahiye to ek-ek index par check karo.
coding.followUp: Multiple keywords (100+) search karne ho to ek-ek find loop kaise slow ho jayega, aur Aho-Corasick ise kaise theek karta hai?

coding.question: Duplicate detector likho jo text me repeated words aur repeated lines dhunde, case-insensitive.
coding.build: find_duplicates(text) -> (duplicate_words, duplicate_lines)
coding.input: Multi-line text with repeated words and one repeated line
coding.expected: Aise words/lines ki list jo ek se zyada baar aayein.
coding.hint: Words ke liye Counter, lines ke liye normalize (strip + casefold) karke Counter.
coding.solution:
from collections import Counter

TEXT = '''Data cleaning is step one.
Python me data cleaning aasan hai.
DATA CLEANING sabse pehla step hai.
'''

def tokens(text):
    return [w.strip('.,!?;:').casefold() for w in text.split() if w.strip('.,!?;:')]

def find_duplicates(text):
    word_counts = Counter(tokens(text))
    line_counts = Counter(' '.join(line.split()).casefold() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip())
    dup_words = {w: c for w, c in word_counts.items() if c > 1}
    dup_lines = {l: c for l, c in line_counts.items() if c > 1}
    return dup_words, dup_lines

dup_words, dup_lines = find_duplicates(TEXT)
print('duplicate words:', dup_words)
print('duplicate lines:', list(dup_lines)[:2])
print('first line duplicates found:', bool(dup_lines))
print('word count check:', len(tokens(TEXT)))
coding.output:
duplicate words: {'data': 3, 'cleaning': 3, 'step': 2, 'hai': 2}
duplicate lines: []
first line duplicates found: False
word count check: 17
coding.explanation: Words ke liye punctuation strip + casefold (warna 'Data' aur 'data' alag), lines ke liye whitespace collapse + casefold — dono normalization levels alag hain kyunki comparison unit alag hai.
coding.better: Bade corpuses ke liye streaming Counter (line-by-line) aur n-gram duplicate detection (near-duplicate lines ke liye) use karo; fuzzy dupes ke liye difflib.SequenceMatcher.
coding.followUp: Near-duplicate lines ('Data cleaning step one' vs 'Data cleaning is step one') kaise pakdoge — similarity threshold kaise choose karoge?

coding.question: Ek text preprocessing pipeline likho: normalize, punctuation strip, stop-word removal, aur token stats — sab string methods + sets se.
coding.build: preprocess(text, stopwords) -> dict with tokens, counts, stats, aur removed info
coding.expected: Clean tokens, top-5 frequency, aur original vs clean token count.
coding.hint: Ek pass me tokens banao, ek pass me filter; stats dict me counts rakho (aur normalization ke stats bhi).
coding.concept: Pipeline design, string normalization, Counter aggregation
coding.solution:
from collections import Counter

STOPWORDS = {'is', 'me', 'ka', 'ki', 'hai', 'aur', 'se', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'to'}

TEXT = '''Python string methods se text clean karna aasan hai!
Data cleaning is the first step of any pipeline.
Methods like strip, split and replace are used the most.'''

def strip_punct(word):
    return word.strip('.,!?;:"()[]')

def preprocess(text, stopwords=STOPWORDS):
    raw_tokens = text.split()
    lowered = [strip_punct(w).casefold() for w in raw_tokens]
    tokens = [w for w in lowered if w]
    kept = [w for w in tokens if w not in stopwords]
    counts = Counter(kept)
    stats = {
        'lines': len(text.splitlines()),
        'raw_tokens': len(raw_tokens),
        'clean_tokens': len(tokens),
        'kept_tokens': len(kept),
        'removed_stopwords': len(tokens) - len(kept),
        'unique': len(counts),
        'avg_token_len': round(sum(len(w) for w in kept) / len(kept), 2) if kept else 0.0,
    }
    return {'tokens': kept, 'top': counts.most_common(5), 'stats': stats}

result = preprocess(TEXT)
for key, value in result['stats'].items():
    print(f'{key:20}: {value}')
print('top terms       :', result['top'])
print('sample tokens   :', result['tokens'][:8])
coding.output:
lines               : 3
raw_tokens          : 28
clean_tokens        : 28
kept_tokens         : 22
removed_stopwords   : 6
unique              : 21
avg_token_len       : 5.09
top terms       : [('methods', 2), ('python', 1), ('string', 1), ('text', 1), ('clean', 1)]
sample tokens   : ['python', 'string', 'methods', 'text', 'clean', 'karna', 'aasan', 'data']
coding.explanation: Pipeline ke stages explicit hain (lower -> strip -> filter empty -> stopwords) isliye har stage ka count track hota hai — data quality debug karna aasan ho jata hai. stats me avg_token_len aur unique jaisa information rakhna downstream analysis (keyword density) me kaam aata hai.
coding.better: Large corpus ke liye streaming + nltk/spaCy tokenizers, aur stemming/lemmatization add karo; stopword list ko language-specific config se load karo (hardcode na karo).
coding.followUp: Kya stopwords hataana sahi hai? ('not' hataane se sentiment ulta ho jata hai) — real NLP me ye decision kaise lena chahiye?

interview.q: Duplicate detection Counter par kyun, difflib par kyun nahi?

Simple ASCII text me casefold length preserve karta hai — isliye ye assumption document karni chahiye.

interview.q: Inverted index se search fast kaise hota hai?
interview.a: Design time par word -> positions ki mapping ban jati hai, isliye query O(1) average hash lookup hai instead of O(n) scan. Cost: build time O(n) aur memory (positions store karni padti hain). Trade-off: positional index space zyada leta hai, boolean index kam.

topic.intro: Decision making hi program ko 'sochne' layak banati hai. if/elif/else simple lagta hai, par asli dikkat do jagah aati hai: condition ka order (pehla match hi chalta hai) aur truthiness (0 aur '' valid data hote hain, par falsy hain). Ye section in dono traps ko pakadta hai aur match/case naam ka modern alternative bhi sikhata hai.
theory: if/elif/else chain top se neeche evaluate hoti hai aur pehli true branch chalne ke baad poora chain skip ho jata hai. Isliye specific condition pehle aur general baad me likhni chahiye — ulta order silently galat result deta hai.

Condition me koi bhi object chalta hai (truthiness): 0, 0.0, '', [], {}, set(), None aur False falsy hain, baaki sab truthy. 'if value:' ko 'value mojood hai' maan lena trap hai — 0 aur '' valid values hain, unke liye 'is None' ya 'is not None' use karo.
Ternary (x if cond else y) ek expression hai, statement nahi — isliye assignment, return aur function argument me seedha use hota hai. Readability ke liye ek level se zyada nesting mat karo.
Lambda/nested conditions ko guard clauses se flatten karo: invalid case pe early return ya continue karo, taaki happy path seedha aur indentation flat rahe.

match/case (3.10+) structural pattern matching hai: literal patterns, OR patterns (|), sequence/mapping patterns, class patterns aur guards (case X if cond). Ye long if/elif chains ko table jaisa readable banata hai jab decisions patterns par based hon.
syntax:
label = 'pass' if score >= 40 else 'fail'
if value is None:
    value = default
if not items:            # empty check
    return 'no data'

match command.split():
    case ['add', name]:
        add(name)
    case ['remove' | 'rm', name]:
        remove(name)
    case ['list']:
        show()
    case _:
        raise ValueError('unknown command')

match payload:
    case {'type': 'user', 'name': str(name)}:
        print('user', name)
    case {'type': 'order', 'total': total} if total > 1000:
        print('big order', total)
    case _:
        print('unhandled')

Tuple return (value, error) se caller ko do possibilities explicitly handle karni padti hain — silent None se better design hai.
discount_label me 'rate is None' aur 'rate == 0' alag handle kiye gaye — yahi truthiness trap ka fix hai: 'if rate:' 0 ko 'no discount' bana deta.

examples.code:
def handle(command, store=None):
    store = store if store is not None else {}
    parts = command.split()
    match parts:
        case ['add', key, value]:
            store[key] = value
            return f'added {key}={value}'
        case ['get', key]:
            if key not in store:
                return f'{key}: not found'
            return f'{key}={store[key]}'
        case ['delete' | 'remove' | 'rm', key]:
            return f'deleted {key}' if store.pop(key, None) is not None else f'{key}: not found'
        case ['list'] if store:
            return 'list: ' + ', '.join(sorted(store))
        case ['list']:
            return 'list: (empty)'
        case ['set', *_] :
            return 'set needs exactly key and value'
        case _:
            return f'unknown command: {command!r}'

for cmd in ('add city Pune', 'get city', 'get missing', 'rm city', 'list', 'set onlykey', 'hello there'):
    print(f'{cmd:18} -> {handle(cmd)}')

print('rules:', sum(1 for c in ('add a b',) if c.startswith('add')))

add city Pune      -> added city=Pune
get city           -> city: not found
get missing        -> missing: not found
rm city            -> city: not found
list               -> list: (empty)
set onlykey        -> set needs exactly key and value

explain: Sequence patterns command string ko tokens me todkar match karte hain, aur OR patterns (delete|remove|rm) ek hi branch me aliases handle karte hain.
Guard (case ['list'] if store) pehle try hota hai; guard false hone par Python agla matching case dhundta hai, isliye 'list' ke liye do branches likh sakte hain.
Wildcard capture (*_) verify karta hai ki galat arity wala command explicit message de, aur case _ fallback hamesha last me — isi se unknown commands crash nahi karte.

realWorld: Access aur eligibility decisions (loan, insurance, discount) rule chains hote hain — condition ka order aur boundary values (0, exactly threshold) business loss ya compliance issue bana dete hain.
API aur CLI command dispatch me match/case se readable routing banta hai; unknown input ke liye explicit fallback rakhna security aur UX dono ke liye zaroori hai.
Form validation me truthiness par bharosa karna classic production bug hai: 0 quantity, '' address aur False consent jaise valid-but-falsy values galat branch me chale jate hain.

interview.q: if/elif/else me condition ka order kyun critical hai?
interview.a: Chain pehla true branch chunte hai aur baaki skip karta hai, isliye general condition pehle likhne se specific case unreachable ho jata hai (dead code). Rule: sabse specific/tight condition pehle, broad baad me; aur agar overlap intentional ho to comment karo.
interview.tip: Dead branch ka chhota example de do — isse pata chalta hai aapne ye bug actually debug kiya hai.

interview.q: Truthiness par bharosa karna kab galat hota hai?
interview.a: Jab 0, '' , False, [] valid data hon. 'if total:' se 0 total skip ho jata hai; 'if name:' se intentionally empty string alag treat hoti hai. Solutions: 'if total is not None:', sentinel object (UNSET), ya explicit type/boundary checks. Ye bug quantity, discount, port, retry-count jaise fields me aata hai.
interview.tip: Ek real field batao (retries=0) — abstract jawab se better hai.

interview.q: match/case kab if/elif se better hai?
interview.a: Jab decision structure par ho: tuples/lists ka shape, dict keys, class types, OR alternatives. Tab code table jaisa readable ho jata hai. Simple range comparisons (score >= 90) me if/elif zyada clear hai. Note: match structural hai — 'case 1' value ka comparison nahi, pattern match hai (aur constants/classes ke liye special rules hain).
interview.tip: Guard clause aur wildcard ka mention karo — isse pata chalta hai aapne actual use kiya hai.

interview.q: Ternary expression me kya limits rakhni chahiye?
interview.a: Ek level tak theek hai: label = 'ok' if status == 200 else 'error'. Nesting (a if x else b if y else c) me readability gir jati hai; walrus (:=) ke saath mix karna bhi confusing ho jata hai. Agar branch me side effect ho, to if/else statement hi likho — expression me side effect chhupana bad practice hai.
interview.tip: Side-effect wala example do: 'do(x) if cond else do(y)' — samajhna mushkil hota hai.

interview.q: Comparison ko float ke saath kaise karte hain?
interview.a: Exact == avoid karo (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3). Tolerance use karo: abs(a - b) < 1e-9, ya math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=1e-9). Money ke liye Decimal aur boundary values par round/quantize karke compare karo.
interview.tip: Boundary condition ke liye > vs >= ka farak test case se dikhao (threshold exactly equal hone par kaun sa branch).

beginner.q: Check karo ki number positive, negative ya zero hai.
beginner.a: if n > 0 / elif n < 0 / else zero — order se farak nahi padta kyunki conditions exclusive hain.
beginner.explain: Exclusive conditions me order se farak nahi padta; overlapping hone par padta hai.
beginner.tip: Interview me boundary (0) ka test mention karo — yahi sabse common miss hota hai.

beginner.q: Ek number even hai ya odd, ternary se ek line me print karo.
beginner.a: print('even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd')
beginner.explain: Ternary expression ko seedha print ke argument me use kar sakte hain — statement nahi hai.

for n in (0, 7, 42):
    print(f'{n:>3}', 'even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd')
beginner.tip: Ternary ko assignment me bhi use karo: label = 'even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd'.

beginner.a: Chained comparison ke saath if/elif, aur invalid age (negative) ke liye alag branch.
beginner.explain: Chained comparison boundary ko readable banata hai (12 < age < 60 jaisi galti nahi hoti).

intermediate.a: List pattern se tokens match karo, OR pattern se aliases, aur case _ se unknown command.

intermediate.code:
def dispatch(command, store=None):
    store = store if store is not None else {}
    match command.split():
        case ['add', key, value]:
            store[key] = value
            return f'added {key}'
        case ['get', key] if key in store:
            return f'{key}={store[key]}'
        case ['get', key]:

        case ['delete' | 'rm', key]:
            return f'removed {key}' if store.pop(key, None) is not None else 'nothing to remove'
        case _:
