topic.intro: Dictionary key-value pairs ka collection hai: ek key se seedha value milta hai, O(1) average. Ye Python ka sabse practical data structure hai — JSON, API responses, records, counts, config sab dictionaries hain. Is topic me do cheezein master karni hain: (1) lookup safe karna (d[key] vs d.get(key)) aur (2) dictionary ko aggregate/structure ki tarah use karna (frequency counting, grouping, nested records) — kyunki real code me dictionary aksar yahi kaam karti hai.
theory: Dictionary mutable hai, keys unique hain, aur insertion order preserve karti hai (Python 3.7+). Key hashable hona chahiye: int, str, tuple chalti hai; list/dict/set keys nahi ban sakti (TypeError).

Lookup d[key] O(1) average hai par missing key par KeyError deta hai; d.get(key, default) missing par default (None) deta hai. Safe read ke liye get, aur 'key chahiye hi' wale code me direct [] — dono ka apna use case hai.

Iteration: for k in d → keys, d.values() → values, d.items() → (key, value) pairs. Iteration ke dauraan dict ka size badalna RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration deta hai — isliye pehle list(d.items()) banao ya nayi dict compose karo.
Counting aur grouping ke liye collections.Counter aur defaultdict(list) dict ke upar built hain; defaultdict missing key par factory call karta hai, isliye 'if key not in d' boilerplate hat jata hai.

Dict comprehension {k: v for ...} ek line me transform/filter deti hai. Merge ke liye d | other (Python 3.9+) nayi dict deta hai, aur d.update(other) in-place hai — update me right side ki value jeet ti hai.
syntax:
d['role']              # KeyError if missing
d.get('city', 'unknown')   # safe read
d['level'] = 'beginner'     # upsert
del d['level']; d.pop('level', None); d.popitem()

examples.code:
student = {'name': 'Neha', 'marks': 88, 'course': 'AI'}
print(student['name'], student.get('city', 'unknown'))
student['marks'] = 92
student['city'] = 'Pune'
print(list(student.keys()))
print(list(student.values()))
print('city' in student, 'phone' in student)
explain: student['name'] direct lookup hai — key guaranteed hai isliye KeyError ka risk nahi.
get('city', 'unknown') missing key par fallback deta hai; direct access hota to KeyError aata.
Assignment naya key add karta hai aur existing key ki value update karta hai (upsert) — dictionary mutable hai isliye ye in-place hota hai.
keys()/values() view objects dete hain jo live hain: dict badalne par view bhi badal jata hai. in operator average O(1) mein membership check karta hai.

examples.code:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

text = 'data is data science and data is powerful'
freq = Counter(text.split())
print(freq.most_common(3))

by_len = defaultdict(list)
for word in set(text.split()):
    by_len[len(word)].append(word)
print(dict(sorted(by_len.items())))

prices = {'apple': 90, 'banana': 80, 'mango': 120}
print(sorted(prices.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]))
print({k: v for k, v in prices.items() if v > 85})
explain: Counter missing key par 0 deta hai (dict me KeyError aata), isliye frequency counting one-liner ban jati hai.
defaultdict(list) me naye key par automatically empty list banti hai — 'if key not in d: d[key] = []' pattern ki zaroorat nahi.
sorted(prices.items(), key=kv[1]) value par sort karta hai; items() tuples deta hai isliye index 1 value hai.
Comprehension me filter lagakar nayi dict banti hai — original prices unchanged rehti hai.
deep_get har level par isinstance + membership check karta hai, isliye missing path par KeyError nahi aata — config/API data ke liye yahi pattern chahiye.
Path string ko split('.') se todte hain, isliye caller ko khud nested dict banane ki zaroorat nahi padti.
group_by defaultdict(list) se ek pass me grouping karti hai; akhir me dict() me wrap karke normal dict return karte hain taaki caller ko defaultdict ki semantics na thop jayein.
json.dumps ko sirf serialisable structures do — dict/list/str/int/float; isliye yahan grouped rows se sirf names nikaal kar bhej rahe hain.

realWorld: API/JSON data: response parse karke keys se value nikalna, missing fields par default dena — deep_get wala pattern har integration me use hota hai.
Grouping aur reporting: SQL jaise GROUP BY ka Python version defaultdict(list) hai — team-wise, category-wise summaries yahi se banti hain.
Config management: layered config (defaults + env + file) dict merge (| ya update) se banati hai, aur environment-specific overrides asaan ho jate hain.
Frequency/counting: logs me error codes, NLP me word counts, analytics me event counts — Counter dict ka hi built-in version hai.

interview.q: Dictionary ki average lookup complexity kitni hai aur worst case kya hai?
interview.a: Average O(1) — key ka hash compute hota hai aur hash table bucket me jaata hai. Worst case O(n) hai jab bahut saare keys ka hash collide kare (adversarial input), isliye Python hash randomization use karta hai. Memory overhead O(n) hi hai.
interview.tip: Hash randomization ka zikr karo — ye security angle dikhata hai.

interview.q: d[key] aur d.get(key) me kya choose karte ho?
interview.a: d[key] tab jab key ka hona contract ka hissa ho — missing key ek real bug hai aur turant KeyError se pata chalna chahiye (fail fast). d.get tab jab default sensible ho (optional field, counter increment, config fallback). Interview me bolna: 'get se bug chhup bhi sakta hai', isliye choice intent ke hisaab se karo.
interview.tip: Fail-fast vs default ka framing strong answer hai.

interview.q: Iteration ke dauraan dict se key delete karna kyun error deta hai?
interview.a: Python RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration raise karta hai kyunki iterator table ke size par walk kar raha hota hai aur size badalne se behaviour undefined ho jata. Solution: list(d.keys()) ka copy par iterate karo, ya comprehension se nayi dict banao.
interview.tip: Ye Python ka deliberate choice hai (silent corruption se better) — ye point bolna acchha lagta hai.

interview.q: Two dictionaries merge karne ke kitne tarike hain?
interview.a: d1.update(d2) in-place (d2 jeetta hai), {**d1, **d2} nayi dict (same precedence), aur d1 | d2 (3.9+) nayi dict. Deep merge ke liye recursive function chahiye kyunki teenon shallow hain — nested dicts replace ho jati hain, merge nahi hoti.
interview.tip: Deep merge ka limitation volunteer karo — bahut se candidates yahan fasste hain.

interview.q: Counter defaultdict aur normal dict ka relation samjhao.
interview.a: Dono collections module me dict ke subclasses hain. Counter missing key par 0 deta hai aur most_common/arithmetic deta hai — counting ke liye. defaultdict missing key par factory call karta hai (list/set/int) — grouping ke liye. Dono 'missing key boilerplate' hatate hain, isliye code chhota aur bug-free hota hai.
interview.tip: Subclass hone ka matlab: ye normal dict ki tarah har jagah chalte hain (isinstance dict True).

interview.q: Dictionary order par bharosa kar sakte ho?
interview.a: Python 3.7+ me insertion order language guarantee hai (CPython 3.6 me implementation detail thi), isliye dict iteration deterministic hai aur JSON output stable rehta hai. Par ordering ke liye sort par bharosa karo jab business rule ho — order change se output na badle.
interview.tip: Version history ka precision dikhao: 3.6 implementation, 3.7 guarantee.

beginner.q: Dictionary se kisi key ki value safely nikaalo.
beginner.a: get() use karo default ke saath; direct access sirf tab jab key guaranteed ho.
beginner.commonMistake: try/except KeyError se simple get() ko replace karna — dono run karte hain, par get intent saaf karta hai.

beginner.q: Dictionary me naya key add karo aur existing update karo.
beginner.a: Assignment hi upsert hai: d['k'] = v naya key banata hai ya purani value badalta hai.
beginner.code:
marks = {'math': 80}
marks['science'] = 85
marks['math'] = 90
print(marks, len(marks))

beginner.q: Dictionary se key delete karo aur delete ke baad check karo.
beginner.a: pop(key, default) safe delete deta hai; del KeyError raise karta hai agar key na ho.

beginner.q: Dictionary ke saare keys aur values ki list banao.
beginner.a: list(d.keys()) / list(d.values()) ya list(d) — views ko list me convert karta hai.
beginner.code:
stock = {'pen': 12, 'book': 5}
print(list(stock), list(stock.values()))
beginner.explain: keys()/values() view hain — list me convert na karo to print par bhi theek dikhta hai par indexing/slicing nahi milegi.

beginner.q: Dictionary se list of tuples banao aur wapas dictionary.
beginner.a: d.items() tuples deta hai; dict(pairs) wapas dictionary banata hai.

intermediate.q: Text me har word ki frequency nikalo.
intermediate.a: Counter split ke result par — O(n) aur missing-key handling automatic.
intermediate.code:
from collections import Counter

text = 'machine learning is a field of study and machine learning needs data'
freq = Counter(w.lower() for w in text.split())
print(freq.most_common(3))

intermediate.q: Do dictionaries merge karo jisme conflict par second jeete.
intermediate.a: d1 | d2 ya {**d1, **d2} — dono me right side ki value jeet ti hai.

intermediate.q: Dictionary ko value ke hisaab se sort karo.
intermediate.a: sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]) — list of tuples sorted milti hai; dict(sorted(...)) se ordered dict.
intermediate.code:
prices = {'OnePlus': 20000, 'Redmi': 12000, 'Poco': 11500, 'Samsung': 14500}
print(dict(sorted(prices.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])))

intermediate.q: List of tuples ko dictionary me convert karo (duplicate keys ke saath).
intermediate.a: Loop me assign karo — duplicate key par last value jeet ti hai; pehla rakhna ho to setdefault use karo.
intermediate.explain: setdefault(key, default) sirf tab set karta hai jab key na ho — 'first wins' semantics ke liye.

intermediate.q: Dictionary ki values ka sum nikalo (mixed nested values ko ignore karke).
intermediate.a: Values par filter lagao: sirf int/float (aur bool nahi) jodo.
intermediate.commonMistake: isinstance(v, bool) ko int me count karna — True == 1 hota hai, isliye bool alag se exclude karna padta hai.

advanced.q: Dictionary ko invert karo (values ko keys banao) aur duplicate values ko group karo.
advanced.a: defaultdict(list) me value → [keys] mapping banao — warna duplicate values ek doosre ko overwrite kar deti hain.
advanced.tip: Simple inversion {v: k for k, v in d.items()} duplicate values par data loss karta hai — yehi follow-up question hota hai.

advanced.q: Nested dictionary se deep value nikaalo missing path par safe rehte hue.
advanced.a: Loop me har level par isinstance + membership check; fail hone par default return.

advanced.q: Nested dictionary ko flatten karo (dot-path keys ke saath).
advanced.a: Recursion ya explicit stack: dict mile to path badha kar andar jao, warna leaf set karo.
advanced.explain: out parameter default None rakha gaya hai (mutable default argument trap se bachne ke liye) — ye classic Python gotcha hai.

advanced.q: Records ko ek key par group karo aur per-group count do.
advanced.a: defaultdict(list) ya single pass me Counter for counts (memory kam).
advanced.code:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

rows = [{'team': 'nlp', 'name': 'a'}, {'team': 'cv', 'name': 'b'}, {'team': 'nlp', 'name': 'c'}]
groups = defaultdict(list)
for r in rows:
    groups[r['team']].append(r['name'])
print(dict(groups))
print(Counter(r['team'] for r in rows))

advanced.q: Dictionary ki keys ko ek naye key par rename karo bina value kho ke.
advanced.a: pop(old, sentinel) se value nikaalo aur naye key par daalo; sentinel se pata chalta hai key thi ya nahi.
advanced.explain: Sentinel object isliye ki None bhi valid value ho sakti hai — 'key thi par value None thi' case safe rahe.

interview.q: Interview: 1 crore log lines me se top-10 error codes nikalo (memory limited).
interview.a: Streaming loop + Counter (ya dict) — per line code nikaalo aur count badhao. Memory unique codes ke proportional hai, total lines ke nahi. Agar unique keys bahut zyada hon to Count-Min Sketch/heavy-hitters approach bolna depth dikhata hai.
interview.code:
from collections import Counter

lines = ['E500 db timeout', 'E500 db timeout', 'E404 not found', 'E500 pool exhausted']
counts = Counter(line.split()[0] for line in lines)
print(counts.most_common(2))
interview.tip: 'Unique keys ki ginti' par memory depend karti hai — ye clarification interviewer ko impress karta hai.

interview.q: Interview: ek dictionary me duplicate keys aa jayein to kaunsa rakhoge?
interview.a: Ye data semantics ka decision hai: 'last write wins' (loop assignment, reverse iteration) ya 'first wins' (setdefault) ya 'collect all' (defaultdict(list)). Interview me pehle clarify karo, phir implementation bolna — warna galat assumption par poora answer galat ho jata hai.
interview.tip: Literal me duplicate key likhna silently last-wins karta hai — ye example bolo.

interview.q: Interview: do dictionaries ka difference nikalo (keys jo pehli me hain par doosri me nahi).
interview.a: d1.keys() - d2.keys() set difference O(n) hai; values bhi compare karni hon to items() par comprehension. Symmetric difference ke liye ^ use karo.
interview.tip: Keys par set operations free milti hain kyunki views set-like hain — ye Python ka strong point hai.

interview.q: Interview: cache/rate-limit ke liye dictionary kaise use karoge?
interview.a: Key → value mapping with TTL timestamp: cache[key] = {'value': v, 'expires': now + ttl}; read par expiry check karke pop. Bounded size ke liye OrderedDict/dict + popitem(last=False) se LRU banao, ya simply size check karke oldest remove karo.
interview.tip: Thread safety ka point add karo — plain dict concurrent writes par safe nahi hota.

realworld.q: API response ko database row jaisa record banao aur missing fields default kar do.
realworld.a: Required keys ke liye direct access, optional ke liye get — aur defaults ek schema dict me rakho.

realworld.q: Layered configuration banao (defaults < file < env).
realworld.a: Merge precedence ke saath: defaults | file_config | env_overrides — rightmost jeetta hai.

realworld.q: CSV rows ko category-wise summarize karo (count, total, average).
realworld.a: defaultdict me rows collect karo, phir per-group aggregates nikalo — ek pass grouping.
realworld.code:
from collections import defaultdict

rows = [('nlp', 120), ('cv', 80), ('nlp', 90), ('cv', 100)]
groups = defaultdict(list)
for cat, val in rows:
    groups[cat].append(val)
summary = {cat: {'n': len(v), 'total': sum(v), 'avg': round(sum(v) / len(v), 1)} for cat, v in groups.items()}
print(summary)

realworld.q: User input/event data me PII keys hata kar clean payload banao (allowlist approach).
realworld.a: Allowlist se nayi dict banao — blacklist/denylist se safer kyunki naye sensitive fields automatically block ho jate hain.
realworld.tip: Allowlist vs blacklist ka reasoning interview me strong signal hai.

coding.question: Text me har word ki frequency nikalo aur top-3 dikhao.
coding.build: Function top_words(text, n) -> [(word, count)] frequency order me.
coding.input: 'data is data science and data is powerful'
coding.hint: Counter(text.split()) aur most_common(n); case normalize karna na bhoolo.
coding.explanation: Counter missing keys par 0 deta hai, isliye counting loop ki zaroorat nahi. Generator expression se lower-case conversion ek hi pass me hoti hai.
coding.better: Bahut bade corpus me heapq.nlargest(n, counts.items(), key=...) se poora sort avoid karte hain.
coding.followUp: Agar 10 lakh unique words hon to memory kaise bachaoge? (heavy hitters / sampling)

coding.question: Dictionary me missing keys ko default value se bharo.
coding.build: Function with_defaults(d, schema) -> dict, sab keys guaranteed.
coding.hint: Schema ke keys par iterate karo aur get(default) se value lo.
coding.explanation: Schema hi single source of truth ban jati hai — API/DB records ko normalize karne ka yahi pattern hai. Extra keys ignore hote hain (allowlist behaviour).
coding.better: Validation ke saath chahiye to same loop me type check add karo, ya dataclasses/Pydantic jaisa schema object banao.
coding.followUp: Extra keys ko bhi rakhna ho to code kaise badalega?

coding.question: Invert a dictionary so values become keys, grouping duplicates.
coding.build: Function invert_grouped(d) -> dict value -> sorted list of keys.
coding.hint: defaultdict(list); phir lists sort karo taki output deterministic rahe.
coding.explanation: Simple inversion duplicate values par data loss karta hai; defaultdict grouping se sab keys bachti hain. Sorting se output deterministic hota hai — tests stable rahte hain.
coding.time: O(n log n) worst case (sorting groups)
coding.better: Order matter na kare to group sort chhod do — O(n) ho jata hai.
coding.followUp: Values unhashable hon (list) to kaise invert karoge?

coding.question: Two-level nested dictionary ko dot-path keys me flatten karo.
coding.build: Function flatten(data, prefix='') -> {'a.b.c': value} mapping.
coding.hint: Recursion with prefix string; mutable default argument se bacho.
coding.concept: Recursion over dicts + defensive default handling
coding.explanation: out=None default isliye ki mutable default (out={}) sab calls me share ho jata — classic Python trap. isinstance check recursion ka base case banata hai. Empty dict par khaali dict return hoti hai, crash nahi.
coding.better: Bahut deep data par explicit stack use karo taki recursion limit na toote.
coding.followUp: Flatten ka ulta (unflatten) kaise likhoge? (path.split('.'))

coding.question: Dictionary ka diff nikalo: added, removed aur changed keys.
coding.build: Function diff(a, b) -> {'added': {...}, 'removed': {...}, 'changed': {...}}.
coding.hint: Set operations on .keys() — donon taraf ka difference aur common keys ka value compare.
coding.concept: Dict views as sets + value comparison
coding.explanation: keys() views set-like hain, isliye - aur & operators bina list conversion ke chalte hain — O(n) total. Changed me tuple (old, new) return karte hain taki direction clear rahe.
coding.better: Config drift detection me nested diff chahiye to recurse karo jab dono values dict hon.
coding.followUp: Ye diff deployment/rollback me kaise use hoga?

coding.question: Bounded LRU cache dictionary se implement karo (capacity ke saath).
coding.build: Class LRUCache(capacity) with get(key) and put(key, value) in O(1).
coding.input: capacity=2, put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), put(3,3) → 2 evicted
coding.hint: OrderedDict ya plain dict (insertion ordered) + move_to_end / pop + re-insert.
coding.explanation: Python 3.7+ me dict insertion-ordered hai, isliye OrderedDict.move_to_end se 'recently used' order maintain karna aasan hai: access par key ko end me le jao aur capacity cross hone par sabse purani (first) key hata do. Dono operations O(1).
coding.better: Production me functools.lru_cache use karo (C implementation, thread-safe lock ke saath); interview me implementation likhwana common hai.
coding.followUp: TTL ke saath LRU kaise combine karoge, aur expiry check lazy kyun rakhte hain?

coding.question: Nested records ko ek path se safely update karo (immutable style).
coding.build: Function set_path(data, path, value) -> nayi dict (original unchanged).
coding.hint: Recursion me dict copy karo; list me nahi badalna hai.
coding.explanation: Har level par {**data, key: ...} se nayi dict banti hai, isliye original structure untouched rehta hai — ye functional-update style hai (Redux/immutable config libraries isi tarah kaam karti hain). Missing intermediate keys automatically banti hain.
coding.better: Deep structures par struct copy path ko cache karo; ya flat dot-path storage rakho aur ek hi dict copy karo.
coding.followUp: Kya isse concurrent readers ke liye safe config update milta hai?

debugging.broken:
user = {'name': 'Ali'}
print(user['city'])
debugging.error: KeyError: 'city'
debugging.why: Direct [] access missing key par KeyError raise karta hai — ye fail-fast behaviour hai, None return karne se bug chhup jate.
debugging.fix: Optional key ke liye get(key, default) use karo; ya key ka hona contract hai to explicit check + clear error do.
debugging.lesson: Default kab dena hai aur crash kab karna hai — ye code ki intent decide karti hai, habit nahi.

debugging.broken:
matrix = {}
key = [1, 2]
matrix[key] = 'value'
print(matrix)
debugging.error: TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'
debugging.why: Dictionary key ko hashable hona chahiye. List mutable hai isliye hash nahi hoti — warna key badalne se lookup table corrupt ho jati.
debugging.fix: List ki jagah tuple use karo (immutable), ya key string me convert karo.
debugging.correct:
matrix = {}
matrix[(1, 2)] = 'value'
matrix['1,2'] = 'string-key value'
print(matrix)
debugging.lesson: "Unhashable" ka matlab hai mutable type key ki tarah use ho raha hai — tuple/str/frozenset keys safe hain.

debugging.error: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
debugging.why: Iterator table ke size par chalta hai; iteration ke beech key delete karne se size badal jata hai, isliye Python turant error deta hai (silently corrupt karne ki jagah).
debugging.fix: Pehle keys ki list banao (list(counts)) ya nayi dict comprehension se rebuild karo.
debugging.lesson: Mutate-while-iterate har collection me khatarnak hai; dict me Python error deta hai jabki list me silently skip hota hai.

debugging.error: Logic error: inclusive/eksclusive threshold galat — 100 wala item bhi aa gaya
debugging.why: Requirement 'target se upar' thi (strictly above), par code me >= likha gaya. Koi exception nahi aata — output galat hota hai, isliye ye silent logic bug hai.
debugging.fix: Boundary ki language check karo: 'se upar' = >, 'se upar ya barabar' = >=. Requirement ke words se operator likho.
debugging.lesson: Threshold bugs silently galat report dete hain; boundary values (99/100/101) ke saath test likhna hi inhe pakadta hai.
debugging.brokenOutput:
above target: pen
above target: bag

debugging.error: Logic error: 'a' ki pehli value gum ho gayi (last-write-wins chup-chaap hua)
debugging.why: Duplicate keys hone par assignment purani value ko overwrite kar deta hai — koi error nahi aata, data loss silent hota hai. 'Pehli value valid hai' wale business rule me ye galat hai.
debugging.fix: Semantics pehle decide karo: first-wins ke liye setdefault, all-values ke liye defaultdict(list), ya duplicate detect karke report karo.
debugging.correct:
from collections import defaultdict

rows = [('a', 1), ('b', 2), ('a', 3)]
first_wins, all_values = {}, defaultdict(list)
for key, value in rows:
    first_wins.setdefault(key, value)
    all_values[key].append(value)
print(first_wins)
print(dict(all_values))
print(sorted(set(k for k, _ in rows) - set(first_wins.keys())))
debugging.lesson: Duplicate keys ka handling business rule hai — code likhne se pehle 'first, last, ya sab' decide karo aur uske hisaab se structure chuno.

challenges.prompt: Ek dictionary se sirf woh entries print karo jinki value 100 se badi hai — comprehension se.
challenges.hint: {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v > 100}
challenges.deliverable: Ek line ka snippet.

challenges.prompt: Word frequency counter banao jo stop words hata kar top-5 de aur total unique words count kare.
challenges.hint: Counter + stop-word set; unique count len(freq) se.
challenges.deliverable: Function + sample output.

challenges.prompt: Do nested configs ka deep diff tool banao (added/removed/changed dot-paths ke saath).
challenges.hint: flatten() se dot-path dict banao, phir keys par set operations.
challenges.deliverable: Script + nested example output.

challenges.prompt: Interview: 1 crore events me per-user last-seen timestamp nikaalo, memory limit ke saath.
challenges.hint: Streaming loop + dict user → timestamp; memory unique users par depend karti hai.
challenges.deliverable: Design answer + working snippet + memory reasoning.

challenges.prompt: Ek mini 'config manager' banao jo defaults, JSON file aur environment se layered config build kare aur validate kare.

projects.name: Grade Calculator (Version 1)
projects.problem: Learners ko dictionary ka pehla practical use chahiye: subject → marks ka record, aur usse aggregate report.
projects.objective: Ek program jo subjects ke marks dictionary se total, average, grade aur topper subject nikaale.
projects.structure:
grade_calculator/
└── grades.py        # marks + report
steps: Marks ko dict me store karo (subject → score).
total/average nikalo aur grade function se letter grade do.
Topper subject max(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]) se nikaalo.
Khali dict aur single subject cases test karo.
projects.output:
total=275 avg=91.7 grade=A
best: english (95) � weakest: science (88)
Koi marks nahi diye gaye.
projects.explanation: marks.values() par sum chalana ek line me total deta hai bina loop ke. max/min me key function items() tuple ka second element (score) leta hai, isliye subject + score dono mil jate hain — sirf score nahi, jo debugging me helpful hai. Khaali dict ka guard division-by-zero se bachata hai.
projects.testing: Khali dict, ek subject, aur equal marks (tie par min/max deterministic hona chahiye) — teenon test karo.
projects.errors: Non-numeric marks par sum() TypeError dega; report me type check add karna next version ka task rakho.
improvements: Marks ko file ya input se lo aur validation add karo (0–100 range)
Subject weights (credits) support karo, weighted average se
Report ko CSV/JSON export karo

argparse CLI (--file, --format json)
pytest tests covering grade boundaries (89.9 vs 90)
Logging + error handling for corrupt files

interview.q: Topper nikalne ke liye max(marks, key=marks.get) se kya farq padta hai?
interview.a: max(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]) subject aur score dono deta hai, jabki max(d, key=d.get) sirf key (subject) deta hai aur value dobara lookup karni padti hai. Dono O(n) hain.

interview.q: Grade boundaries ko function me kyun rakha?
interview.a: Boundaries ek jagah collect rehti hain, isliye rule change par ek hi jagah edit karna padta hai — aur boundary tests (89.9 vs 90) likhna aasan hota hai.

interview.q: Empty dictionary par kya hota hai?
interview.a: Early return se friendly message milta hai; warna average me ZeroDivisionError aata.

projects.name: Log Analyzer (Version 2)
projects.problem: Version 1 ek record ka report deta hai. Real logs me hazaaron lines hoti hain aur unse per-level counts, top error codes aur slowest endpoints nikalne padte hain — dict-based aggregation ka asli use case.
projects.objective: Ek analyzer banao jo log lines parse kare, level-wise aur endpoint-wise group kare, error rates nikale aur invalid lines report kare.
features: Log line parsing with tolerance for malformed lines
Reusable module split: parse vs aggregate
projects.structure:
log_analyzer/
├── parser.py      # line → record
├── aggregate.py   # counts, latency stats
└── main.py        # sample run
steps: parse_line() likho jo 'ts LEVEL endpoint ms' se dict banaye; invalid par None.
aggregate me per-level Counter aur per-endpoint latency list banao.
Invalid lines ko line number ke saath collect karo.
main.py se sample logs chalao aur summary print karo.
projects.explanation: parse_line ek hi jagah validation karta hai aur None deta hai (silent skip nahi, caller decide karta hai) — isliye malformed lines line numbers ke saath report hoti hain. defaultdict(list) se endpoint grouping ke liye 'if key not in' boilerplate nahi likhna padta. Endpoint stats ek comprehension me banti hain (count/avg/max), isliye ek hi pass me sab aggregates mil jate hain. Empty input par khali structures return hote hain, crash nahi.
projects.testing: Malformed line, non-numeric latency, unknown level, empty input, aur single-endpoint input ke tests likho. avg rounding ka bhi test rakho.
projects.errors: float conversion ValueError pakadta hai; extra/missing columns par None; unknown level reject hota hai — teenon deliberate hain aur bad-lines list me report hote hain.
improvements: Streaming file reader (line by line) add karo, poori file memory me na lo
Percentiles (p95/p99) calculate karo sorted latency se
JSON export + alerting threshold (error rate > X%) add karo
advanced: Time-bucketed aggregation (per-minute rates) for dashboards
Config-driven parsing (regex/format string) taki dusre log formats support hon
Structured logging + CI with pytest coverage gate
CLI tool (argparse) with --file, --top, --json flags
projects.realWorld: API observability: latency percentiles aur error-rate by endpoint wahi metrics hain jo production dashboards/on-call playbooks me use hote hain.

interview.q: Poora file memory me load karna kyun problem hai?
interview.a: Production logs GB me hote hain — isliye line-by-line streaming chahiye; aggregation state (counts, sums, max) chhota hota hai, raw lines nahi rakhni padti.

interview.q: Average latency enough kyun nahi hai?
interview.a: Average outliers se distort hota hai; p95/p99 tail latency batate hain jo users ko actually feel hoti hai — isliye percentiles 'improvements' me hain.

interview.q: Malformed lines handle karne ka sahi tarika kya hai?
interview.a: Reject karo par count/record karo (line number ke saath) — silently ignore karna data quality issue chhupata hai, aur crash karna ek kharab line se poora analysis rok deta hai.

projects.resume: Built a streaming log analyzer that groups by level and endpoint, reports latency stats and error frequency, and surfaces malformed lines with line numbers.

projects.name: JSON-Backed Config Service (Version 4)
projects.problem: Application config production me layered hoti hai aur galti se corrupt likhne par service down ho jati hai. Dictionary-based config ko deep-merge, validate, version aur audit karna padta hai.
projects.objective: Ek config service banao jo defaults + file + env se layered config build kare, deep merge kare, schema validate kare, atomic JSON persist kare aur drift diff report kare.
features: Layered merge with explicit precedence (defaults < file < env)
Deep merge for nested dicts (shallow replace nahi)
Schema validation with clear dotted-path errors
projects.structure:
config_service/
├── merge.py      # deep_merge + flatten/diff
├── schema.py     # validation rules
├── store.py      # atomic save/load
└── main.py       # demonstration run
steps: deep_merge(base, override) recursive likho (dict me recurse, warna override jeete).
flatten() aur diff() add karo dot-path comparison ke liye.
schema validate likho jo missing/typed fields par dotted path error de.
store save/load atomic banao; main me layering + drift diff dikhao.
projects.explanation: deep_merge recursion sirf tab recurse karta hai jab dono taraf dict ho — warna override replace karta hai, isliye nested partial overrides sahi kaam karte hain (shallow {**a, **b} nested keys ko poora replace kar deta hai). flatten + diff dot-path comparison dete hain, jisse config drift log/PR me readable hota hai. validate dotted paths par type report karta hai — errors machine-readable hain. mask allowlist-style secret detection se logging-safe snapshot deta hai. save atomic hai (temp + replace) aur load corrupt JSON par backup rakh kar empty deta hai, isliye ek kharab file service ko down nahi karti.
projects.testing: deep_merge ke nested override cases, diff ka changed/added/removed, validation ke missing + wrong-type paths, masking (nested secret), aur corrupt file recovery — sab pytest me cover karo.
projects.errors: JsonDecodeError recovery (backup + empty), validation problems list (caller decide kare fail karna hai ya warning), aur atomic write failures clean-up ke saath — sab explicit hain.
improvements: Environment variable expansion inside config values (${VAR})
Schema version field + migration function for old configs
Watch/reload on file change with debounce
advanced: Secrets via secret manager/encrypted file, not plain JSON
Structured audit log of config changes (who/when/diff)
pytest + CI, plus property-based tests for deep_merge idempotency
Dockerised service with README (config precedence, failure playbook)
projects.realWorld: Application config layering (defaults → file → env → secrets), feature-flag management aur deployment drift detection — yehi design har production service me hota hai.

interview.q: Shallow merge se nested config kaise toot jati hai?
interview.a: Shallow merge {**a, **b} me nested dict poora replace hoti hai, isliye b me sirf ek key dena bhi a ke baaki keys hata deta hai. Deep merge se sirf wahi keys override hoti hain jo caller ne di.

interview.q: Config ko validate kyu karna zaroori hai, defaults kaafi nahi?
interview.a: Env/file se aaya data untrusted hai: 'port': '5432' (string) ya missing key runtime crash karta hai. Startup par validate karke fail karna cheap hai, baad me request ke beech crash karna mehnga.

interview.q: Logging ke liye masking kaise karo aur kyun?
interview.a: Keys ke naam par allowlist/denylist match se '***' lagao — plaintext secrets logs me chale jayein to compliance breach hota hai aur log aggregation systems unhe permanently store kar lete hain.

interview.q: Atomic write aur reload race ka solution kya hai?
interview.a: os.replace atomic hai isliye readers ko poora file dikhta hai; reader ko bhi ek hi baar load karke immutable object use karna chahiye. Multi-process consistency chahiye to file lock ya central config service (etcd/Consul) le lo.

projects.resume: Engineered a layered configuration service in Python with recursive deep merge, dotted-path validation and diffing, secret masking and atomic JSON persistence with corrupt-file recovery.
readme: Precedence order diagram (defaults → file → env)
Validation error examples
Failure semantics: corrupt file recovery + atomic write
Roadmap: env expansion, schema migration, secret store

understanding: Grade Calculator me items() par max/min kyun use kiya, keys ya values par kyun nahi?
Log analyzer me defaultdict(list) ne kaunsa boilerplate bachaya?
Config service me deep merge shallow merge se kaise alag hai?
Masking ke liye allowlist approach kyun safer hai?
coding: Grade calculator me subject-wise rank add karo.
Log analyzer me p95 latency calculate karo.
Config service me ${VAR} environment expansion add karo.
Config diff ko CLI command banao jo do files compare kare.
advanced: Log analyzer ko streaming mode me convert karo (line-by-line file read).
Config validation ko dataclass/Pydantic schema se replace karo aur compare karo.
Bade configs ke liye diff ko path-wise sort karke deterministic output do.
Memory profile karo: 10 lakh log lines par analyzer ka peak memory measure karo.
interview: Is project ko production me kaise scale karoge?
Aggregation ki time complexity kya hai?
Memory usage kaise reduce karoge jab input bahut bada ho?
Konsi error cases abhi handle nahi hoti?
Config service ko API me kaise convert karoge?

interviewTasks.q: Live coding: text me duplicate words nikalo aur unki count report karo.
interviewTasks.a: Counter(words) se counts lo aur {w: n for w, n in counts.items() if n > 1} se filter karo — O(n). Order matter kare to first-seen order preserve karne ke liye dict comprehension ki jagah iteration order use karo.

interviewTasks.q: Interview: kya dictionary ka iteration order deterministic hai? Production me isse kaise use karoge?
interviewTasks.a: Python 3.7+ me insertion order guaranteed hai, isliye JSON/config output deterministic likha ja sakta hai. Par business ordering chahiye to explicit sort karo — order guarantee language ka hai, business rule ka nahi.
interviewTasks.deliverable: Explanation + snippet jisme explicit sort dikhe.

interviewTasks.q: Practical: API payload se PII hata kar logging-safe dict banao.
interviewTasks.a: Allowlist approach: sirf allowed keys copy karo; secrets ke liye masking ('***'). Nested payload me recursive walk karo. Denylist avoid karo kyunki naye sensitive fields silently leak ho jate hain.

interviewTasks.q: Interview: ek dictionary me d1 | d2 vs d1.update(d2) — kya farq hai aur kaunsa kab?
interviewTasks.a: | nayi dict deta hai (originals untouched), update in-place mutate karta hai aur None return karta hai. Functional/immutable flow me |, hot-path me update (allocation bachti hai). Dono me right side ki value jeet ti hai.

interviewTasks.q: Design task: per-user request count rate limiter dictionary se banao (window ke saath).
interviewTasks.a: dict user → deque of timestamps; request par purane timestamps window se bahar hatado, phir len check karo. Memory bounded rakhne ke liye stale keys periodic cleanup se hatao (ya OrderedDict-based LRU).

revision: Dictionary mutable, keys unique aur hashable — insertion order 3.7+ me guaranteed.
d[key] KeyError deta hai (fail fast), get(key, default) safe read; choice intent ke hisaab se.
Iteration me keys/values/items views; size badalna iteration ke dauraan RuntimeError deta hai.
Counter counting ke liye, defaultdict grouping ke liye — missing-key boilerplate dono hatate hain.
Merge: update in-place, {**a, **b} / a | b nayi dict; teenon shallow hain (deep merge recursion chahiye).
0 falsy hai — numeric threshold par truthiness check kabhi mat likho.
Duplicate keys par semantics (first/last/all) pehle decide karo, phir setdefault/defaultdict chuno.

concepts.title: Section overview
concepts.body: OOP 13 (Object Oriented Programming) Level: Advanced Time: ~120 min 19 topics OOP me data (attributes) aur kaam (methods) ko ek saath ek class me bandh dete hain. Bade projects ko organized, reusable aur maintain karne layak banane ka ye best tarika hai. Python ke saare built-in types (str, list, dict) bhi classes hi hain. Class ek ghar ka naksha (blueprint) hai, object uska asli ghar. Ek naksha se kai ghar ban sakte hain, har ghar ka apna rang, apna saman.

concepts.title: class & object
concepts.body: Class ek blueprint hai. Object uska real instance hai. Naam ka pehla letter capital rakhte hain
concepts.code:
class Car:
    pass

my_car = Car()
other = Car()           # alag objects

print(type(my_car))
print(my_car is other)

concepts.title: __init__()
concepts.body: Constructor method. Object banate hi apne aap call hota hai. self us object ko refer karta hai jo abhi ban raha hai. 1 Car("Tesla") likhte hi Python ek khaali object banata hai. 2 __init__ automatically call hota hai, self = naya object, brand = "Tesla". 3 self.brand = brand se value object ke andar save hoti hai.
concepts.tip: Method ke pehle parameter me self likhna mat bhoolo, warna TypeError aayega.

concepts.title: instance method
concepts.body: Class ke andar normal function jo object ke apne data par kaam karta hai. Pehla parameter hamesha self.

concepts.title: class variable
concepts.body: Ye variable sabhi objects ke beech shared hota hai. Instance variable (self.x) har object ka apna hota hai.
concepts.code:
class Car:
    wheels = 4                  # class variable

    def __init__(self, brand):
        self.brand = brand      # instance variable

c1 = Car("Tesla")
c2 = Car("BMW")
print(c1.wheels, c2.wheels)
Car.wheels = 6                  # sabke liye badla
print(c1.wheels, c2.wheels)

concepts.title: class method
concepts.body: @classmethod se decorate hota hai. Pehla parameter cls (class), object nahi. Alternative constructors me kaam aata hai.

concepts.title: static method
concepts.body: @staticmethod ko na self chahiye na cls. Ye class ke andar rakha ek normal utility function hai.
concepts.tip: Instance method = object data (self). Class method = class data (cls). Static method = kisi data ki zarurat nahi.

concepts.title: inheritance
concepts.body: Child class parent ki properties aur methods reuse kar leti hai. Syntax: class Child(Parent).

guide.what: Class ek blueprint hai (state + behaviour), aur object uska instance. Per-object data instance attributes me rehta hai, behaviour methods me — aur subclass parent ka code super() se reuse karta hai.
guide.why: OOP se related data aur logic ek jagah rehta hai: interface saaf, dependencies inject ho sakti hain, aur testing aasan hoti hai. Bade codebases me yahi Wrapper/Client/Fixture patterns ka base hai.
guide.whereUsed: Model wrappers (predict + counters), API clients (retry/timeout), dataclasses for records, test fixtures aur dependency injection.
guide.howItWorks: class statement ek type object banata hai. Instance banate waqt __init__ chalta hai aur self par attributes set hote hain; attribute lookup instance dict → class dict → base classes (MRO) ke order me hota hai. Method call par self automatically bind hota hai, isliye self explicitly pass nahi karte.

explain: __init__ instance banate hi chalta hai, aur self.name per-object state hai (do objects ka naam alag ho sakta hai).
predict har call par self.calls badhata hai — behaviour aur state ek hi object me band rehte hain.
type(m).__name__ class ka naam deta hai aur isinstance() inheritance chain check karta hai.
Subclass ne kind override kiya, aur super() parent ka describe() chalata hai — reuse without copy-paste.
c.describe() me 'cached -> ' prefix aur parent ka format dono milte hain (override + super ka combo).
Attribute lookup instance dict → class → base chalta hai, isliye class variable default value ki tarah kaam karti hai.
@dataclass __init__, __repr__ aur __eq__ generate karta hai — value objects ka boilerplate hat jata hai.
@property se computed attribute milta hai jo method ki tarah call nahi hota (r1.label, r1.label() nahi).
default_factory har object ko alag list deta hai, isliye r1.tags khaali rehta hai — mutable default ka classic bug nahi hota.

howToCode.detail: Attributes list karo (kya state hai), uske baad methods (kaunse operations hai). Ek class ki ek responsibility rakho.
Client/session/config ko __init__ ka argument banao, class ke andar hardcode na karo — testing aur reuse dono aasan ho jaate hain.
Sirf 'is-a' relation me extend karo; warna doosra object attribute ki tarah rakho (has-a).
Debug me print(object) se state dikhni chahiye; value-equality chahiye to __eq__ bhi add karo.

commonMistakes: Mutable default (def f(x, acc=[]) ya class attribute tags=[]) — sab objects ek hi object share karte hain.
Method definition me self bhool jana — TypeError: takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given.
Parent ka __init__ call na karna — base state setup hi nahi hota.
Teen se zyada level deep inheritance — behaviour trace karna mushkil ho jata hai (composition behtar hai).
bestPractices: Value objects ke liye @dataclass use karo (__init__/__eq__/__repr__ free milte hain).
Sirf public API expose karo; internal helpers par _ prefix lagao.
Type hints likho — mypy integration bugs ko runtime se pehle pakadta hai.
Constructor me I/O na karo (network/disk) — object sasta banao, setup ke liye alag method rakho.

guide.howItWorks: Call par Python arguments ko parameters se bind karta hai (positional → keyword → default). Har call naya local scope banati hai. Default values function definition ke waqt sirf ek baar evaluate hoti hain — isliye mutable default do calls ke beech state leak karta hai.

logic.text: `def f(x, acc=[]): acc.append(x); return acc` ko do baar call karo — `f(1)` phir `f(2)` — second call ka return value kya hoga?
logic.answer: `[1, 2]` — default argument ek hi list object function definition par banti hai aur har call me reuse hoti hai. Isliye pehli call ka effect doosri call me dikhta hai; `None` sentinel + `bucket = [] if bucket is None else bucket` se fix hota hai.

logic.text: `def add(a, b=10): return a + b` par `add(5)` aur `add(5, 1)` — dono calls me `a`, `b` aur return value likho.
logic.answer: `add(5)` → a = 5, b = 10 (default laga), return 15. `add(5, 1)` → a = 5, b = 1 (default override hua), return 6. Keyword form `add(a=5, b=1)` bhi same deta hai — positional pehle bind hota hai, default tab lagta hai jab argument missing ho.

logic.text: Function expected value ki jagah `None` return kar raha hai — pehla suspect kya hai?
logic.answer: Koi code path `return` ke bina khatam ho raha hai (silent fall-through) — Python har function se implicitly `None` return karta hai. Har branch ka return check karo, aur `-> int` type hint + mypy se ye statically pakdo.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case is function ko todta hai: `def avg(nums): return sum(nums) / len(nums)`?
logic.answer: Khaali list — `sum([])` 0 deta hai par `len([])` 0 hai, isliye `ZeroDivisionError`. Guard lagao: `if not nums: return None` (ya 0.0), aur contract document karo taaki caller `None` handle kare. Ek aur edge: `None` values wali list (`TypeError`).

logic.text: Validation function ke andar ho ya caller par?
logic.answer: System boundary par validate karo (input function me aate hi, ek hi jagah), phir andar ke reusable helpers bharosa karein. Isse har internal call ke liye duplicate checks nahi likhne padte, aur error message bhi boundary par hi achha likha ja sakta hai.

logic.text: Reusable function likhne me pehle kya optimize karoge: kam lines, readability, ya testability?
logic.answer: Readability + testability pehle — single-purpose chhota function likho jo alag se test ho sake; premature generalisation (har jagah `**kwargs`, flexible flags) se bacho. Performance sirf measurement ke baad tune karo, kyunki read karna hi sabse zyada karna padta hai.

def square_sum(nums): return sum(x*x for x in nums) Reason: Generator expression avoids building a second list. O(n) time, O(1) extra space (excluding result object). Complexity: O(n) / O(1)

concepts.title: Exceptions, Files & Modules
concepts.body: Exception ek error ka structured object hai jo normal flow ko rokta hai; file I/O aur module imports ke saath mil kar yehi production code ka failure-handling base banate hain.
concepts.tip: Interview me ye framework do: 'transient errors par retry with backoff, permanent errors par fail fast with actionable message, aur silent failure kabhi nahi'.

guide.what: Exception ek error ka structured object hai jo normal flow ko rokta hai; file I/O aur module imports ke saath mil kar yehi production code ka failure-handling base banate hain.
guide.why: Production me cheezein fail hoti hain: file missing, API timeout, JSON kharab. try/except/finally, context managers aur import structure ke bina system silently galat ya crash karta hai.
guide.whereUsed: File/CSV reading, API retry, config loading, resource cleanup, aur library code me custom errors.
prereqs: Classes (exception class bhi ek class hai)
guide.howItWorks: raise exception ko upar propagation ke liye bhejta hai; try block ka exception matching except clause me pakda jata hai (specific se general order me). finally hamesha chalta hai, aur 'with' statement context manager ke __exit__ par cleanup karta hai — error aaye ya na aaye.

explain: Sirf specific exception (JSONDecodeError) pakdi gayi — bare except sab bugs chhupa deta hai.
except block ek safe default (khaali dict) set karta hai, isliye aage code crash nahi hota.
json.dumps() me separators default hote hain; output deterministic rehta hai, isliye usse test me compare kar sakte ho.

examples.code:
import tempfile, os

path = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "aiml-guide.txt")
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("line1\nline2\n")
with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:

except FileNotFoundError as e:

explain: with open(...) file ko guarantee se close karta hai — exception aaye to bhi __exit__ chalta hai.
encoding='utf-8' explicitly dena zaroori hai warna platform default (Windows cp1252) pe data kharab ho sakta hai.
FileNotFoundError me .filename attribute hota hai, isliye error message actionable banaya jaa sakta hai.
Custom exception class (Exception se derived) library ka error contract ban jati hai — caller specific naam se pakad sakta hai.
fail-fast pattern: pehle sab required keys validate hoti hain, phir kaam shuru — aadha-loaded config se bachav.
Exception ka message actionable rakho (kaunsi key missing) — debugging time bachta hai.

howToCode.detail: Kaunsi cheez fail ho sakti hai: file missing, network timeout, kharab JSON, permission? Har ek ka behaviour decide karo (retry, default, ya raise).
except ValueError as e likho, bare except nahi — warna KeyboardInterrupt aur programming bugs bhi chhup jaate hain.
open(), lock, DB session — sab context manager se, taaki error par bhi cleanup ho.

howToCode.detail: Library code me print error message chhupa deta hai; raise karne se caller decide karta hai. Custom exception se contract saaf rakho.

commonMistakes: Bare `except:` — KeyboardInterrupt/system exit bhi pakad leta hai aur asli bug chhup jata hai.
Exception ko chup-chaap pass karna — silent failure debug karna sabse mushkil hota hai.
open() ke saath with use na karna — file handle leak ho jata hai.
encoding specify na karna — cross-platform par data corrupt ho sakta hai.
Error message me sensitive value (API key) print kar dena.
bestPractices: Fail fast: input boundary par validate karo aur clear error message do.
Error handling aur business logic alag rakho (wrapper/decorator), taaki happy path readable rahe.
Retry sirf transient errors par (timeout/5xx) karo; ValueError par retry bekaar hai.
finally ya with se cleanup guarantee karo; logs me kaunsi layer fail hui wo likho.
guide.realWorld: CSV/JSON ingestion me bad row skip karna, API call ke around retry with backoff, aur config validation at startup — teeno production ke daily kaam hain. Interview me 'silent failure sabse mehnga bug hai' bolkar apna error philosophy bata sakte ho.

interview.q: Custom exception class kab banani chahiye?
interview.a: Jab caller ko specific error pakadna ho (ConfigError vs ValueError) — library ke liye public error contract, aur readable traceback.

interview.q: Bare except kyun khatarnak hai?
interview.a: SystemExit aur KeyboardInterrupt bhi catch ho jaate hain, aur programming bugs chhup jaate hain. Isliye specific exception ya except Exception with re-raise use karo.

interview.a: Logging me levels, timestamps, handlers aur persistent configuration hoti hai. Production debugging ke liye more controllable hai.

interview.a: Domain-specific failure ko clear type dene ke liye, jisse caller specific recovery strategy bana sakta hai.

concepts.title: Core Concepts
concepts.body: Advanced Python ka focus magic ya tricks nahi, balki behavior samajhna hai. Generator memory bachata hai, decorator behavior wrap karta hai, dataclass data-centric classes ko concise banata hai. GENERATOR DECORATOR

concepts.title: Interview Depth
concepts.body: Is page ka goal hai concept ko implementation decision tak le jana. Interviewer ko syntax se zyada reasoning, edge cases aur trade-offs dikhte hain. Har concept par 4 sawal tayyar rakho: WHAT (kya hai aur kab use karoge), WHY (kaunsi problem solve hoti hai), RISK (common bug / failure mode kya hai), TRADE-OFF (simple option aur scalable option me kya difference hai).

concepts.title: Advanced Python & Performance
concepts.body: Generators, comprehensions, itertools, aur profiling — ye topics Python ko bade data par memory-safe aur tez banate hain, aur 'slow script' ko measure karke fix karne ka tareeka dete hain.
concepts.code:
from collections import Counter, deque
from itertools import islice

log = ["GET /a", "POST /a", "GET /a", "GET /b"]
print(Counter(line.split()[0] for line in log))

window = deque(maxlen=2)
for line in log:
    window.append(line)
print(list(window))

print(list(islice((l.upper() for l in log), 2)))
print(dict.fromkeys(log))
concepts.tip: Interview me ye sequence do: 'pehle main measure karta hoon, phir data structure/algorithm badalta hoon, aur aakhir me micro-tuning — aur improvement ka number saath rakhta hoon'.

guide.what: Generators, comprehensions, itertools, aur profiling — ye topics Python ko bade data par memory-safe aur tez banate hain, aur 'slow script' ko measure karke fix karne ka tareeka dete hain.
guide.why: AI/data code me data memory se bada ho jata hai. Lazy iteration aur sahi data structure ka choice, brute-force loop se dash times farq daal deta hai — aur interview me yahi depth poochi jaati hai.
guide.whereUsed: Large file ingestion, token streaming, batching, feature pipelines, aur performance debugging.
guide.howItWorks: Generator function yield par state preserve karta hai, isliye poori list memory me nahi banti (lazy). timeit/time.perf_counter se measure hota hai ki bottleneck CPU hai ya I/O — uske baad algorithm ya data structure badla jaata hai, na ki andaze se micro-optimization ki jaati hai.
guide.syntax:
def stream(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:        # lazily read
            yield line.rstrip()

sum(x for x in nums if x > 0)      # generator expression
from collections import deque, Counter
from itertools import islice, chain, groupby

examples.code:
import sys

def stream(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        total += i
        yield total

gen = stream(5)
print(next(gen), next(gen))
print(list(stream(5)))
print(sys.getsizeof(range(1000000)), sys.getsizeof(list(range(1000))))
explain: yield par function rukta hai aur next() par wahi se chalta hai — poori list banane ki zaroorat nahi.
list(stream(5)) cumulative sums deta hai, isliye generator ko dobara consume kar sakte ho (naya generator ban gaya).
range object ka size almost constant rehta hai jabki list ka size elements ke saath badhta hai — yahi lazy vs eager ka farq hai.

examples.code:
import timeit

setup = "nums = list(range(1000))"
loop = "out = []\nfor x in nums:\n    if x % 2 == 0:\n        out.append(x * 2)"
comp = "out = [x * 2 for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]"

t_loop = timeit.timeit(loop, setup=setup, number=2000)
t_comp = timeit.timeit(comp, setup=setup, number=2000)
print("loop  ", round(t_loop, 4))
print("comp  ", round(t_comp, 4))
print("ratio", round(t_loop / t_comp, 2))
print([x * 2 for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0])
explain: timeit sirf snippet run karta hai (setup separate hai), isliye measurement clean rehta hai.
Comprehension aksar loop se tez hota hai (dedicated bytecode), par farq aksar 1.5-2x hai — algorithmic improvement isse bada hota hai.
Ratio print karna important hai: 'tez lagta hai' ke bajaye measured number bolo.

examples.code:
from collections import Counter, deque
from itertools import islice

log = ["GET /a", "POST /a", "GET /a", "GET /b"]
print(Counter(line.split()[0] for line in log))

window = deque(maxlen=2)
for line in log:
    window.append(line)
print(list(window))

print(list(islice((l.upper() for l in log), 2)))
print(dict.fromkeys(log))
explain: Counter generator bhi accept karta hai — poori intermediate list memory me nahi banti.
deque(maxlen=2) sliding window free me deta hai; purane elements automatically drop ho jaate hain.
islice lazy stream ka pehla N elements leta hai (poori list materialize nahi hoti).
dict.fromkeys order-safe unique list deta hai — set se behtar jab order matter kare.

howToCode.detail: timeit ya time.perf_counter se baseline lo. Bottleneck pata hone se pehle optimization karna sirf complexity badhata hai.
Nested loop ko set/dict lookup, heap, ya sorted two-pointer se badlo — O(n^2) → O(n log n) ka farq micro-optimization se hamesha bada hota hai.
Bade data par generator/generator expression use karo; file line-by-line padho, list me poori mat lao.
sys.getsizeof ya tracemalloc se check karo — aksar speed ke saath memory hi asli problem hoti hai.

commonMistakes: Generator ko do baar consume karna (dusri baar khaali milta hai) — ya toh list bana lo ya naya generator.
Loop ke andar string concatenation (s += x) — O(n^2); list + join use karo.
Loop ke andar list membership check (x in big_list) — set/dict use karo.
Bina measure kiye andaze se 'tez' code likhna.
Bade data par list comprehension ko zaroorat se zyada use karna (memory blow-up).
bestPractices: Function ko lazy banao: input iterable lo, iterable lauto (poori list nahi).
Hot path me local variable lookup, built-ins (sum, min, max, Counter) aur C-implemented modules use karo.
Batching karo (chunks of N) jab network/DB calls ho — per-row call sabse mehnga pattern hai.
Optimization ko test se lock karo: same output + measured improvement, warna regression chup-chaap aa jaati hai.
guide.realWorld: 10 lakh rows wali CSV ko line-by-line stream karna, inference ko batch me chalana, aur sliding-window metrics (p95 over last 100 requests) — teeno production me isi chapter ke tools se likhe jaate hain.

practice.text: Ek generator likho jo file ki lines ko lazily yield kare aur blank lines skip kare.
timeit se list membership vs set membership ka ratio measure karo (1000 elements, 10k lookups).
Ek chunked(iterable, n) generator likho aur batao ki usse API calls kitne kam ho jaate hain.

interview.q: Generator aur list ka farq performance ke liye?
interview.a: Generator lazy hai — ek waqt me ek element memory me, isliye bade data par memory constant rehti hai. List eager hai: sab elements memory me, par multiple passes aur indexing possible.

interview.q: O(n^2) ko kaise theek karoge?
interview.a: Pehle bottleneck identify (nested loop me kya dobara compute ho raha hai), phir hash/set lookup, sorting + two-pointer, ya DP. Claim ke saath complexity bolo.

interview.q: Profiling ke tools?
interview.a: timeit micro-benchmark ke liye, cProfile/time.perf_counter macro hotspots ke liye, aur tracemalloc/psutil memory growth ke liye — measure karke fix karo.

guide.miniChallenge: Ek function likho jo 10 lakh numbers ko single pass me stream kare aur running mean, p95 window aur top-3 frequent simultaneously nikaale (bina poori list banane ke).
guide.debugTask: Ek script 500 MB CSV par MemoryError deta hai kyunki wo read().split('\n') karta hai. Reproduce karo aur streaming fix likho.

Generator expression memory bachata hai

guide.interviewTip: Interview me ye sequence do: 'pehle main measure karta hoon, phir data structure/algorithm badalta hoon, aur aakhir me micro-tuning — aur improvement ka number saath rakhta hoon'.

interview.q: Generator memory kaise bachata hai?
interview.a: Saara result list me materialize karne ke bajay yield se ek item at a time produce karta hai.

interview.q: Decorator ka basic model?
interview.a: Outer function inner wrapper return karta hai; wrapper original function call se pehle/baad behavior add karta hai.

interview.q: Shallow vs deep copy?
interview.a: Shallow copy outer container copy karta hai but nested references share ho sakte hain. Deep copy recursively nested objects clone karta hai.

interview.q: Dataclass ka benefit?
interview.a: Data-holding classes ke boilerplate __init__, repr, comparison etc. reduce karta hai.

interview.q: O(n) se O(log n) better kab?
interview.a: Large input me growth slower hoti hai, but operation aur data structure fit hona zaroori hai. Binary search classic example hai.

interview.q: Profiling kyun?
interview.a: Performance guess se nahi, measurement se optimize karo. Hot path identify karke targeted change karo.

concepts.title: NumPy Arrays, Shape & Broadcasting
concepts.body: NumPy array ek fixed-dtype, contiguous n-dimensional buffer hai. Shape (dimensions ka tuple), dtype aur axis — ye teen cheezein samajh lo to baaki sab numpy predictable lagne lagta hai.
concepts.code:
import numpy as np

rows = np.arange(1_000_000, dtype=np.float64)
squared = rows ** 2
print(squared.dtype, squared.nbytes)
small = squared.astype(np.float32)
print(small.dtype, small.nbytes)
print("approx mean:", float(small.mean()))
print("vectorized, no python loop:", squared[:3].tolist())

guide.what: NumPy array ek fixed-dtype, contiguous n-dimensional buffer hai. Shape (dimensions ka tuple), dtype aur axis — ye teen cheezein samajh lo to baaki sab numpy predictable lagne lagta hai.
guide.why: Array operations C speed me chalti hain aur vectorized code loop se dash guna tez hota hai. Shape aur dtype ka concept ML code me har jagah chahiye — galat shape hi silent bug ka sabse bada source hai.
guide.whereUsed: Feature matrices, embeddings, image tensors, normalization aur batching — numpy se sklearn/torch tak ka data flow.
guide.howItWorks: Array ki shape right se left align hoti hai; har dimension ya equal honi chahiye ya 1 (broadcasting). Aggregation (sum/mean) axis par hoti hai: axis=0 rows ko mila deta hai (column-wise result) aur axis=1 across-row chalta hai — result ki shape ek dimension kam ho jati hai.

zip shorter tuple par ruk jata hai — missing dimension ko 1 maan lena hi asli broadcasting rule hai.
(3, 2) + (4,) fail karta hai kyunki 2 aur 4 na barabar hain na 1 — yahi classic shape error hai.
(3, 1, 4) + (4,) chalta hai: 1 kisi bhi size se align ho jata hai.

logic.text: Shape `(3, 2)` wale array me shape `(2,)` ka vector add karo, phir `(3, 1)` aur `(4,)` wala case sochо — kaun chalta hai aur result shape kya hoga?
logic.answer: `(3,2) + (2,)` → `(3,2)` aur `(3,2) + (3,1)` → `(3,2)` — trailing dimensions align hote hain (compatible jab equal ho ya ek 1 ho). `(3,2) + (4,)` → `ValueError`, kyunki 2 aur 4 na barabar hain na koi 1. `(3,1,4) + (4,)` → `(3,1,4)`.

logic.text: `a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])` par `a.mean(axis=0)` aur `a.mean(axis=1)` ka result likho.
logic.answer: `axis=0` → `[2.0, 3.0]` (column-wise: rows collapse hoti hain) aur `axis=1` → `[1.5, 3.5]` (row-wise: columns collapse hoti hain). Shape bhi badalta hai — `(2,2)` se `(2,)` dono case me, par kis axis ka index bacha wo alag hai.

logic.text: Normalization ke baad array me NaN aa rahe hain — sabse likely kya hai?
logic.answer: Do common wajah: (1) kisi column ka mean 0 hai ya std 0 hai → zero-division se NaN/inf, aur (2) input me pehle se NaN hai jo propagate ho gaya. Check karo `np.isnan(x).sum()` aur per-column std; fix `np.nanmean` + std-zero guard se.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case row-wise normalization ganit ko todta hai?
logic.answer: Constant column (std = 0) → 0 se division. Guard: `if std == 0: std = 1` (ya us column ko normalize na karo), warna poora column NaN ban jata hai aur model usse kuch seekh nahi paata.

logic.text: Shape aur dtype validation kahan karo — data load karte waqt ya function ke andar?
logic.answer: Load boundary par strong validation (expected shape, 2D hona, dtype float, NaN count) aur function ke andar sirf sasta assert (`arr.ndim == 2`). Warna har numpy call par shape check kernal ki speed kha jata hai.

logic.text: Memory-bound pipeline me pehle kya optimize karoge: dtype, copies, ya vectorization?
logic.answer: Pehle unnecessary copies hatao (views chuno, `inplace`/out-parameter use karo), phir dtype downcast (`float64` → `float32` = half memory, aksar same accuracy), phir algorithm/vectorization. Har step ko memory-profiler se measure karo, andaaze se nahi.

concepts.title: Pandas DataFrame Workflow
concepts.body: DataFrame ek labeled 2D table hai (Series = ek column). Real workflow: load → inspect (shape/dtypes/nulls) → clean/transform → groupby/merge → aggregate → report.
concepts.code:
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "region": ["e", "w", "e"]})
right = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1, 2], "amount": [5.0, 7.0, 3.0]})

print(right["id"].duplicated().tolist())
print(len(left), "left rows")

agg = right.groupby("id")["amount"].sum().reset_index()
merged = left.merge(agg, on="id", how="left", validate="one_to_one")
merged["amount"] = merged["amount"].fillna(0.0)
print(len(left), len(merged), round(merged["amount"].sum(), 2))
print(right["amount"].sum())
concepts.tip: Interview me data question ka jawab inspection se shuru karo: 'shape, dtypes aur nulls dekhne ke baad main grain fix karta hoon' — ye structured approach instantly alag dikhta hai.

print(right["amount"].sum())

logic.text: CSV load karne ke baad `df.shape` aur `df.dtypes` — inme se kaun aage ka code todega, aur kyun?
logic.answer: `dtypes` — jo column numbers dikh raha hai par dtype `object` hai, uspar arithmetic silently galat ya `TypeError` deti hai. Shape theek hone par bhi dtype galat ho sakti hai, isliye dono print karo: `print(df.shape); print(df.dtypes)`.

logic.text: `df.groupby('region')['amount'].sum()` kya return karta hai aur uska index kya hota hai?
logic.answer: Ek Series return hoti hai jiska index unique `region` values hain aur values per-region sums. Flat DataFrame chahiye to `reset_index(name='revenue')` lagao; index ko sort/order ke liye bhi use kar sakte ho (`sort_index()`).

logic.text: Merge ke baad row count badh gaya — sabse likely reason?
logic.answer: Join key me duplicates (one-to-many ya many-to-many fan-out): ek left row kai right rows se match kar jati hai. `df[key].duplicated().any()` se check karo, aur duplicated side ko pehle aggregate karke unique karo — phir merge karo.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case `df['amount'].mean()` ko galat jawab dene par majboor karta hai?
logic.answer: NaN values — `mean()` unhe skip karta hai par `count()` me unhe ginnta hi nahi, isliye numerator aur denominator ka basis alag ho jata hai. Khaali DataFrame par `NaN` aata hai. Decide karo: `skipna=False` (honest NaN) ya pehle `dropna`/`fillna`.

logic.text: Data cleaning pipeline me validation kahan lagao?
logic.answer: Har transform ke baad light assertions (shape, null counts, key uniqueness) — ya schema-level check ingestion par. Ye leakage aur silently misaligned columns ko wahi rokta hai jahan wo banta hai, warna bug downstream model metrics me dikhta hai.

logic.text: Bade CSV me pehle kya optimize karoge: dtype downcast, chunks me read, ya column selection?
logic.answer: Pehle sirf zaroori columns padho (`usecols`) — kam I/O aur kam memory dono, phir dtype specify karo (`float32`, `category`), phir chunks + aggregation. Padhna kam karna computing tez karne se hamesha sasta hai.

concepts.title: SQL Joins, Grouping & Window Functions
concepts.body: SQL ek declarative language hai: tum batate ho kya chahiye, planner decide karta hai kaise. Core tools — JOIN (tables jodna), GROUP BY + aggregates (summarise) aur window functions (row ke context ke saath value).
concepts.code:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = con.cursor()
cur.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE sales (region TEXT, month TEXT, revenue INTEGER);
INSERT INTO sales VALUES
 ('east','2026-01',120),('east','2026-02',150),
 ('west','2026-01',90),('west','2026-02',99);
""")
rows = cur.execute("""
SELECT region, month, revenue,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rn,
       revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) AS mom_delta
FROM sales ORDER BY region, month
""").fetchall()
for r in rows:
    print(r)
con.close()
concepts.tip: SQL design question par ye bolo: 'main pehle grain aur NULL behaviour likhta hoon, phir query — aur EXPLAIN se verify karta hoon ki index use ho raha hai'.

guide.what: SQL ek declarative language hai: tum batate ho kya chahiye, planner decide karta hai kaise. Core tools — JOIN (tables jodna), GROUP BY + aggregates (summarise) aur window functions (row ke context ke saath value).
guide.why: Data ka 90% kaam SQL me hi hota hai. NULL semantics, logical execution order aur grain samajh liya to reports bharosemand banti hain; warna silent galat numbers aate hain jinpar business decisions liye jaate hain.
guide.whereUsed: Analytics reports, feature extraction for ML, KPI dashboards, aur application queries (list/filter/paginate).
guide.howItWorks: Logical execution order hai: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. Isliye WHERE aggregate par nahi chal sakta (aggregates GROUP BY ke baad banti hain) aur ORDER BY me SELECT alias use ho sakta hai. NULL ke saath comparison 'unknown' deta hai, isliye IS NULL likhna padta hai.
guide.syntax:
SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM orders
WHERE amount IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY region
HAVING SUM(amount) > 0
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- window: har row ke saath partition ka context
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC)

import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
cur = con.cursor()
cur.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER, name TEXT);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, user_id INTEGER, amount REAL);
INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b'),(3,'c');
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (10,1,5.0),(11,1,7.0),(12,2,3.0),(13,NULL,9.0);
""")
print(cur.execute("""
SELECT u.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total
FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id ORDER BY u.id
""").fetchall())
print("NOT IN with NULL:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders)").fetchone())
print("NOT EXISTS:", cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id)").fetchone())
con.close()

NOT IN with NULL: (0,)

explain: LEFT JOIN har user ko rakhta hai; jis user ke paas order nahi hai uske liye SUM NULL aata hai, isliye COALESCE se 0 dikhate hain.
Subquery me ek NULL hone se NOT IN ka poora comparison unknown ban jata hai — result chup-chaap khaali (0) aa jata hai.
NOT EXISTS wahi sawal sahi jawab deta hai (1 user bilkul bina order) — isliye NULL-safe anti-join NOT EXISTS se likho.

logic.text: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders;` aur `SELECT COUNT(city) FROM orders;` — city me 2 NULL hain, to dono kya return karenge?
logic.answer: `COUNT(*)` sab rows ginta hai (jaise 5), `COUNT(city)` sirf non-NULL values (3). NULL kisi bhi aggregate me count nahi hota — isliye null-heavy column par `COUNT(col)` ko completeness ka proxy samajhna galat hai.

logic.text: SQL ka logical execution order likho (FROM se LIMIT tak) aur batao `WHERE` aggregate par kyun nahi chalta.
logic.answer: `FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT`. `WHERE` GROUP BY se pehle chalta hai, jabki aggregates GROUP BY ke baad banti hain — isliye `WHERE SUM(x) > 10` invalid hai aur wahi shart `HAVING` me likhni padti hai.

logic.text: Query NULL wali rows chup-chaap drop kar rahi hai — kya check karoge?
logic.answer: `col = NULL` kabhi True nahi hota (NULL ke saath comparison unknown deta hai) — `IS NULL` likhna padta hai. Aur `NOT IN (SELECT ...)` me agar subquery me ek bhi NULL aa gaya to poori condition unknown ho jati hai aur result khaali aa jata hai; `NOT EXISTS` safe hai.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case `ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3` wale top-N ko galat banata hai?
logic.answer: Ties — agar 4th aur 3rd row ka revenue barabar hai to LIMIT 3 result ko arbitrary tarike se kaat deta hai (run-to-run badal sakta hai). Fix: `DENSE_RANK()/ROW_NUMBER()` window function se tie-aware cutoff, ya ORDER BY me deterministic tiebreaker (id/date) add karo.

logic.text: Validation application me karo ya database constraints me?
logic.answer: Dono: DB me NOT NULL / UNIQUE / FOREIGN KEY / CHECK (concurrent writers aur buggy scripts ke liye last line of defence), application me friendly errors + business rules. Constraints ko skip karke sirf app-level validation par bharosa karna corruption invite karta hai.

logic.text: Slow query par pehle kya karoge: index add, query rewrite, ya caching?
logic.answer: Pehle `EXPLAIN` (ya `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`) dekho: full scan hai to index, join order/type galat hai to rewrite, aur wahich query baar-baar chal rahi hai to caching/materialized view. Index bina dekhe add karna write cost badhata hai aur galat column par bekaar hota hai.

guide.what: ML workflow ka skeleton: data split → pipeline (preprocessing + model) → fit → predict → metric ke saath evaluate → baseline se compare. Model se pehle measurement aata hai.
guide.why: Model banane se zyada important hai ye prove karna ki wo baseline se behtar hai aur leakage-free hai. Leakage aur galat metric sabse common reasons hain jahan offline score production me jhootha nikalta hai.
guide.whereUsed: Fraud/churn/classification systems, ranking aur scoring models, aur LLM era me bhi evaluation harness (metrics ka base wahi hai).
guide.howItWorks: fit() parameters data se seekhta hai, transform()/predict() unhe apply karta hai. Agar preprocessing split se pehle ho jaye to test set ka information train me chala jata hai (leakage). Pipeline is problem ko structurally khatam karta hai: CV ke har fold par preprocessing sirf train part par fit hoti hai.
guide.syntax:
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y, random_state=42)
pipe = Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()), ("clf", LogisticRegression())])
pipe.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(classification_report(y_test, pipe.predict(X_test)))

examples.code:

precision = tp / (tp + fp)
recall = tp / (tp + fn)
f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
accuracy = (tp + tn) / (tp + fp + fn + tn)
majority = max(tp + fn, fp + tn) / (tp + fp + fn + tn)

print("precision", round(precision, 3), "recall", round(recall, 3), "f1", round(f1, 3))
print("accuracy", round(accuracy, 3), "majority-baseline", round(majority, 3))
print("beats baseline:", accuracy > majority)

Majority-class baseline print karna zaroori hai: 0.85 accuracy akeli kuch prove nahi karti, 0.55 baseline ke against hi value hai.
F1 precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai, isliye dono ko ek number me balance karta hai.

howToCode.step: Baseline aur metric pehle fix karo
howToCode.detail: Problem se metric chuno (false negative mehnga → recall-first; imbalance → PR-AUC). Majority/heuristic baseline ka number likho — uske bina koi improvement claim nahi.

howToCode.step: Split se pehle kuch na dekho
howToCode.detail: Scaling/encoding/imputation sab pipeline ke andar, taaki test information train me na jaye.
Same entity ya time-series ho to GroupKFold/GroupShuffleSplit ya time-based split use karo.
Overall metric ke saath per-class aur per-bucket breakdown do — chhote buckets par 'insufficient data' bolna honest hai.

commonMistakes: Split se pehle scaling/encoding — leakage se test score optimistically high.
Imbalanced data par sirf accuracy dekhna (majority class 95% de deti hai).
Random split grouped ya time-series data par (entity/period leakage).
Threshold tune na karna — default 0.5 business cost ke hisaab se galat hota hai.
CV score ke bina hyperparameters fix karna.
bestPractices: Sab preprocessing Pipeline/ColumnTransformer me rakho (leakage-proof aur serving me same path).
Stratification use karo (stratify=y ya StratifiedKFold).
Metric ke saath baseline aur per-segment breakdown report karo.
Threshold ko cost matrix se choose karo aur usse config me version karo.
Fitted pipeline ko serialize karo — train-serve skew khatam.
guide.realWorld: Churn prediction me recall-first threshold, fraud detection me PR-AUC, aur ranking me NDCG — metric choice hi project ki quality decide karti hai. Interview me 'maine baseline 0.55 se 0.85 accuracy ki, per-class recall bhi report kiya' bolna strong hai.

practice.text: Ek confusion matrix diya gaya hai — precision, recall, F1, accuracy aur majority baseline calculate karo.

interview.q: Train/test split se pehle scaling kyun galat hai?

interview.q: Accuracy 95% par model bekaar kaise?
interview.a: Class imbalance: majority class predict karke hi 95% mila. Precision/recall per class dekho aur majority baseline se compare karo.

interview.q: Grouped data me split kaise karoge?
interview.a: GroupKFold/GroupShuffleSplit ya time-based split — same entity ya future data test me na aaye, warna leakage hoti hai.

concepts.title: Text Preprocessing & Bag-of-Words
concepts.body: Text ko model-friendly banane ka process: normalize (lowercase/unicode) → tokenize → stopwords/stemming (optional) → numeric representation (bag-of-words, TF-IDF ya embeddings).
concepts.code:
tokens = ["[CLS]", "bought", "shoes", "[SEP]", "[PAD]"]
labels = ["bought", "shoes"]

mask = [1 if t not in {"[CLS]", "[SEP]", "[PAD]"} else 0 for t in tokens]
aligned = [-100 if m == 0 else 0 for m in mask]

print(tokens, mask)
print(aligned)
print("real tokens:", sum(mask), "labels:", len(labels))

guide.what: Text ko model-friendly banane ka process: normalize (lowercase/unicode) → tokenize → stopwords/stemming (optional) → numeric representation (bag-of-words, TF-IDF ya embeddings).
guide.why: Tokenization aur normalization ke bina same word ke kai versions vocabulary me chale jaate hain — matching aur similarity dono kharab ho jati hai. Ye foundation embeddings/transformers tak jaata hai.
guide.whereUsed: Search/retrieval, sentiment aur intent classification, topic detection, aur RAG ka chunking/embedding stage.
guide.howItWorks: Bag-of-words document ko token counts ke vector me badalta hai (order kho jata hai). Cosine similarity do vectors ke angle se similarity deti hai, isliye length se independent rehti hai. Subword tokenization (BPE) ne rare words problem solve ki, par labels ko token-level align karna padta hai.

def tokens(text):

from collections import Counter
Counter(tokens(doc)).most_common(10)

# vector space

examples.code:
import re
from collections import Counter

def tokens(text):
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())

print(tokens("AI, agents! Agents run."))
print(Counter(tokens("ai agents ai rag")).most_common(2))
print(len(set(tokens("ai agents ai rag"))))
explain: Regex tokenizer punctuation hata deta hai, isliye 'Agents!' aur 'agents' ek hi token ban jate hain.
lower() + regex dono mil kar normalization karte hain — warna vocabulary me 'AI', 'ai', 'agents!' alag alag ho jaate.
unique tokens ki count vocabulary size ka idea deti hai (bag-of-words vector ki length).
'ai agent' vs 'ai agents' ka score 0.5 hai kyunki sirf 'ai' match hua — morphology (stemming) miss ho rahi hai.
Zero overlapping tokens par similarity 0.0 aati hai (dot product zero), isliye retrieval me threshold lagana zaroori hai.
Frequency ka asar dikhta hai: 'ai' do baar hone se score 0.949 tak jaata hai — TF-IDF isi ko normalize karta hai.
