Real tokens ki count aur labels ki length match honi chahiye — mismatch silently metrics galat kar deta hai.

howToCode.step: Normalize ek hi function me karo
howToCode.detail: lowercase, unicode normalize, whitespace collapse — ek versioned function banao jo training aur serving dono me chale (warna train-serve skew hoga).
split() punctuation chipka deta hai; regex pattern se saaf tokens milte hain.
max_length + truncation set karo — silent truncation debug karna mushkil hota hai.
Khaali/whitespace-only text par vocabulary lookup khaali hota hai — guard lagao aur defined output do.

commonMistakes: Train aur serving me alag cleaning code — classic train-serve skew.
Punctuation strip na karna (agents! aur agents alag tokens).
Stopwords blindly hatana — negation ('not good') ka matlab badal jata hai.
Khaali text par crash ya silent khaali vector.
Padding/special tokens ko loss me shamil karna.
bestPractices: Cleaning ko ek shared, versioned function me rakho (train + serve reuse).
Stemming/lemmatization ka effect similarity metric par measure karo, assume na karo.
TF-IDF se common words ka weight kam karo; retrieval ke liye threshold rakho.
Subword tokenization par label alignment explicitly handle karo (ignore index).
Vocabulary/model version ko artifacts ke saath version karo.
guide.realWorld: Search relevance ka lexical baseline (BM25), sentiment classifier ka TF-IDF vector, aur RAG ke retrieval eval ka hit-rate — teeno is chapter par khade hain. Interview me 'tokenization choice vocabulary aur matching quality decide karti hai' bolna practical depth dikhata hai.

practice.text: Ek tokenize(text) function likho jo lowercase, punctuation strip aur empty-input guard kare.
Bag-of-words cosine similarity implement karo aur test case se batao ki stemming kis pair ko theek karti hai.
Ek mini TF-IDF (3 documents) implement karo aur sabse high-scoring term per document print karo.

interview.q: Bag-of-words ki limitations kya hain?
interview.a: Word order aur context kho jata hai ('not good' vs 'good'), vocabulary explode hota hai aur synonyms miss hote hain — isliye embeddings/transformers aage aate hain.

interview.q: Cosine similarity Euclidean distance se behtar kyun?
interview.a: Cosine length-invariant hai: lamba document chhote document se match kar sakta hai, jabki Euclidean me sirf length ka farq dominate kar jata hai.

interview.q: Subword tokenization ka label alignment problem?
interview.a: Ek word kai tokens me toot jata hai, isliye word-level labels ko token-level me align karna padta hai — padding/special tokens ko loss se exclude karte hain (-100/attention mask).

guide.miniChallenge: Ek lexical search index likho (tokens + counter) jo query par top-3 documents cosine similarity se laute aur zero-hit par khaali list de.
guide.debugTask: Local me model theek chalta hai par production me predictions shift ho gayi hain — preprocessing me kaun si do cheezein mismatch ho sakti hain?

coding.text: Coding task: regex tokenizer + bag-of-words cosine similarity likho — `'AI, agents!'` ke tokens nikalo aur `'ai agent'` vs `'ai agents'` / `'cats'` ka similarity print karo.
coding.solution:
import re
from collections import Counter
def tokens(text):
    return re.findall(r'[a-z0-9]+', text.lower())
def cosine(a, b):
    ca, cb = Counter(tokens(a)), Counter(tokens(b))
    dot = sum(v * cb.get(k, 0) for k, v in ca.items())
    na = sum(v * v for v in ca.values()) ** 0.5
    nb = sum(v * v for v in cb.values()) ** 0.5
    return 0.0 if not na or not nb else dot / (na * nb)
print(tokens('AI, agents!'))
print(round(cosine('ai agent', 'ai agents'), 3), round(cosine('ai agent', 'cats'), 3))
# ['ai', 'agents']
# 0.5 0.0
coding.check: Regex tokenizer punctuation hata deta hai (`split()` nahi hatata). 0.5 similarity dikhata hai ki 'agent' aur 'agents' alag tokens hain — stemming/lemmatization ka justification yahi hai. Khaali token list par 0.0 return karne ka guard bhi laga hua hai.

logic.text: `'AI, agents!'.lower().split()` aur regex tokenizer `[a-z0-9]+` — output kya hoga?
logic.answer: `split()` → `['ai', 'agents!']` (punctuation token ke saath chipka rehta hai), regex → `['ai', 'agents']` (saaf tokens). Vocabulary aur cosine similarity regex version par hi sahi kaam karti hai — warna `agents!` aur `agents` do alag tokens ban jate hain.

logic.text: Bag-of-words me `'ai agent'` vs `'ai agents'` ka cosine similarity kitna aayega?
logic.answer: 0.5 — tokens `['ai','agent']` vs `['ai','agents']`, sirf `ai` match karta hai: dot = 1 aur dono norms √2 hain → 1/2. `'cats'` ke saath 0.0 aata hai. Ye ek number hi stemming/lemmatization ki zaroorat proof karta hai.

logic.text: Transformer ke outputs me labels tokens se misalign hain — pehla check kya?
logic.answer: Labels aur token list ki length match karo: tokenization ke baad `input_ids` me special tokens ([CLS]/[SEP]/padding) add hote hain, jo labels me nahi hone chahiye. Padding tokens ko loss se exclude karo (`-100` ya attention mask) warna loss aur metrics dono galat aate hain.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case text pipeline ko todta hai?
logic.answer: Khaali/whitespace-only input (vocab lookup me kuch nahi milta → empty vector ya crash) aur max-length se lamba text (silent truncation). Guard: `if not text.strip(): return []` aur explicit `truncation=True, max_length=...` — truncation ko chhupne na do.

logic.text: Text cleaning kahan karo — ingestion par ya model input ke waqt?
logic.answer: Ingestion par normalize karo (lowercase, unicode normalisation, whitespace collapse) ek versioned function me, aur wahi function training aur serving dono me reuse karo; model input par sirf tokenizer-specific step. Do jagah alag cleaning = train-serve skew.

logic.text: Bada model vs fast inference — pehle kya optimize karoge?
logic.answer: Pehle latency budget aur quality bar likho, phir sasta option test karo: quantization → distillation → chhota model/caching. Bade model ka fayda eval set par measurable ho tabhi lo, warna latency aur cost dono badhte hain bina user-visible gain ke.

concepts.title: RAG: Chunk, Retrieve, Ground & Evaluate
concepts.body: RAG = retrieval + generation: apne documents ko chunks me todo, unhe index karo, query par relevant chunks laao, aur model ko sirf usi context se jawab likhne do — citation ke saath.
concepts.output:
recall@1 0.5
recall@2 0.5
frozen eval set size 2
concepts.tip: Interview me RAG ko do-stage system ki tarah describe karo aur har stage ka metric batao — isse pata chalta hai ki tum measurement culture laate ho, sirf prompt engineering nahi.

guide.what: RAG = retrieval + generation: apne documents ko chunks me todo, unhe index karo, query par relevant chunks laao, aur model ko sirf usi context se jawab likhne do — citation ke saath.
guide.why: LLM apne parameters se jawab 'bana' deta hai (hallucination) aur private/fresh data nahi jaanta. RAG grounding deta hai: jawab source se bandha hota hai, aur update sirf index refresh se hota hai (retraining nahi).
guide.whereUsed: Docs/support assistants, policy aur order lookups, codebase Q&A, aur internal knowledge search.
prereqs: FastAPI Request, Validation & Response (serving ke liye)
guide.howItWorks: Offline: chunk (size + overlap) → embedding → vector index. Online: query embed → top-k similarity search → context assembly (chunk ids ke saath) → LLM call under a prompt contract → answer + citations. Do jagah evaluation hoti hai: retrieval (hit-rate/recall@k) aur generation (faithfulness/correctness).
guide.syntax:
# offline
chunks = chunk(doc, size=800, overlap=100)
index = [(c.id, embed(c.text)) for c in chunks]

# online
hits = top_k(index, embed(question), k=5, threshold=0.35)
if not hits:
    return "context me nahi hai"        # abstain
prompt = build_prompt(question, hits)   # ids included
answer = llm(prompt)

examples.code:
docs = {
    "d1": "python list methods append extend remove",
    "d2": "sets give o(1) membership and dedupe",
    "d3": "offline retrieval uses cosine similarity",
}

def retrieve(query, k=2):
    qs = set(query.lower().split())
    scored = [(d, len(qs & set(text.split()))) for d, text in docs.items()]
    return sorted((s for s in scored if s[1] > 0), key=lambda p: -p[1])[:k]

print(retrieve("set membership dedupe"))
print(retrieve("kubernetes cluster"))
explain: Token overlap ek explainable baseline hai — production me embedding search isse behtar hoti hai par ye zero-dependency version debugging me kaam aata hai.
Sirf positive score wale chunks lautate hain, isliye zero-hit par khaali list milti hai (ye abstain ka signal hai).
Threshold ke bina har query kuch na kuch lauta degi — aur wahi hallucination ka pehla karan hai.

examples.code:
chunks = [
    {"id": "d2", "text": "sets give o(1) membership and dedupe", "score": 2.0},
    {"id": "d4", "text": "offline retrieval uses cosine similarity", "score": 0.5},
]

def build_prompt(question, chunks, threshold=1.0):
    kept = [c for c in chunks if c["score"] >= threshold]
    if not kept:
        return "NO_CONTEXT: jawab context me nahi hai"
    ctx = "\n".join(f"[{c['id']}] {c['text']}" for c in kept)
    return f"Answer only from the context and cite ids.\n\nContext:\n{ctx}\n\nQ: {question}"

print(build_prompt("dedupe kaise?", chunks))
print(build_prompt("kubernetes?", []))
examples.output:
Answer only from the context and cite ids.

Context:
[d2] sets give o(1) membership and dedupe

Q: dedupe kaise?
NO_CONTEXT: jawab context me nahi hai
explain: Score threshold se kam-relevance chunk prompt me jata hi nahi — isse grounding better hoti hai aur tokens bhi bachte hain.
Har context block ke saath stable id bhejna citations ko reliable banata hai (warna model id andaaza lagata hai).
Zero-hit case ka explicit jawab ('NO_CONTEXT') model ko apni memory se banane se rokta hai.

examples.output:
recall@1 0.5
recall@2 0.5
frozen eval set size 2
explain: Retrieval evaluation generation se alag hai: recall@k yahi batata hai ki sahi chunk aaya ya nahi.
recall@1 vs recall@2 ka farq se pata chalta hai ki top-1 ranking weak hai ya retrieval hi.
Frozen eval set (small, versioned) hi honest improvement ka proof hai — 'better lagta hai' nahi.

howToCode.detail: Chunk size aur overlap data ke shape se chuno (table-heavy PDF me structure-aware). Bahut chhota chunk context todta hai, bahut bada noise laata hai.
Top-k plus score threshold — threshold ke bina har query kuch lauta deti hai aur model galat context par jawab bana deta hai.
howToCode.code:
hits = top_k(index, q, k=5, threshold=0.35)
if not hits: return abstain()

howToCode.detail: Context ke saath chunk ids bhejo, model se structured output (answer + source_ids) maango, aur 'sirf context se jawab do, warna abstain' rule likho.
Retrieval par recall@k/hit-rate aur generation par faithfulness/correctness — ek hi 'accuracy' me mila dena debug impossible banata hai.

commonMistakes: Zero-hit par bhi top-k bhej dena (ya context khaali chhod dena) — model apni memory se jawab likh deta hai.
Citation ids prompt me na bhejna, phir citation ka reliable hone ki umeed rakhna.
Chunk size ko tune na karna (sabse zyada impact wala knob yahi hai).
Grounding ko sirf prompt instruction se maangna — output schema validation ke bina.
Retrieval aur generation ko ek metric me mila dena.
bestPractices: Citations ko output schema ka part banao (structured output + validation).
Relevance threshold par explicitly abstain karo — 'context me nahi hai' ek valid answer hai.
Prompt me context dedupe karo aur max tokens cap lagao (cost + noise dono kam).
Eval set frozen rakho (JSONL + version) aur regression gate lagao.
Chunk ids ko stable rakho taaki citation aur trace id match karein.
guide.realWorld: Support assistant jo article ids cite karta hai, policy lookup jahan 'docs me nahi mila' acceptable answer hai, aur internal codebase Q&A — teeno me yahi pipeline chalti hai. Interview me 'recall@5 0.62 se 0.86 (table-aware chunking + hybrid retrieval)' bolna strong evidence hai.

practice.text: Ek chunk(text, size, overlap) function likho aur overlap ka effect word count par dikhaao.
Retrieval ke liye hit-rate aur recall@k implement karo aur ek score threshold tune karo.
Ek full eval harness likho: 20 cases, recall@k + abstention rate + markdown report — CI me gate karne layak.

interview.q: RAG aur fine-tuning me kab kaunsa?
interview.a: RAG tab jab knowledge badalti rahe aur citations chahiye (update = index refresh). Fine-tuning tab jab style/format/behaviour chahiye ya latency critical ho. Dono saath bhi use hote hain.

interview.q: Hallucination ko kaise kam karoge?
interview.a: Retrieval threshold + abstention, chunk ids ke saath grounded prompt, structured output validation, aur citation-checking eval — sirf prompt me 'sach bolo' likhna kaafi nahi.

interview.q: RAG me evaluation do level par kyun?
interview.a: Retrieval fail ho to model ke paas sahi context hi nahi tha; generation fail ho to context tha par jawab galat bana. Dono ko alag measure karke hi pata chalta hai fix kahan karna hai.

guide.miniChallenge: Ek toy RAG evaluator likho jo 5 documents par query de, top-k laute, abstain kare jab score threshold se neeche ho, aur recall@k print kare.
guide.debugTask: Citations galat chunk ka naam de rahe hain jabki answer sahi hai. Prompt me kya missing hoga, aur fix kya hai?

coding.solution:
from collections import Counter
DOCS = [
    ('d1', 'python list methods append extend remove'),
    ('d2', 'sets give O(1) membership and dedupe'),
    ('d3', 'offline retrieval uses cosine similarity'),
]
def retrieve(query, k=2):
    q = Counter(query.lower().split())
    scored = []
    for cid, text in DOCS:
        t = Counter(text.lower().split())
        dot = sum(v * t.get(w, 0) for w, v in q.items())
        scored.append((dot, cid))
    scored.sort(reverse=True)
    return [(cid, score) for score, cid in scored[:k] if score > 0]
print(retrieve('set membership dedupe'))
print(retrieve('python list'))
print(retrieve('kubernetes'))

# [('d1', 2)]
# []

logic.text: RAG pipeline ke steps ka order likho (ingest se answer tak) aur batao evaluation do jagah kyun hoti hai.
logic.answer: chunk → embed → index → (query: embed) → top-k retrieve → prompt assemble (context + question + ids) → LLM → answer + citation. logic.text: LLM ka jawab sahi hai par citation galat chunk ka hai — likely cause?

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case RAG ko hallucination par majboor karta hai?

Fix: score threshold par explicitly 'no relevant context' return karo aur model ko bolo ki wo 'context me nahi hai' bole.

logic.text: Prompt building me validation kahan lagao — retrieval par ya generated answer par?

logic.text: Retrieval quality vs latency — pehle kya tune karoge?

concepts.title: Agent Loops, Tools & Guardrails
concepts.body: Agent ek loop hai: observe → plan → tool call → result → repeat, jab tak goal na pura ho ya bound hit na ho. LLM decision leta hai, host loop ko bound karta hai, aur tools side effects karte hain.

guide.what: Agent ek loop hai: observe → plan → tool call → result → repeat, jab tak goal na pura ho ya bound hit na ho. LLM decision leta hai, host loop ko bound karta hai, aur tools side effects karte hain.
guide.why: Unbounded agents cost blow-up aur production incidents ka source hote hain (infinite tool calls, duplicate orders, galat arguments). Bounds + validation + idempotency ke bina agent demo theek chalta hai, production me nahi.
guide.whereUsed: Support automation, data pipelines jo multi-step hain, research/summarisation workflows, aur n8n/LangChain style orchestrations.
guide.howItWorks: Har step par planner ek action chunta hai (tool + arguments), host action ko validate karta hai, tool execute hota hai aur uska result context me wapas jaata hai. Loop ke teen guards: max_steps, repeated-action detection, aur per-tool attempt cap. Side-effecting tools ke liye idempotency key chahiye — retry ko naya event samajhna duplicate side effect deta hai.

explain: Bounded loop: har action ek step hai, aur 'stop' action par clean exit hota hai.
Khaali plan par safe no-op (stop) hota hai — agent ko crash nahi hone dena chahiye.
Plan me stop na ho to max_steps guard loop ko rokta hai — yahi cost runaway se bachata hai.
Repeated-action detection wahi action dobara dekh kar loop halt kar deta hai — planner ke loop me phasne ka fix.
max_steps host ka guard hai aur repeated-action check planner ke bug ka guard — dono chahiye.
Dusre case me teen alag actions hain aur 'stop' par clean exit hota hai, isliye halting trigger nahi hoti.
Tool arguments ko execute karne se PEHLE schema se validate kiya jata hai — LLM output 99% sahi hota hai, bacha 1% production me har din aata hai.
bool ko explicitly reject kiya gaya kyunki Python me True int ka subclass hai (isinstance(True, int) True hota hai).

coding.text: Coding task: bounded agent loop likho — `run_agent(plan, max_steps)` jo repeated action detect karke halt kare aur `max_steps` par ruke; teen plans par test karo.
coding.solution:
def run_agent(plan, max_steps=4):
    seen, log = [], []
    for step in range(1, max_steps + 1):
        action = plan[min(step - 1, len(plan) - 1)] if plan else 'stop'
        log.append((step, action))
        if action == 'stop':
            break
        if seen.count(action) >= 1:
            log.append(('halt', 'repeated action: ' + action))
            break
        seen.append(action)
    return log
print(run_agent(['search', 'search', 'stop']))
print(run_agent(['search', 'calc', 'stop']))
print(run_agent([]))
# [(1, 'search'), (2, 'search'), ('halt', 'repeated action: search')]
# [(1, 'search'), (2, 'calc'), (3, 'stop')]
# [(1, 'stop')]

concepts.title: FastAPI Request, Validation & Response
concepts.body: HTTP API ek contract hai: request ka shape (types + ranges), response ka shape, aur error ka shape. FastAPI me ye contract Pydantic models se likha jata hai aur usi se validation + docs automatically bante hain.
concepts.tip: API design par ye sequence bolo: 'schema pehle, limits aur timeouts uske baad, phir throughput tuning — kyunki bina limits ke tuning sirf outage ki speed badhati hai'.

guide.what: HTTP API ek contract hai: request ka shape (types + ranges), response ka shape, aur error ka shape. FastAPI me ye contract Pydantic models se likha jata hai aur usi se validation + docs automatically bante hain.
guide.why: 90% production bugs invalid/unexpected input se aate hain. Boundary par strict validation, consistent error shape aur timeouts ke bina API 'sometimes works' ban jati hai — jo debug karna sabse mehnga hai.
guide.whereUsed: ML inference endpoints (/predict), RAG /ask endpoints, webhooks, aur internal service-to-service APIs.
guide.howItWorks: Request path: ASGI server → middleware (logging/CORS/auth) → router → dependencies → request model validation (fail par 422) → handler → response model serialisation (fail par 500) → JSON. Validation request model par hone se error response automatic aur consistent milta hai; isliye app/service/DB teen layer par apni apni responsibility rehti hai.

examples.code:
def validate(payload):
    problems = []
    text = payload.get("text")
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        problems.append("text: required non-empty string")
    top_k = payload.get("top_k", 3)
    if not isinstance(top_k, int) or isinstance(top_k, bool) or not (1 <= top_k <= 10):
        problems.append("top_k: int in 1..10")
    return problems

print(validate({"text": "  "}))
print(validate({"text": "hi", "top_k": 99}))
print(validate({"text": "hello", "top_k": 5}))
explain: Whitespace-only text 'non-empty' lagti hai — isliye strip() ke baad check karna padta hai.
Bool ko alag se reject kiya gaya kyunki Python me True int ka subclass hai (True ko 1 maan lena silent bug hai).
Valid payload par khaali list aati hai — handler tab hi chalta hai jab problems khaali hon.
Exponential backoff (base x 2^i) se retries clustered nahi hote — upstream ko recover karne ka time milta hai.
Delays ko record karke return kiya gaya, isliye behaviour observable hai (test me assert kar sakte ho).
Attempts khatam hone par clear exception raise hoti hai — silent default return karna debugging ko mushkil banata hai.
Success aur error dono ka same envelope shape (ok + request_id) rakha gaya — client ko do alag parse paths nahi likhne padte.
request_id har response me jaata hai, isliye client complaint se server logs tak trace karna ek step ka kaam hai.
Timestamp UTC me ISO format me diya gaya — timezone ambiguity JSON me silent bug ban jati hai.

howToCode.detail: Types, ranges aur required fields model me likho — validation aur OpenAPI docs dono free mil jate hain.
Har error (validation, auth, upstream) ka same JSON shape do — client side branching kam ho jati hai.
Har outbound call par timeout do, payload size limit aur rate limit lagao — warna ek hung dependency poori service le doobti hai.
Request id, latency aur error-rate metrics; logs me content nahi, ids — PII safe rakho.

commonMistakes: Validation ko sirf frontend par chhod dena (curl/scripts se invalid data aata hai).
Bare except se saare errors ko 500 bana dena — caller ko actionable 4xx chahiye.
Outbound calls me timeout na dena (worker hang).
Error response me stack trace ya secrets bhej dena.
Error case me alag schema lautana — client parse todta hai.
bestPractices: Request/response models se contract lock karo (versioned API path ya header).
Timeouts + retries sirf idempotent operations par.
Rate limit aur payload size limit har public endpoint par.
Structured logging with request id (aur latency field).
Smoke test deploy ke baad (health + ek real request).
guide.realWorld: Ek /ask endpoint jahan top_k range-bound hai, upstream LLM call retry+timeout ke saath chalti hai, aur error envelope consistent rehta hai — yahi production-grade minimal API hai. Interview me 'main schema, timeouts aur limits pehle rakhta hoon, phr throughput tune karta hoon' bolna senior signal hai.

practice.text: Ek validate(payload) function likho jo text aur top_k (1..10) check kare.
Retry with exponential backoff + jitter implement karo aur delays ko return karo taaki test ho sake.
Ek consistent response envelope likho (success + error) aur uske liye 3 unit tests likho.

interview.q: Validation kis layer me honi chahiye?
interview.a: Request model par schema/types, service layer me business rules, aur DB me integrity constraints — teeno, kyunki har layer alag failure mode rokti hai.

interview.q: Retry kab nahi karna chahiye?
interview.a: Non-idempotent operations par (POST payment) bina idempotency key ke, aur permanent errors (4xx validation) par — retry sirf transient (timeout/5xx) par.

interview.q: 500 ke baad logs me kuch nahi milta — kya check karoge?
interview.a: Log level/buffering, request id ki presence, unhandled exception handler, aur upstream timeout — structured logs ke bina 'occasional 500' guesswork hai.

guide.miniChallenge: Ek mini API contract likho (models + validate + error envelope) aur uske against 5 test cases chalao: empty text, bool top_k, out-of-range, valid, aur upstream failure.
guide.debugTask: Local me sab chal raha hai par production me 500 aur logs khaali hain. Structural order likho jisme tum debug karoge.

logic.text: `POST /predict` par `{'text': '  '}` aaya — validator kya return karega aur kyun?
logic.answer: `['text: required non-empty string']` — whitespace-only string "non-empty" lagti hai, isliye `strip()` ke baad check karna padta hai (`if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip()`). Warna khaali query model par chali jati hai.

logic.text: Request ka lifecycle likho: socket se JSON response tak (layers ke naam ke saath).
logic.answer: ASGI server (uvicorn) → middleware (logging/CORS/auth) → router (path + method match) → dependency injection (auth/db session) → request model validation (fail par 422) → handler → response model serialisation (fail par 500) → JSON. Errors ek central exception handler se consistent shape me bhejo.

logic.text: Endpoint kabhi-kabhi 500 deta hai par logs me kuch nahi milta — kya suspect karoge?
logic.answer: Teen common wajah: unhandled exception jo log se bahar ho rahi hai (worker crash, hard timeout), log level/buffering (request id missing), ya upstream dependency ka silence (bina timeout ke hang). Fix: exception handler, request id har log line me, aur explicit timeouts + metrics.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case schema validation ko chakma de deta hai?
logic.answer: Type coercion: `'1'`/`1` aksar `int` ban jate hain, `True` bhi `1` ban jata hai (bool int ka subclass hai), aur JSON me NaN/Infinity allowed hote hain. Fix: strict types (`StrictInt`), bool ko explicitly reject karo, `allow_inf_nan=False`, aur boundary checks (1..10) likho.

logic.text: Validation kis layer me ho — app, service, ya database?
logic.answer: Request model par schema + types, service layer me business rules (permissions, state transitions), database me constraints (unique/foreign keys/not null). Teenon rakho: schema UX deta hai, service policy enforce karta hai, DB integrity guarantee deta hai.

logic.text: Throughput vs correctness — pehle kya tune karoge?
logic.answer: Pehle correctness (timeouts, payload limits, idempotency) taaki retries aur concurrency safe hon, phir concurrency (workers, connection pool, caching). Limits ke bina throughput tuning sirf tail latency aur outage probability badhati hai.

concepts.title: Analytics KPIs & Growth Metrics
concepts.body: KPI ek measurable business number hai (revenue, growth %, conversion, retention). Achha KPI: defined grain, defined filters, aur defined time window — warna har banda apna number laata hai.
concepts.code:
orders = [{"id": 1, "items": 2}, {"id": 2, "items": 3}]
items = [
    {"order_id": 1, "amount": 10.0},
    {"order_id": 1, "amount": 5.0},
    {"order_id": 2, "amount": 7.0},
]

item_total = sum(i["amount"] for i in items)
naive = sum(o["items"] * 7.5 for o in orders)   # wrong grain: items x avg price

guide.what: KPI ek measurable business number hai (revenue, growth %, conversion, retention). Achha KPI: defined grain, defined filters, aur defined time window — warna har banda apna number laata hai.
guide.why: Dashboard ka number decision leta hai. Grain ya filter ki chhoti galti (fan-out, NULL bucket, zero base) poore business ko galat direction me le jaati hai — aur trust ek baar tootne par wapas nahi aata.
guide.whereUsed: Revenue/growth reporting, funnel aur conversion analysis, retention cohorts, aur experiment readouts.
guide.howItWorks: KPI do cheezon par khada hai: grain (ek row kya represent karti hai) aur denominator (ratio ka base). Growth window function (LAG) se nikalta hai, aur ratio metrics ko sum nahi kiya jaa sakta — numerator aur denominator alag sum karke divide karna padta hai.

explain: Month-over-month change ((cur - prev) / prev) do consecutive points par chalta hai — window function LAG ka plain-Python version.
Negative growth bhi print hoti hai (-40%) — use chhupana ya clip karna metric ko jhootha banata hai.
Base month zero hone par None lauta rahe hain (division by zero ke bajaye) aur khaali input par khaali list.

examples.code:
rows = [
    ("east", "2026-01", 120),
    ("east", "2026-02", 150),
    ("west", "2026-01", 90),
    ("west", "2026-02", 99),
]

total = sum(r[2] for r in rows)
best = max(rows, key=lambda r: r[2])
by_region = {}
for region, _, amount in rows:
    by_region[region] = by_region.get(region, 0) + amount

print(total, best)
print({k: round(v / total * 100, 1) for k, v in sorted(by_region.items())})
print(sum(by_region.values()) == total)
explain: Grain yahan region-month hai, isliye total SUM aur best MAX se nikalte hain.
Share (%) nikalne ke liye denominator poora total hai — ratio metrics ko isi tarah base ke saath report karo.
Reconciliation check (grouped total == overall total) dashboard ki honesty ka sabse sasta test hai.

Percentage ko average mat karo: sum(num)/sum(den) karo, aur zero/near-zero denominators par 'n/a' do.

commonMistakes: Ratios ko sum karna (averages of averages) — galat number.
Fan-out join se double counting (grain mismatch).
Zero base period par growth calculate karna (division by zero / infinity).
NULL/unknown bucket ek jagah count karna aur doosri jagah nahi — totals mismatch.
Timezone/grain mismatch (month boundary UTC vs local).
bestPractices: KPI definition document karo (grain, filters, window, exclusions).
Har report me baseline/comparison period rakho.
Data quality checks model/data layer par lagao, BI me nahi.
Slow dashboard ke liye pehle model/grain theek karo, phir DAX-metrics tune karo.
Totals ke next to reconciliation test rakho (visual vs model).
guide.realWorld: Monthly revenue dashboard, funnel conversion report, aur retention cohorts — teeno me grain aur denominator define karna hi 80% kaam hai. Interview me 'ratio metrics ko main numerator/denominator se banata hoon' bolna instantly correctness-first mindset dikhata hai.

interview.q: Ratio metrics ko sum kyun nahi kar sakte?
interview.a: Average of averages galat hota hai: 2/10 aur 100/1000 ka simple average 0.55 dikhata hai jabki sach 102/1010 = 0.101 hai. Isliye numerator aur denominator alag sum karo.

interview.q: Dashboard total sahi par per-region sum mismatch — pehla check?
interview.a: Grain/fan-out (duplicate keys se rows multiply) aur filter context ka farq; row counts compare karke shuru karo.

interview.q: Seasonality kaise handle karoge?
interview.a: Same-period-last-year comparison aur trailing averages use karo; month-over-month akela Dec→Jan ke liye misleading hai.

coding.text: Coding task: monthly KPIs nikalo — total revenue, best month, aur MoM growth % (Jan 120000, Feb 150000, Mar 90000), khaali series ka guard bhi dikhao.
coding.solution:
months = [('2026-01', 120000), ('2026-02', 150000), ('2026-03', 90000)]
def mom(series):
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(series)):
        prev, cur = series[i - 1][1], series[i][1]
        out.append((series[i][0], round(100 * (cur - prev) / prev, 1)))
    return out
print('total:', sum(v for _, v in months), '| best:', max(months, key=lambda m: m[1]))
print('mom:', mom(months))
print('mom(empty):', mom([]))
# total: 360000 | best: ('2026-02', 150000)
# mom: [('2026-02', 25.0), ('2026-03', -40.0)]
# mom(empty): []

logic.text: Monthly revenue Jan 120000, Feb 150000, Mar 90000 — Feb aur Mar ka MoM growth % kya hoga?
logic.answer: Feb = +25.0%, Mar = -40.0% — formula `(cur - prev) / prev * 100`. Dhyan do ki base month zero/khaali ho to division by zero aata hai, isliye `NULLIF` ya guard chahiye.

logic.text: KPI: total revenue, best month, MoM growth — calculation order likho.
logic.answer: Pehle per-month aggregate (GROUP BY month — grain fix), phir total = SUM, best = MAX by revenue, phir MoM = window `LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)`. Order matter karta hai: aggregate se pehle MoM nikalna galat deta hai (row-level pe growth).

logic.text: Dashboard me total sahi hai par per-region totals ka sum mismatch hai — likely cause?
logic.answer: Grain ka fan-out: order-items level join se rows multiply ho gayi (double counting), ya filter context alag hai (page-level filter vs visual filter), ya koi NULL/unknown bucket ek jagah count ho raha hai doosri jagah nahi. Pehle grain confirm karo: 1 row = 1 order ya 1 order-item?

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case growth ya percentage metrics ko todta hai?
logic.answer: Zero/missing base period (naya segment pehle month 0 → division by zero ya infinity) aur seasonality (Dec vs Jan ka naive comparison). Fix: base zero ho to 'n/a' dikhao (NULLIF/guard) aur same-period-last-year comparison saath rakho.

logic.text: Data quality checks source par lagao ya BI model me?
logic.answer: Primary checks source/ELT par (grain, key uniqueness, null rates, referential integrity) taaki model saaf data par bane; Power BI me sirf display-level sanity (totals reconcile, outliers visible). DAX me data cleaning karna tech debt hai — logic do jagah bikharta hai.

logic.text: Dashboard slow hai — pehle kya optimize karoge?
logic.answer: Pehle model (star schema, correct grain, unnecessary columns/relationships hatao), phir DAX (iterator `SUMX` ki jagah column aggregate, `CALCULATE` filter count kam karo), phir visual count aur incremental refresh. Measure page ka time sabse pehle.

concepts.title: MLOps: Docker, CI/CD & Deploy
concepts.body: MLOps ka core: reproducible environment (Docker + pinned deps), automated checks (CI), aur safe deploy (immutable image tag, health checks, rollback).
concepts.tip: Production sawal par ye teen cheezein naam se bolo: 'pinned image, readiness probe aur ek-command rollback' — yahi teen production readiness ki asli definition hain.

guide.what: MLOps ka core: reproducible environment (Docker + pinned deps), automated checks (CI), aur safe deploy (immutable image tag, health checks, rollback).
guide.why: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' ka matlab environment drift hai. Reproducible image + config validation + rollback plan ke bina deployment ek gamble hota hai.
guide.whereUsed: Model serving containers, batch jobs, API deploys, aur scheduled pipelines (retrain/eval).
guide.howItWorks: Build se deploy tak: commit → CI (lint/tests/build) → image build + tag (commit sha) → registry push → deploy with config inject → startup/readiness probe → traffic shift. Rollback = purana tag dobara deploy karna, isliye image immutable aur tag traceable hona chahiye. Liveness 'process zinda hai?' poochta hai, readiness 'traffic le sakta hai?' — dono alag rakhna must hai.
guide.syntax:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

Validation failure par clear message milta hai (kaun kaun si key missing/typed galat) — fail fast, silent default nahi.

examples.code:
import hashlib

commit = "8f2c1ab"
sha = hashlib.sha1(commit.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
registry = "registry.example.com/app"
tags = {"prod": f"{registry}:{commit}", "previous": f"{registry}:1a2b3c4"}

def rollback(current, history):
    return {"action": "redeploy", "tag": history[-1], "from": current}

print("sha", sha)
print(tags)
print(rollback(tags["prod"], [registry + ":1a2b3c4"]))
print("immutable:", commit in tags["prod"] and tags["prod"] != tags["previous"])
explain: Image tag commit ko reference karta hai, isliye 'kaun sa code live hai' ka ek hi jawab hota hai aur rollback deterministic.
Rollback ek data operation hai (purane tag ko redeploy karna) — isliye rollback ko rehearsed script ki tarah rakho.
Immutable tags (latest nahi) use karne se same tag par alag code deploy hone ka risk khatam hota hai.
Liveness sirf process check karta hai (restart decision), readiness dependencies bhi check karta hai (traffic decision).
DB down hone par readiness fail hoti hai par liveness pass — isliye orchestrator container restart nahi karega (galat restart se cascade outage hota hai).
Detailed result print karne se pata chalta hai kaunsi dependency fail hui — debugging me seedha kaam aata hai.

howToCode.detail: Missing env var par boot fail ho, chup-chaap default na le — fail-fast config se ek deploy me pata chal jata hai.
Liveness ko sirf process check karna do, readiness ko dependencies; startup probe ko slow init ke liye time do.
Image tag = commit sha, migrations expand-contract (purane aur naye version saath chalein), aur rollback ek script/command ho.

commonMistakes: latest tag use karna (rollback ka koi deterministic target nahi).
Lockfile commit na karna — CI me build pass, production me 'module not found'.
Liveness me dependency check karna — ek DB hiccup poori fleet restart kar deta hai.
Secrets image ya git me daalna.
Rolling deploy ke saath incompatible schema migration — mixed versions ke requests fail.
bestPractices: Immutable image tags (commit sha) aur ek-command rollback.
Secrets secrets-manager/env se inject karo, .env.example version karo.
Observability minimum: structured logs, latency/error metrics, ek dashboard, ek alert.
Migrations expand-contract pattern me karo (zero-downtime).
Post-deploy smoke test aur health endpoint rakho.
guide.realWorld: Ek FastAPI model server jo free tier par deploy hai (cold start ke saath warm-up ping), aur ek nightly eval job jo CI me regression gate chalata hai — dono MLOps ke daily kaam hain. Interview me 'maine image tag commit sha rakha, rollback ek command hai' bolna production maturity dikhata hai.

practice.text: Ek Dockerfile likho (pinned base, requirements pehle, code baad me) aur build time kam karne ka order explain karo.
Config validation likho jo missing env var par startup fail kar de.
Ek deploy checklist likho: probes, migrations, rollback, smoke test aur alert — har item ka failure mode bhi likho.

interview.q: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' ka pehla check?
interview.a: Environment parity: base image tag, pinned dependencies (lockfile), env vars/secrets, aur paths/permissions — 90% aise issues yahin se aate hain.

interview.q: Liveness aur readiness probe me farq?
interview.a: Liveness process zinda hai ya nahi (fail → restart), readiness traffic le sakta hai ya nahi (fail → load balancer se hatao). Dependencies sirf readiness me check karo.

interview.q: Rolling deploy ke baad 5% requests fail kyun ho jaati hain?
interview.a: Mixed versions old/new code ya DB schema ke saath incompatible hote hain — expand-contract migration chahiye, aur logs me version tag hona chahiye.

guide.miniChallenge: Ek deploy plan likho (checklist form me) jo cold start, config validation, probes, rollback aur post-deploy smoke test cover kare.
guide.debugTask: Local me pip install theek chal raha hai par CI image me 'module not found'. Do sabse likely cause batao aur fix likho.

logic.text: Retry policy `attempts=3, base=0.01s` exponential backoff ke saath — upstream pehle 2 calls fail kare aur teesri par chale to total sleep kitna hoga?
logic.answer: 0.01 + 0.02 = 0.03s (pehli failure ke baad 0.01, doosri ke baad 0.02, teesri attempt success par loop khatam) aur attempts log `[0, 1, 2]` rahega; result `'ok'`. Sirf transient errors (TimeoutError) retry hote hain — ValueError turant raise hoti hai.

logic.text: Container build se deploy tak ke steps likho (git se live traffic tak).
logic.answer: commit → PR review → CI (lint + tests + build) → image build + tag (commit sha) → registry push → deploy (env/config inject) → startup probe/health check → traffic shift. Rollback = purane tag ko dobara deploy karna, isliye image immutable aur tag traceable hona chahiye.

logic.text: "Mere machine par chalta hai" par production me fail — pehla check kya?
logic.answer: Environment parity: Python/base image ka exact version, dependencies pinned (lock file), env vars aur secrets, aur file paths/permissions. Dockerfile me base image ko explicit tag karo aur requirements lock karo — `latest` aur unpinned deps dono silent drift dete hain.

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case deployment ko todta hai?
logic.answer: Startup par migration/secret missing, health-check timeout (slow cold start par app 'unhealthy' mark ho jata hai), aur concurrent duplicate deploys. Fix: startup probe + readiness separate, idempotent migrations, aur deploy lock (ek writer).

logic.text: Config aur secrets kahan rakho?
logic.answer: Secrets secrets-manager/env se inject karo (image me ya git me kabhi nahi), non-secret config env vars + sensible defaults me, aur app startup par validate karke fail-fast karo (missing var par boot hi na ho). `.env` sirf local ke liye aur gitignore me.

logic.text: Reliability vs delivery speed — pehle kya invest karoge?
logic.answer: Pehle observability + rollback (structured logs, metrics, health checks, ek-command rollback) — bina inke speed sirf outage ki speed hai. Uske baad caching/autoscaling/resource tuning: reliability ke bina kiya gaya optimization phatne par debug hi nahi ho pata.

title: AI Engineer + Data Scientist Interview Mastery

concepts.title: Core Concepts
concepts.body: Interview me knowledge + communication dono measure hote hain. Strong answer concise hota hai, example deta hai, trade-off batata hai aur interviewer ke follow-up ke liye clear hooks deta hai. PROJECT STORY DEBUGGING STORY Problem -> approach -> architecture -> your Symptom reproduce -> isolate layer -> inspect contribution -> challenge -> result -> learning. types/inputs/logs -> fix -> test regression. TRADE-OFFS BEHAVIORAL Accuracy vs latency, cost vs quality, batch vs STAR: Situation -> Task -> Action -> Result. real-time, simple vs scalable. Context ke saath Result measurable ho to better. answer.
concepts.code:
def project_answer(problem, approach, result):
    return (f"Problem: {problem}. "
            f"Approach: {approach}. "
            f"Result: {result}.")

print(project_answer("manual support workflow",
                     "API + webhook + validation",
                     "less manual repetition and better traceability"))
concepts.output: Problem: manual support workflow. Approach: API + webhook + validation. Result: less manual repetition and better traceability.

concepts.title: Interview Depth
concepts.body: Is page ka goal hai concept ko implementation decision tak le jana. Interviewer ko syntax se zyada reasoning, edge cases aur trade-offs dikhte hain. WHAT Kya hai aur kab use karoge? WHY Kaunsi problem solve hoti hai? RISK Common bug / failure mode kya hai? TRADE-OFF Simple option aur scalable option me kya difference hai?

concepts.title: Interview Answer Structures & Trade-offs
concepts.body: Structured answer = fixed skeleton + ek measurable result. Technical me problem → approach → trade-off → result, behavioural me STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result), aur dono me 60-90 second ka time budget.
concepts.code:
options = [
    {"name": "greedy", "cost": "low", "quality": 0.62, "latency_ms": 120},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 400},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank+cache", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 180},
]

def pick(options, quality_bar, latency_budget):
    ok = [o for o in options
          if o["quality"] >= quality_bar and o["latency_ms"] <= latency_budget]
    return min(ok, key=lambda o: (o["latency_ms"], o["cost"]))["name"] if ok else None

print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.8, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.9, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.6, latency_budget=200))
concepts.tip: Agar interviewer 'ek number do' bole to turant ek do aur uska source batao — number ke bina confidence claim ka koi weight nahi hota.

guide.what: Structured answer = fixed skeleton + ek measurable result. Technical me problem → approach → trade-off → result, behavioural me STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result), aur dono me 60-90 second ka time budget.
guide.why: Interviewer ke paas 45 minute hote hain aur wo signal dhoondhte hain: kya tum trade-offs sochte ho, kya numbers ke saath baat karte ho, aur kya honest ho. Structure ke bina achha kaam bhi adhoora lagta hai.
guide.whereUsed: Technical rounds, behavioural rounds, project deep-dives, aur salary/negotiation conversations.
prereqs: Ek real project (ya course project) jiska data tumhare paas ho
guide.howItWorks: Skeleton ka kaam hai attention ko content par laana. Har jawab me teen layer rakho: context (problem + constraint), decision (option + kyun), proof (number/outcome). Aur last me ek 'kya alag karta' line — ye senior signal hai kyunki isse pata chalta hai ki tumne result ke baad socha.

Result me number hona chahiye (0.62 → 0.86) — 'bahut improve hua' koi evidence nahi hai.
Action me lever ka naam hai (table-aware chunking, hybrid retrieval) — interviewer isi par follow-up karega.

examples.code:
lat = [120, 130, 125, 140, 360, 400]
lat.sort()

def pct(xs, p):
    if not xs:
        return None
    k = (len(xs) - 1) * p
    lo, hi = int(k), min(int(k) + 1, len(xs) - 1)
    return xs[lo] + (xs[hi] - xs[lo]) * (k - lo)

import statistics
print("p50", pct(lat, 0.5), "p95", pct(lat, 0.95), "max", max(lat))
print("mean", round(statistics.mean(lat), 1))
print("tail ratio", round(pct(lat, 0.95) / pct(lat, 0.5), 2))

p50 135.0 p95 390.0 max 400
mean 212.5
tail ratio 2.89
explain: Percentile interpolation se p50/p95 nikalte hain — average ke bajaye tail experience describe karna strong hota hai.
Mean (212.5) aur p95 (390.0) ka bada farq batata hai ki kuch requests outliers hain (cold start/dependency).
Tail ratio (p95/p50) ek line me 'kitna bura worst case hai' bata deta hai — interviewer ise instantly samajhta hai.

    {"name": "greedy", "cost": "low", "quality": 0.62, "latency_ms": 120},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 400},
    {"name": "hybrid+rerank+cache", "cost": "mid", "quality": 0.86, "latency_ms": 180},
]

def pick(options, quality_bar, latency_budget):
    ok = [o for o in options
          if o["quality"] >= quality_bar and o["latency_ms"] <= latency_budget]
    return min(ok, key=lambda o: (o["latency_ms"], o["cost"]))["name"] if ok else None

print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.8, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.9, latency_budget=500))
print(pick(options, quality_bar=0.6, latency_budget=200))
explain: Trade-off ko explicit constraint (quality bar + latency budget) me likha gaya — isi tarah interview me bolo: 'budget ye tha, isliye ye chuna'.
Jab koi option bar meet nahi karta to None lauta rahe hain — yahi honest jawab hai: 'is budget me koi option nahi tha, isliye main constraint change karne ko bolta'.
Sorting key (latency, phir cost) decision ko deterministic banati hai — 'kyun ye option' ka jawab reproducible ho jata hai.

concepts.body: Coding round me pattern recall kaam aata hai: problem ke signals se data structure aur technique chunna (hash-map, two-pointer, sliding window, binary search, heap, DP, graph traversal).
concepts.code:
PATTERNS = [
    {"name": "hash-map", "when": "lookup complement grouping",
     "cost": "O(n) time, O(n) space"},
    {"name": "two-pointer", "when": "sorted monotonic window",
     "cost": "O(n) time, O(1) space"},
    {"name": "binary-search", "when": "sorted predicate on value", "cost": "O(log n)"},
    {"name": "heap", "when": "top-K streaming max-min", "cost": "O(n log k)"},
    {"name": "DP", "when": "overlapping subproblems optimal substructure",
     "cost": "states x transitions"},
]

def suggest(signals):
    return [p["name"] for p in PATTERNS if any(s in p["when"] for s in signals)]

print(suggest(["sorted", "monotonic"]))
print(suggest(["top-K", "streaming"]))
print(suggest(["overlapping"]))
print(suggest(["lookup"]))

guide.what: Coding round me pattern recall kaam aata hai: problem ke signals se data structure aur technique chunna (hash-map, two-pointer, sliding window, binary search, heap, DP, graph traversal).
guide.why: Har problem naye sire se solve karne me time khatam ho jata hai. Signals → pattern map hone se approach 30 second me nikal jati hai aur baaki time complexity aur edge cases par lagta hai.
guide.whereUsed: DSA rounds, online assessments, aur production me bhi (streaming metrics, dedupe, batching, top-K).
guide.howItWorks: Constraints hi hint dete hain: n = 1e5 → O(n log n) ya O(n) chahiye, n = 20 → exponential/bitmask, memory tight → streaming. Uske baad do sawal: kya lookup/grouping hai (hash), kya monotonic/sorted hai (two-pointer/binary search), kya repeated subproblem hai (DP).
guide.syntax:
# decision map (signals -> pattern)
lookup/complement/grouping      -> hash map / set      O(n) time
sorted + pair/window           -> two-pointer          O(n) time, O(1) space
contiguous subarray + condition -> sliding window      O(n) time
sorted + value predicate       -> binary search        O(log n)
top-K / streaming max-min      -> heap                 O(n log k)
overlapping subproblems        -> DP                   states x transitions
reachability/levels/ordering   -> BFS/DFS (queue/stack) O(V+E)

explain: Hash map se O(n^2) brute force O(n) ban jata hai: complement dhoondhna ek O(1) lookup hai.
Pehle check karte hain ki complement mila kya, phir current value store karte hain — isse same element do baar use nahi hota.
Khaali input aur no-solution case defined output dete hain (None) — edge cases bolkar test karna strong signal hai.

examples.code:
def longest_unique(s):
    seen, start, best = {}, 0, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in seen and seen[ch] >= start:
            start = seen[ch] + 1
        seen[ch] = i
        best = max(best, i - start + 1)
    return best

print(longest_unique("abcabcbb"))
print(longest_unique(""))
print(longest_unique("bbbbb"))
print(longest_unique("abba"))
explain: Sliding window: window ka start sirf aage badhta hai, isliye total work O(n) rehta hai (har character ek baar add, ek baar remove).
seen[ch] >= start check zaroori hai — warna purana index window ke bahar wale character par start peeche chala jata.
Edge cases (khaali string, repeated characters, 'abba' jaisa trap) explicitly print kiye gaye.

guide.realWorld: Ye patterns production me bhi aate hain: dedupe/grouping (hash), rate limiting (sliding window), top-K frequent queries (heap), retry scheduling (binary search on time), aur dependency ordering (graph traversal). Coding round ki tayari asal me system design ki tayari bhi hai.

interview.q: O(n^2) ko optimize karne ka pehla step?
interview.a: Bottleneck identify karo: dobara kya compute ho raha hai? Lookup hai to hash/set, sorted property hai to two-pointer/binary search, repeated subproblem hai to DP.

interview.q: Two-pointer kab valid hai?
interview.a: Jab monotonic property ho — sorted array, ya window me add/remove se condition predictably badle. Bina monotonicity ke pointer movement ka logic galat ho jata hai.

interview.q: Hash map ka worst case kab O(n) ho jata hai?
interview.a: Collisions zyada hone par (bura hash ya adversarial keys) lookup O(n) ho jata hai — isliye average aur worst case dono bolna sahi hai.

interview.a: Fast lookup or frequency counting when keys can be hashed.

interview.q: Sliding window kab?

interview.q: Two pointers kab?
interview.a: Sorted sequence or left/right scan where pointer movement can eliminate work.

interview.a: Constraint size padho; simple brute force helps validate logic, then optimize if needed.

interview.a: Clarify input/output -> examples -> approach -> code -> complexity -> tests.

guide.what: Project defense = 60-second pitch + evidence card + honest boundaries. Interviewer tumhare system ke numbers, failures aur decisions sunna chahta hai — tool list nahi.
guide.why: Portfolio me project likhna aasan hai; uski depth prove karna mushkil. Jo candidates numbers, trade-offs aur 'kya alag karta' bata paate hain, unka project 'tutorial' nahi lagta.
guide.whereUsed: Portfolio projects, final-year projects, capstone, aur internal projects (promotion/promo conversations me bhi).
guide.howItWorks: Defense teen cheezon par khada hai: (1) architecture ek line me (client → API → data flow), (2) evidence — measured numbers aur unka source, (3) failure stories — kya toota, kaise detect hua, kaise fix hua. Sabse strong signal: '3 numbers jo mera kaam prove karte hain' aur ek honest 'dobara banata to kya alag karta'.

howToCode.detail: Client → API → services → data stores; arrows par protocol/async. Framework names baad me, data flow pehle.

Ek incident: symptom → measurement → fix → verification. Yahi story 'kya tum production sochte ho' ka jawab hai.
Kya solve nahi karta (freshness lag, high-stakes decisions) — scope honest bolna maturity dikhata hai.

commonMistakes: Frameworks ki list dena bina data flow ya trade-off batane ke.
Numbers yaad na hona (kitne rows, kaun sa chunk size, kaun sa index).
Demo reproduce na ho paana (data/branch/environment alag).
Sirf happy path batana — failure aur degraded mode ka koi zikr nahi.
Team project me apna contribution unclear chhodna.
bestPractices: Seeded sample data + README steps rakho taaki demo reproducible ho.
Har number ka source likho (kis dataset par, kab measure kiya).
Decision log (ADR) maintain karo — 'kya alag karta' ka material wahi se aata hai.
Degraded modes likho (dependency down par kya hota hai) aur ek test se prove karo.
Claim ko bound karo: 'is data par ye metric' — global claim se bacho.
guide.realWorld: Portfolio project ka interview round, capstone viva, aur internal design review — teeno me yahi playbook chalti hai. Interview me 'teen numbers do jo mera kaam prove karte hain' ka ready jawab alag level par rakhta hai.

interview.q: System kitna scale karega — kaise answer karoge?
interview.a: Current measured state + bottleneck + plan: '20 rps par p95 400ms, bottleneck DB connections aur vector index; plan read replicas + caching + sharding'.

interview.q: Accuracy par confidence kya hai?
interview.a: Eval set size, per-bucket breakdown aur limitation batao: chhote buckets par 'insufficient data' — overclaiming se better hai honest confidence interval.

interview.q: Dependency failure par system kya karta hai?
interview.a: Degraded modes named hon: retrieval down → retry with message, model down → fallback provider, DB slow → cached response. Aur har mode test se proven.

coding.text: Coding task: project metrics summary banao — latency list [120, 90, 200, 80, 400] se p50, p95 aur max nikalo, aur single-value series par bhi test karo.
coding.solution:
latencies = [120, 90, 200, 80, 400]
def pct(xs, p):
    ordered = sorted(xs)
    k = (len(ordered) - 1) * p / 100
    lo, hi = int(k), min(int(k) + 1, len(ordered) - 1)
    return round(ordered[lo] + (ordered[hi] - ordered[lo]) * (k - lo), 1)
print('p50:', pct(latencies, 50), 'p95:', pct(latencies, 95), 'max:', max(latencies))
print('p50 [80]:', pct([80], 50), 'p95 empty guard:', pct([1, 2], 0))
# p50: 120.0 p95: 360.0 max: 400
# p50 [80]: 80.0 p95 empty guard: 1.0

logic.text: Interview me tumne kaha "p50 latency 120ms, p95 360ms" — interviewer isse kya samajh raha hai?
logic.answer: Ki 1 in 20 request 360ms tak jaati hai, isliye average ke bajaye tail experience describe ho raha hai. Numbers ke saath source bhi batao (kitne requests, kis load par) — warna interviewer impressionistic samjhega.

logic.text: Apne capstone project ka 60-second answer ka structure likho.
logic.answer: (1) Problem + scale (users/rows/latency), (2) meri role aur constraints, (3) approach + ek explicit tradeoff, (4) result ek number me, (5) ek bug/lesson aur next improvement. Har step 10-15 sec — interviewer interruption ke liye jagah bachao.

logic.text: Capstone project ke follow-up question par atak gaye — sabse likely reason?
logic.answer: Numbers aur decisions yaad nahi (kitne rows, kyun wo chunk size, kya index lagaya). Fix: ek 'metrics card' yaad rakho — scale, latency, accuracy, cost — aur har number ka source bata sako (kahan measure kiya, kaunsa tool).

logic.text: Kaun sa edge case demo/interview me project claim ko todta hai?
logic.answer: Reproduce na ho paana (data/branch/environment alag) aur claim ka number already stale hona. Fix: seeded sample data, README me exact run steps, aur wahi branch/commit demo karo jiska number bata rahe ho — ya claim ko 'jis data par measure kiya wo ye tha' likh kar bound karo.

logic.text: Project architecture samjhate waqt pehle kya rakho — framework list ya data flow?
logic.answer: Data flow ki ek line: input → validation → transform → model/SQL → output/storage; uske baad us line ke around decisions (schema, batching, error handling, retry). Framework names sabse aakhir me — interviewer decisions aur constraints sunna chahta hai, tool list nahi.

logic.text: Interviewer "isko kaise improve karoge" pooche — pehle kya bologe?
logic.answer: Ek measured bottleneck bolo (p95 latency / cost per 1k calls / accuracy gap) aur uska specific fix (caching, batch size, index, quantization) — impact aur effort dono estimate karke. "Sab kuch better karunga" ya tool-stack badalna weak lagta hai kyunki problem statement hi nahi hota.
